A6.6.detail: Adding interface_methods to graph::SymbolTable hard-breaks the compile at store/src/lib.rs:246 (exhaustive struct literal in SymbolTableStore::to_owned_table), and the natural fix puts the field in the rkyv-archived on-disk struct read through validated rkyv::access (store/src/lib.rs:449) — every pre-existing .gmap would fail load_from_gmap, with no MANIFEST_VERSION bump anywhere in the plan. Keep interface_methods BUILD-TIME ONLY (the pattern A6.2a uses correctly: CodeNavStore::to_owned starts from CodeNav::default() and mutates). If it must persist, it is PARKED to the joint repo-graph+glia version.

A3.1.detail: A3.1 inserts the ANY-wildcard tier ahead of the existing endpoint-side prefix strip and returns on first hit, so `GET /api/users` that today strips to `/users` and binds `GET /users` would instead bind the ANY route — an existing HTTP_CALLS edge silently retargeted. A3.4/A4.1/A4.4/A4.5 manufacture exactly those ANY routes. Ladder must be exact -> endpoint-strip -> ANY.

A13.1.detail: canonical_entity_name is genuinely additive (buckets only merge). MAX_ENTITY_FANOUT=12 is pure edge removal: DbResolver has no cap today (graph/src/lib.rs:1640), so a qname in 13+ merged repos goes from 78+ SHARES_DATA_ENTITY edges to zero. Ship the canonical join key; the cap becomes its own declared content_change, capping emitted pairs deterministically rather than dropping the bucket.

A11.3.detail: A11.3 and A13.7 are the same change authored twice in two areas, both attaching cell_type::ENV(12) to CONFIG_KEY with INCOMPATIBLE payload schemas. A11.3 has NO redaction, so `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_...` is written verbatim into the persisted <repo>/.ai/repo-graph .gmap and into the dense_text handed to an LLM. A13.7's shape wins (denylist + userinfo masking + source discriminator). Redaction is non-optional. Reclassify as content_change/cell_value — projection-text/src/lib.rs:443 renders every cell unconditionally, so dense_text output and .gmap bytes change.

A3.6.detail: A3.6 calls its rewrite of the locate_node POSITION loop 'a pure refactor', but A2.8 rewrites the SAME loop with opposite semantics (engine/src/lib.rs:1986-1998 has no break, so LAST POSITION wins today; A2.8 makes FIRST win). Landing A3.6 second silently reverts A2.8 for every multi-POSITION node. A3.6 depends_on A2.8 and position_of must implement first-wins.

A16.8.detail: Asserts fixtures==71 && blind_spots==[], which A14.1 makes impossible by design (it takes blind spots 0->12 to record the Kotlin baseline honestly). completeness_gaps.item: §1 table, row 5: "70 | ParseCache pub iter/diff, BTreeMap, per-pid tmp | engine/src/cache.rs:73,175" — the **pub iter/diff** half.
completeness_gaps.why_it_matters: A1.3 delivers the BTreeMap and the per-pid tmp file, but its breaking note explicitly locks the surface: "`entries` is a private field of a struct whose public API (`new`/`get`/`put`/`retain_paths`/`len`/`is_empty`/`load`/`save`/`purge`/`validate_context`) is unchanged." Verified on main: `entries: HashMap<String, CacheEntry>` at engine/src/cache.rs:74 is private and there is no iterator or diff accessor. Without iter/diff nothing outside the cache can answer "which files changed since the last build" — that is the per-file delta the incremental story (and Engram/neuropil's #1 upstream need) is built on, and it is the reason the row exists.
completeness_gaps.suggested_packet: A1.8 — ParseCache::iter() + ParseCache::diff(&self, &[(path, hash)]) -> {reused, reparsed, evicted} as public API, with the marker counts computed from diff() instead of ad-hoc counters in engine/src/lib.rs:340-399.

completeness_gaps.item: §2 #2, bullet 2: "…so a submodule or linked worktree is walked INTO the parent RepoId: duplicate symbols, pick_primary flapping, **Go imports misclassified (root go.mod only, engine:164-175)**."
completeness_gaps.why_it_matters: A8.1 collapses the nested `.git` directory to a REGION, which kills the duplicate symbols and the pick_primary flapping. It does nothing about the third consequence: `go_prefix` is read from the ROOT go.mod only, so every nested Go module in a monorepo (and every `services/*/go.mod`) has its imports classified against the wrong module path — internal imports look like library imports and vice versa. A8.4 detects `go.mod` roots but states "No graph change at all in this packet"; A8.5 emits edge-less PROJECT nodes. Nothing threads the per-module go.mod into Go import resolution, and ParseCache keys on a single `go_prefix` string (engine/src/cache.rs:71-73), so the wrong value is also cached.
completeness_gaps.suggested_packet: A8.7 — per-project-root go_prefix: use A8.4's roots to pick the nearest enclosing go.mod per file instead of the root one, and key the ParseCache on the set rather than one string.

duplications_to_resolve: **grade.py forbidden-edge assertion — FIVE packets, four key names.** A2.0 (`forbid_edges`), A3.0 (`expect_absent_edges` + `expect_absent_nodes`), A5.0 (`expect_absent_edges`), A11.6 (`expect_absent_edges` + `expect_category_counts`), A15.1 (`forbid`). Each claims "purely additive, all existing fixtures parse and score identically" and each is a dependency of its own area (A2.1-A2.9 → A2.0; A3.4/A3.5 → A3.0; A5.4/A5.5/A5.6 → A5.0; A11.4 → A11.6; A15.3-A15.12 → A15.1). Only one key name can exist. Resolve to ONE harness packet before any area starts, and re-point the four dependency edges.

**grade.py cell/position assertions — three packets.** A2.0 adds `"located": true` (POSITION present), A12.0 adds `expect_cells` (cell payload contains), A15.1 adds `expect_literals` (searches cell payloads for the identifying literal). All three read `node_cells`/`nodes_json` for the same purpose. A15.1 even carries the warning that touching `_node_matches` to search cells would flip existing node_recall — which is precisely what A12.0's and A2.0's paths risk doing independently.

**`${base}` / base-URL folding — A3.1 vs A11.2.** A3.1 ships a `BaseFold` tier inside `lookup_route_with_prefix_strip` with fixture `http-base-prefix` asserting ``` `${environment.apiUrl}/users` → chi `route:/users` (BaseFold) ```; A11.2 ships an engine pre-pass `endpoint_fold.rs` consuming A11.1's ConstTable with fixture `angular-base-url` asserting the same Angular-environment→Go-route pairing. Same review bullet ("`${base}` prefix unpairable (60 LOC)"), two layers, two fixtures, two baselines. A11.2's approach rewrites the ENDPOINT qname (breaking); A3.1's is resolver-local (non-breaking). Pick one — if A11.2 lands, A3.1's BaseFold tier is dead code.

**TS/Dart client host+query strip — A3.3 vs A11.2 vs A11.5.** A3.3 "Client request-path normalisation for TypeScript and Dart (host + query strip)" changes ENDPOINT qnames in typescript/ and dart/. A11.2 independently does the TypeScript half ("split authority off the path, record host on the cell", same file parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs). A11.5 independently does the Dart half ("Carry the request authority through the shared ClientEndpoint seam (go, python, java, swift, dart)"). Three packets, two of them breaking on qname shape, editing the same two parsers for the same review bullet ("TS/Dart skip `url_to_path` (host/query kept)").

**`store::is_gmap_stale` gating — A1.5 vs A8.1 vs A8.2.** A1.5 "is_gmap_stale reuses the walker's gating (audit #17), including gated-directory mtimes"; A8.1 "one shared gate for the engine walker **and store::is_gmap_stale**"; A8.2 adds the `ignore`-crate matcher to store/src/lib.rs:937-985 as well. All three rewrite the same scan with overlapping test names (A1.5's `stale_scan_skips_gated_dirs` vs A8.1's two new store tests vs A8.2's). acceptance_gate_defects.detail: SIX packets in six different areas each independently rewrite bench/substrate-gap/grade.py with an overlapping, mutually incompatible key.json schema extension, and each one's acceptance gate is written against its own naming. 'An edge that must not exist' is spelled three ways: `forbid_edges` (A2.0, rolled into per_cat as forbidden/forbidden_found, printed as 'FALSE PAIRINGS'), `expect_absent_edges` (A3.0 -> a separate `absent_violations` list printed as 'FALSE POSITIVES'; A5.0 -> a `"!"+CATEGORY` synthetic column in per_cat printed as 'absent'; A11.6 -> 'EXPECT-ABSENT VIOLATIONS'), and `forbid` (A15.1, which also carries node and max_cells_of_type forms). Cell grading is spelled two ways: `expect_cells` (A12.0) and `expect_literals` (A15.1). A3.0 and A5.0 use the IDENTICAL key name with DIFFERENT aggregation, so they silently overwrite each other. Whichever lands first wins; every downstream packet that declared depends_on the loser (A2.3, A2.7, A2.9, A3.4, A3.5, A5.4, A5.5, A5.6, A11.4, A12.1, A12.4, A15.6-A15.12) then has an acceptance gate that cannot be evaluated at all, because grade.py raises on unknown keys only for kinds/categories and SILENTLY IGNORES an unrecognised top-level key -- so the fixture would read a green 1.00 with its precision assertion never executed. That is the exact silent-dead-code failure the house rule exists to prevent.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Collapse all six into ONE harness packet that lands before any consumer, with a single frozen vocabulary: `forbid: [{kind,name?} | {from,to,category} | {kind,name,max_cells_of_type}]`, `expect_cells: [{kind,node,cell,contains?,where?}]`, and `cells: ["<lang>/<mech>"]` (A15.1's shape, which is the superset). Make grade_fixture RAISE `ValueError(f"{fixture}: unknown key.json field {k!r}")` on any top-level key outside the frozen set, so a packet written against the wrong spelling fails loudly instead of scoring green. Then rewrite the acceptance line of every dependent packet to name that one vocabulary.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: The xcut-graphql-precision key.json contains `{"kind":"GRAPHQL_RESOLVER","name":"graphql_resolver:getUsers","note":"field-level resolver, the only real one"}`. MEASURED on main with exactly the packet's source: the graph emits GRAPHQL_RESOLVER 'Query' and GRAPHQL_RESOLVER 'Resolver' (the decorator nouns) and NO 'getUsers' node at all. A5.5's change is confined to `names_match_graphql` in graph/src/lib.rs -- it does not touch graphql.rs's RESOLVER_FIELD_DECORATORS -- so that expect_nodes row reads XX before the fix and XX after it, permanently. The fixture would therefore land a permanent entry in run.py's MISSING NODES block, breaking the committed `BLIND SPOTS: 0 / MISSING NODES: none` invariant that A15.1/A15.6/A15.7 all use as their regression diff. I also confirmed the positive half is real: the forbidden edge `graphql_op:useQuery -> graphql_resolver:Query` GRAPHQL_CALLS DOES exist today.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Drop the `graphql_resolver:getUsers` row from A5.5's expect_nodes (or move it into a separate, explicitly-deferred fixture owned by whoever fixes field-level resolver extraction). Keep only `{"kind":"GRAPHQL_OPERATION","name":"graphql_op:useQuery"}` plus the forbid entry, so the cell is `forbid 1 violation -> 0 violations` with no MISSING NODES residue.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: A16.8's depends_on names 'A15 packet that adds the results-latest.json writer to bench/substrate-gap/run.py' and its acceptance asserts `d['fixtures']==71 and d['blind_spots']==[] and d['engine']=='0.4.18'`. acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Split the filenames and make the dependency explicit. A16.8 owns `bench/substrate-gap/legacy-latest.json` written by run.py on every invocation INCLUDING `--no-log`, schema `{engine, fixtures:int, blind_spots:[], missing_nodes:[], cells:[{framework,language,per_category}]}` with `json.dump(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True)` and no timestamp; A15.4 keeps `results-latest.json` for the 16x30 matrix. Change A16.8's depends_on to name its OWN run.py edit (it is ~15 LOC, no A15 dependency needed) and add the falsification it already describes: hand-edit one recall and confirm check-latest.sh exits 1.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: All three acceptance gates are stated against a fixture count of 49: A2.0 'prints the same 49-fixture matrix', A5.0 'still prints exactly 49 fixtures with 0 blind spots', A12.0 'all 49 existing fixtures behave identically'. MEASURED: `ls bench/substrate-gap/fixtures | wc -l` = 71, and `python3 run.py --no-log` prints 71 rows with `BLIND SPOTS (recall 0.00): 0`. A10.1 likewise says 'the other 49 fixtures unchanged'. A3.0, A15.1, A15.6 correctly say 71. A gate written against a wrong count is unverifiable as written and invites an implementer to 'reconcile' by deleting rows.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Restate every such gate as: `diff <(python3 run.py --no-log) /tmp/before.txt` is EMPTY, having captured /tmp/before.txt on the unmodified tree -- a byte-diff, not a count. Where a count is genuinely wanted, use the measured 71 and note that BLIND SPOTS is 0 and MISSING NODES is absent entirely on main (I verified both, plus that the single sub-1.0 cell in the whole corpus is php-laravel-calls CALLS at 0.50, which run.py hides because line 63 tests `recall == 0.0`).

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: Four ORM packets propose a fixture whose declaration and use live in DIFFERENT files, while the implementation each packet specifies is an explicitly PER-FILE pre-pass. go-gorm puts `func (User) TableName() string { return "app_users" }` in model.go and `db.Model(&User{})` in store.go; ruby-ar-tablename puts `self.table_name` in app/models/legacy_user.rb and the query in app/controllers/users_controller.rb; php-eloquent splits Models/User.php from Http/UserController.php; py-django-orm splits shop/models.py from shop/views.py. A13.12, A13.13 and A13.17 each name this in their own risks field ('decide before authoring the 0.00 baseline') but the acceptance still asserts the cell flips to 1.00. As written, these four gates would FAIL after a correct implementation -- which is worse than a gate that proves nothing, because it will be 'fixed' by loosening the fixture until it passes.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: For each of the four, either (a) collapse the fixture into ONE file so the per-file pre-pass is exercised and the 1.00 claim is honest, or (b) keep two files and change the acceptance to assert the FALLBACK key (A13.1's canonical fold of the type name) rather than the override, and move the override assertion into a second single-file fixture. State the choice in key.json's note so the next reader cannot mistake the fallback for full coverage. Do not defer the decision to the implementer.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: Acceptance includes 'Existing fixture angular-http-calls: node count drops 11 -> 10, edge count 11 -> 10, exactly one route:/users ROUTE node remains'. These are RAW COUNTS that go DOWN, they are not asserted by grade.py (node_count/edge_count are printed, never compared), and the two ROUTE nodes are indistinguishable by name OR qname -- I measured both as `[ROUTE] '/users' qname='route:/users'`, so grade.py's substring matcher literally cannot tell them apart. The 'exactly one remains' clause is therefore a human eyeballing `--dump`. (The underlying defect is real and I confirmed it: angular-http-calls emits two identical route:/users nodes and two identical HTTP_CALLS edges today.)
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Delete the count clauses. Gate the precision on the new http-client-not-route fixture's frozen `forbid` entries only -- `{"kind":"ROUTE","name":"route:/users"}` and `{"category":"HTTP_CALLS"}` -- reading 2 violations before and 0 after. For angular-http-calls, add a `forbid` entry with the max-count form once the frozen vocabulary supports it: `{"kind":"ROUTE","name":"route:/users","max_nodes":1}`, which reads 1 violation today and 0 after. That makes the count machine-checkable instead of narrative.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: Three packets gate their headline deliverable on reading a `--dump` line by eye. A5.1: 'the GRPC_SERVICE line changes from path=None to path=user.proto'. A5.8: 'GRPC_CLIENT UserService changing from path=None to path=main.go AND a new [USES] edge'. A14.5: 'the ROUTE node id must be unchanged, verifiable by diffing nodes_json() ids before and after' plus 'the ROUTE node's POSITION cell is Some'. grade.py has no notion of a node's `path` or of its cells, and `--dump` output is not compared against anything. I confirmed the baselines are real (xcut-grpc-grpc_calls shows GRPC_SERVICE path=None and only 4 nodes with no MODULE for the .proto), but 'a human looked at a dump' is not a gate.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Once the frozen cell vocabulary lands, express all three as `expect_cells` rows: A5.1 `{"kind":"GRPC_SERVICE","node":"grpc:helloworld.Greeter","cell":"POSITION","contains":"helloworld.proto"}`; A5.8 the same for GRPC_CLIENT against main.go; A14.5 `{"kind":"ROUTE","node":"GET /api/items","cell":"POSITION","contains":"app.kt"}`. For A14.5's id-stability claim, add a Rust unit test asserting `NodeId::from_parts(GRAPH_TYPE, repo, node_kind::ROUTE, "GET /api/items")` equals the emitted id, rather than a before/after diff a human performs.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: Six packets share exactly two marker strings with no per-language discriminator: A6.2a/b/c all emit `[recv] receiver-typed calls bound: N (fields=F)` and A6.3/A6.4/A6.5 all emit `[heritage] refs bound=N unresolved=M`. A6.4 and A6.5 declare no marker of their own at all -- their stated proof is 'A6.3's [heritage] line fires on this Solidity-only/Dart-only fixture'. That makes it impossible to grep-prove that the Dart reroute ran as opposed to the Solidity one, and if the shared line is emitted at all the packet reads as fired even when its own code path is dead. This is exactly the failure mode A7.0 was designed to avoid, and A7.0's `[di] injects refs: java-lombok=1 csharp-primary-ctor=1` per-shape token scheme is the right answer sitting one area away.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Adopt A7.0's pattern. Add a shared `repo_graph_code_domain::resolve_stats` counter module (or extend A7.0's di_stats) with per-source tokens, and change the markers to `[recv] receiver-typed calls bound: csharp=1 typescript=0 java=0` and `[heritage] refs bound: ts=2 solidity=0 dart=0 unresolved=0`. Then each packet's fired_on_marker becomes a token that is zero before it lands: A6.4 greps `solidity=1`, A6.5 greps `dart=2`, A6.2c greps `java=1`. Verified this is cheap to prove at baseline: engine/src/lib.rs has exactly ONE `eprintln!("[` today (the [incremental] warning at :64), so every new bracketed marker returns nothing on main.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: fired_on_marker is the bare string `family_mismatch=`, which is a token in the MIDDLE of A2.3's line `[queues] resolver paired=N skipped_unresolved=N family_mismatch=N wildcard=N skipped_catchall=N`. It has no stable prefix, so `grep '^\[queues\]'` will not find it and a bare `grep family_mismatch=` matches source code as readily as stderr. The brief's rule is that a marker is a literal stderr string with a stable prefix.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Change the fired_on_marker to the full line with the prefix: `[queues] resolver paired=1 skipped_unresolved=0 family_mismatch=1 wildcard=1 skipped_catchall=0`, and make the acceptance `glia analyze <fixture> 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -c '^\[queues\] resolver '` == 1 with `family_mismatch=1` in the same line. Apply the same prefix rule to A9.1, which declares no marker at all.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: fired_on_marker is 'none of its own -- A9.1 is a pure library function with no side effects', and the stated proof is `cargo test -p repo-graph-graph cross_link -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep 'test result: ok. 4 passed'`. A passing test count is not a fired-on marker: it proves the tests compile and pass, not that `cross_links` is reached by any real build. Since A9.2 consumes it and A9.2's `[arch]` line reports `links` = cross_links().0.len() after a filter, a dead cross_links would still print a plausible `[arch] 2 services, 0 links`.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Give A9.1 a real token inside A9.2's line: change the marker to `[arch] {S} services, {L} links (keying=... self=... unlocated=... buckets={B} unplaced={U})` where `buckets` is `cross_links` map length and `unplaced` is its second return value, and make A9.1's gate `glia arch bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/xstack-ts-go-http 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -o 'buckets=[0-9]*'` printing `buckets=2`. Alternatively, if A9.1 must ship alone, gate it on `cargo test -p repo-graph-graph cross_links_normalises_symmetric_and_counts_unplaced` by NAME, not by a passing-count grep.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: Both packets capture env-var VALUES onto a `cell_type::ENV` cell (id 12, already in the ALL table -- verified) and both gate only on Rust unit tests, each stating 'grade.py cannot assert cell contents'. That was true when they were written, but A12.0 and A15.1 both add exactly that capability, and A11.3 is a declared PREREQUISITE of A11.4's hostname join while A13.7 is a declared prerequisite of area A11. A unit test proves the extractor returns the right struct; it does not prove the value survives merge_parses, the store round-trip and `node_cells`, which is the contract A11.4 actually consumes. The two packets also duplicate each other (both capture compose/k8s/dotenv env values into an ENV cell) without cross-referencing.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Merge A11.3 and A13.7 into one packet, declare depends_on the frozen harness, and add a fixture gate: `config-env-values` with one .env or docker-compose.yml defining `API_URL=http://users-svc:8080` and a Python reader, keyed `{"kind":"CONFIG_KEY","node":"API_URL","cell":"ENV","contains":"users-svc:8080"}`. That reads 0 today (build_nodes emits `cells: vec![]`) and 1 after. Add a second row asserting a SECRET-named key has NO value in its payload, so the redaction rule is graded and not merely described.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: A8.1's whole point is PRECISION -- collapsing obj/bin and nested .git so phantom nodes stop existing -- but its only fixture gate is the recall half (REGION region:obj / region:bin flipping 0.00 -> 1.00). The packet states 'grade.py has no expect_absent_nodes, so the precision half is only provable by the engine unit tests'. That is no longer true once A3.0/A15.1 land, and A8.1 declares no dependency on either. I MEASURED the phantoms it is meant to kill: a minimal .NET tree emits MODULE obj::Debug::net8.0::Api.AssemblyInfo, MODULE bin::Debug::Api.g, CLASS PhantomAssemblyInfo, CLASS PhantomBinClass, METHOD GeneratedNoise and PACKAGE Shop::Api::Generated -- 6 junk nodes of 11 -- with zero REGION anchors, and the CALLS Configure->Boot control passing.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Add depends_on the frozen harness and put the phantoms in the key as forbid rows: `{"kind":"CLASS","name":"PhantomAssemblyInfo"}`, `{"kind":"CLASS","name":"PhantomBinClass"}`, `{"kind":"METHOD","name":"GeneratedNoise"}`, `{"kind":"PACKAGE","name":"Shop/Api/Generated"}` -- 4 violations before, 0 after. Do the same for walk-nested-submodule with `{"kind":"CLASS","name":"VendorClient"}`, which is the node that currently duplicates across RepoIds and drives the pick_primary flapping the packet cites.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: The two packets make CONTRADICTORY measured claims about the same language and library. A15.8 pins `matrix/csharp/kafka` as the harness's canonical `none` anchor asserting `extract=0/2`, with test_matrix.py asserting it. A12.1's csharp-kafka-msgtype fixture asserts the OPPOSITE -- that a QUEUE_PRODUCER tag node IS emitted -- and explicitly says 'Drop the BootstrapServers line and it emits nothing at all; keep it'. I measured both: the C# source WITHOUT any lowercase `kafka` token yields ZERO QUEUE_* nodes, but adding the realistic `var config = new ProducerConfig { BootstrapServers = "kafka:9092" };` yields `[QUEUE_PRODUCER] 'kafka' qname='queue_producer:kafka'`. A15.8's `extract=0/2` anchor is therefore silently dependent on the fixture omitting a bootstrap string that a real C# producer always has, and A15.8's own AUTHORING guidance (A15.5) tells authors to write 'the smallest source a real repo would contain'.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Reconcile explicitly. Make A15.8's matrix/csharp/kafka source INCLUDE the BootstrapServers line (it is what a real repo contains) and change the anchor to `csharp/kafka = partial (extract=1/2 literal=0/2 route=0/1)` -- producer collapses to the framework tag, consumer emits nothing, no QUEUE_FLOWS -- with a key note citing both causes (case-sensitive gate at queues.rs:120 defeated by `using Confluent.Kafka;`, and no capitalised `.Subscribe(` needle). Move the pure `none` anchor to `csharp/azure_sb`, which I can confirm has no needle of any kind. Update test_matrix.py's third anchor accordingly and cross-reference A12.1 so the two fixtures state the same fact.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: A15.3 is the eval gate for the entire 16x30 harness, but three of its four anchor assertions (go/nats=full, python/kafka=partial, csharp/kafka=none) depend on fixtures that A15.6, A15.7 and A15.8 have not yet authored, and the packet resolves this by saying 'until then the test skips with an explicit SKIP line'. That leaves A15.3 landing with exactly ONE asserted anchor (clojure/kafka=unknown, i.e. 'no fixture exists'), which any implementation trivially satisfies. The tri-level derivation -- the actual deliverable, and the thing that distinguishes measured `none` from unmeasured `unknown` -- ships ungated.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Make A15.3 depend on A15.6 (legacy backfill is key.json-only, zero new source) and assert the go/nats=full anchor at landing -- I verified fixtures/xcut-queue-queue_flows yields QUEUE_PRODUCER orders + QUEUE_CONSUMER orders + a QUEUE_FLOWS edge, so `full via=queue` is measurable today. For the other two, build the python/kafka fixture inside A15.3 itself (I measured it: producer `queue_producer:orders`, consumer `queue_consumer:kafka`, QUEUE_FLOWS 0.00 -- exactly `partial`) so at least one of each of full/partial/none is asserted, not skipped.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: Three packets have no literal stderr marker with a stable prefix. A4.0: 'Compile-time packet, so the marker is a grep not a stderr line' -- `grep -rn 'endpoint::join_path\|...' | wc -l` >= 4, which counts source text and would pass on a half-applied edit that never runs. A16.6: 'No stderr marker' -- the gate is grade.py STDOUT `OK  CALLS          'index' -> 'greet'`, whose column alignment is produced by an f-string and is whitespace-fragile. A16.7: the marker is a `git log --grep` on the commit subject, which proves a commit message was written, not that anything changed.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: A4.0: the join helpers are consumed by A4.1-A4.8, so give it no marker of its own and instead make its gate the two existing cells it must not move (`elixir-phoenix-handled_by` and `go-handled-by` both staying 1.00, which I confirmed are 1.00 today) plus `cargo test -p repo-graph-code-domain abs_path_forces_single_leading_slash` by name. A16.6: replace the whitespace-sensitive stdout line with the machine form `python3 -c "import grade;r=grade.grade_fixture('fixtures/php-laravel-calls');assert r['per_category']['CALLS']['recall']==1.0"` -- I verified it returns 0.5 on main, so this is a genuine before/after. A16.7: replace the git-log grep with the seven concrete `git grep -n ... -> no hits` assertions the packet already lists, plus `git status --porcelain` empty.

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: A1.7's gate is `python3 bench/substrate-gap/incremental_check.py` printing '49 fixtures, 0 divergent' and exiting 0 against the CURRENT tree -- a guard that passes before and after, which the packet states plainly ('this closes no blind spot and flips no cell'). That honesty is correct and the packet should ship, but two things weaken it: the count 49 is wrong (measured 71), and the negative control it describes -- 'hand-edit the copied sidecar's stored content_hash for one entry and confirm the script reports that fixture as divergent' -- is narrative rather than a runnable step, so nothing proves the guard CAN fail.
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Fix the count to 71. Turn the negative control into a committed, runnable flag: add `--self-test` to incremental_check.py which copies one fixture, warms the sidecar, corrupts a single entry's content_hash in place, re-grades and asserts the script reports divergence and exits 1. Make the acceptance require BOTH `python3 incremental_check.py` exiting 0 AND `python3 incremental_check.py --self-test` exiting 0 (meaning: the injected divergence was detected).

acceptance_gate_defects.detail: A10.1's acceptance flips only node recall (DOC_SECTION 0/2 -> 2/2) and explicitly has no edges; A10.2 then adds the DOCUMENTS edges to the SAME fixture's key.json. That sequencing is fine, but A10.1's acceptance line 'python3 run.py shows the other 49 fixtures unchanged' carries the wrong count, and more importantly A10.2's gate depends on path-parameter folding that the packet itself flags as absent: it notes `<int:uid>` does not fold and warns 'keep such a path OUT of this packet's key.json'. The fixture as specified uses `/users` with a `servers: /api/v1` base, which I verified is safe -- but the constraint lives only in the risks field, not in the key.json note, so an author extending the fixture with a parameterised path would record a permanent 0.00 and read it as a substrate gap. (I confirmed the baseline: an openapi.yaml with servers+paths produces 3 nodes total and zero DOC_SECTIONs, with the Flask ROUTE control passing.)
acceptance_gate_defects.fix: Move the constraint into the committed artefact: add to contract-openapi-yaml/key.json a top-level note 'Paths here are deliberately parameter-free. `<int:id>` / `{id}` do not fold in normalise_segment (graph/src/lib.rs:1299) until Batch A rank 3 lands, so a parameterised op would record a permanent 0.00 for an unrelated reason.' Fix the 49 -> byte-diff gate as above.

additive_audit.what: A6.6 declares is_breaking=false / kind=none and lists a single in-repo consumer (a bench fixture). It adds `interface_methods: HashMap<NodeId, HashMap<String, NodeId>>` to `graph::SymbolTable` (/home/ivy/Code/glia/graph/src/lib.rs:56). That struct is persisted: `store::SymbolTableStore` (/home/ivy/Code/glia/store/src/lib.rs:121) is its on-disk mirror, and `SymbolTableStore::to_owned_table()` at store/src/lib.rs:246 rebuilds it with an EXHAUSTIVE struct literal `SymbolTable { module_by_qname, module_symbols, class_methods, module_import_bindings }`. Adding a field makes store/src/lib.rs fail to compile, which the packet does not mention at all. The obvious fix — adding the field to `SymbolTableStore` — is a .gmap layout change: that struct is `#[derive(rkyv::Archive, rkyv::Serialize, rkyv::Deserialize)]` and `Container::open` reads it through validated `rkyv::access::<ArchivedContainer, rkyv::rancor::Error>` (store/src/lib.rs:449), so every pre-existing .gmap fails validation and `repo_graph_py.load_from_gmap(dir)` raises PyValueError. Nothing in the plan bumps `MANIFEST_VERSION` (store/src/lib.rs:629, still 1), and A1.2 explicitly instructs implementers NOT to touch it.
additive_audit.mitigation: Either (a) keep interface_methods build-time only and say so, mirroring what A6.2a correctly does for CodeNav::field_types — note that `CodeNavStore::to_owned` starts from `CodeNav::default()` and mutates, which is exactly why A6.2a compiles and A6.6 does not; or (b) if it must persist, bump MANIFEST_VERSION and add the field to SymbolTableStore in the same commit, and confirm the wrapper calls is_gmap_stale(dir, repo) before load_from_gmap — note load_from_gmap(dir) takes no repo_path, so a wrapper that loads a cached dir directly gets an exception rather than a regenerate. Add store/src/lib.rs:218 and :246 to in_repo_consumers either way.

What actually leaks into eventbus.rs is Redis **pub/sub** and MQTT, for which no queue needle exists at all. Worse, eventbus.rs:15 `("publish(", true)` is UNGATED and matches `nc.publish(` / `channel.publish(` / `producer.publish(`, so every NATS and RabbitMQ producer DOUBLE-emits: the existing fixture bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/xcut-queue-queue_flows/server/publisher.go produces both QUEUE_PRODUCER:orders and a phantom Weak EVENT_EMITTER:orders.

A2 — queue / message-broker extraction correctness across all 16 languages (queues.rs, eventbus.rs, QueueStackResolver): REVIEW §2 #4, 'C# is \"accidentally partial\" (producer-only, gate-dependent)' — wrong on both halves. C# Redis-as-queue is bidirectional today: ListLeftPop/ListRightPop consumers (queues.rs:77-80) and ListLeftPush/ListRightPush producers (:113-116), gated on the exact-case literal "StackExchange.Redis" which is exactly what a `using` line contains. What is gate-dependent is C# *Kafka*: `_producer.ProduceAsync(` matches the needle "producer.Produce" (:107) only by substring luck, and its gate ["kafka","confluent"] is case-sensitive (signals_present:121-123 uses `source.contains`), so `using Confluent.Kafka;` alone FAILS the gate and the file emits nothing — not even the tag node. A2 — queue / message-broker extraction correctness across all 16 languages (queues.rs, eventbus.rs, QueueStackResolver): REVIEW §2 #4, 'ProduceAsync("orders"), kafkajs send({topic:\'x\'}), Java new ProducerRecord<>("x"), Go kafka.Message{Topic:"x"} ALL collapse to the topic-agnostic tag node queue_producer:kafka' — overstated for Java and Go. A2 — queue / message-broker extraction correctness across all 16 languages (queues.rs, eventbus.rs, QueueStackResolver): REVIEW §2 #4 / §3, 'the resolver pairs all-to-all (graph:1420)' — imprecise mechanism. graph/src/lib.rs:1413-1432 joins on the EXACT string after the prefix, and the tag node dedups per repo (NodeId::from_parts(GRAPH_TYPE, repo, kind, qname), queues.rs:147/:178), so there is exactly one `queue_producer:kafka` per repo. area_summaries.area: A1 — incremental build correctness (PARSER_STAMP, ParseCache determinism, generate_many cache, is_gmap_stale gating)
area_summaries.summary: The hazard is real and I reproduced its mechanism exactly. `engine/src/cache.rs:22` is `const CACHE_VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, engine inherits `version.workspace = true` (engine/Cargo.toml:3, root Cargo.toml `[workspace.package] version = "0.4.18"`), and `ParseCache::load` accepts any sidecar whose stored string equals that (engine/src/cache.rs:153). The store's `is_gmap_stale` keys on the same bare release (store/src/lib.rs:951, written at :749). I dumped the live sidecar at `/home/ivy/Code/glia/.ai/repo-graph/parse_cache.bin` — bincode 1 fixint layout, first 8 bytes `06 00 …` then `0.4.18` — so the recorded identity is literally the release string and a parser edit merged without a workspace bump is invisible to both caches. Audit 2026-06-10 #4 and #5 are DONE (the workspace-lockstep version and `Manifest.engine_version` + its test at store/src/lib.rs:1276); what remains is that a *release* is the wrong granularity. The pyo3 default is incremental (`#[pyo3(signature = (repo_path, incremental=true))]`, py/src/lib.rs:353) while the whole substrate-gap bench builds cold (grade.py:74 `generate(dirs[0], False)`, grade.py:76 `generate_many(dirs)` which passes `cache: None` at engine/src/lib.rs:125) — so eval cells flip while a real MCP-served repo keeps returning pre-fix nodes. Secondary findings I verified myself: `cli/Cargo.toml:3` pins `version = "0.4.13"` (not workspace), so `glia --version` already misreports a 0.4.18 engine — the same bug class as audit #4; `.github/workflows/wheels-py.yml:17-24` omits `engine/**` and `store/**` from its PR path filter; `cli/src/main.rs:584 generate_for` uses `generate_one` so every P2/P3 query command reparses from scratch. For the walk gating, `store/src/lib.rs:957` has a 6-name skip list while the engine walker gates on `is_hard_skip` (engine:996), `always_region` (engine:1003), `.gitignore` dirs (engine:1019) and `dir_is_build_bundle` (engine:1062) — glia's own `.venv-eval/` (.gitignore:16) is walked by `is_gmap_stale` and collapsed by the builder, which is audit #17 exactly. Hashing every graph-shaping source is cheap: 45 files / 1.32 MB, 11 ms with sha256 in shell, so a build-script content stamp costs nothing measurable.

area_summaries.area: A2 — queue / message-broker extraction correctness across all 16 languages (queues.rs, eventbus.rs, QueueStackResolver)
area_summaries.summary: Queue extraction is a 387-line text scanner (parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs) with two needle tables (CONSUMER_PATTERNS:46, PRODUCER_PATTERNS:83), a case-SENSITIVE gate (signals_present:121), and one identity function: extract_topic_near:196 does `source.find(pattern)` — literally the FIRST occurrence in the file — then extract_first_string_literal:202 accepts a quoted literal only if it sits immediately after an optional single `(` (:207-215, `'` and `"` only; no backticks, no `:atom`, no `@"..."`). Everything else falls back to framework_tag:192, so one topic-agnostic node per (repo, framework) is emitted with `cells: vec![]` (:152, :183) and Confidence::Medium. QueueStackResolver (graph/src/lib.rs:1409-1433, index at :1436) joins on the exact string after `queue_producer:`/`queue_consumer:`, so every repo whose topics failed to parse gets a false QUEUE_FLOWS edge to every other such repo of the same framework (N×M, bounded by repo count, not call sites). Three further facts I verified that the review does not state: the needles are receiver-name-bound ("producer.send", "writer.WriteMessages", "reader.ReadMessage", "nc.Publish", "queue.add"), so Spring's `kafkaTemplate.send("orders")` and Go's `w.WriteMessages` match NOTHING and emit no node at all; queue nodes have no in-repo edge whatsoever (QueueNodes has no `edges` field, :125-128; engine wires them with `run!`, engine/src/lib.rs:890-891, not `run_with_edges!`), so blast_radius can never reach a topic from the function that publishes to it; and `extract_queue_consumers`/`QueueConsumer` (:4-38) is dead code with no caller outside its own three tests (:236,:243,:253). Duplicate topic NodeIds do not lose nodes — merge_parses (graph:177-186) appends cells — but merge_nav (graph:207-215) overwrites `parent_of`, so per-file provenance is lost. No POSITION means position_file (engine:703) and locate_node (engine:1986-1998) return None for every queue node, and languages_present (engine:1629) cannot see a Kafka-only C# repo. Finally, bench/substrate-gap/grade.py:97-111 measures recall only — it has no negative assertion, so no fixture can currently catch a regression to tag-pairing; packet A2.0 adds `forbid_edges` before any other fixture is authored.

The whole HTTP pairing surface is four private functions in `graph/src/lib.rs`: `HttpStackResolver::resolve` (:1131), `build_route_index` (:1171), `index_route_node` (:1204) and `lookup_route_with_prefix_strip` (:1309), plus `normalise_http_path`/`normalise_segment` (:1278/:1295) and the hardcoded `API_PREFIXES` (:1307). Matching is a single exact `HashMap<(METHOD, norm_path)>` hit with one fallback that strips up to two leading API-prefix segments **from the endpoint side only**, so every review claim (a)-(g) reproduces. (a) `"ANY"` is emitted by nine parsers (ruby:469 `resources`, java:659/665, php:327, scala:429, dart:681, csharp:504, clojure:379, go:1152, python:1738) and is never a lookup key — all dead weight; I additionally found that Django (`ANY users/`, python:1738) and ASP.NET (verified `ANY api/users`, `GET {id}` in fixtures/csharp-aspnet) are dropped a *second* time by the leading-slash guard at graph:1228, so the ANY fix alone does not lift them. (c) `${base}` reproduces: `` `${env.apiUrl}/users` `` normalises to `/{}/users`, `API_PREFIXES` does not contain `{}`, lookup dies. (d) reproduces exactly in fixtures/py-http: ROUTE `GET /users/<int:uid>` and ENDPOINT `GET /users/${…}` coexist with zero HTTP_CALLS, and that fixture's own key.json admits it in a note. (e) TypeScript never calls `url_to_path` — `classify_path_arg` (typescript:1005) returns the raw literal, host and query intact; Dart is different from the review's claim (see corrections). (f) react.rs:70, angular.rs:51 and vue.rs:83 all mint `GET <path>` ROUTE nodes with a Text `ROUTE_METHOD` cell, which `index_route_node`'s legacy branch (:1227) indexes indistinguishably from a server route. (g) is not theoretical — I dumped `fixtures/angular-http-calls` and it emits **two** `route:/users` ROUTE nodes (one phantom, minted in the *client* repo from `this.http.get("/users")`, ROUTE_METHOD `{"method":"GET","handler":"","file":"users.service.ts","line":0}`) and **two** HTTP_CALLS edges, one of which is false; grade.py's recall-only scoring hides it. (h) confirmed by `--dump` across four fixtures: every ROUTE and ENDPOINT prints `path=None`; `locate_node` (engine:1969) reads only POSITION cells, and only parser-go and ts_routes put file/line in ROUTE_METHOD at all — the other thirteen ROUTE emitters write bare `CellPayload::Text(method)`.

VERIFIED: `check_route_attrs` (parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:470) opens with `let text = text_of(node, src)` (:471) and is called on the class at :218 and on each method at :351, so the class-level call text-scans the whole class body and re-emits every action route — I measured `HANDLED_BY 'GET {id}' -> 'GetUser'` AND `'GET {id}' -> 'UsersController'` on the shipped fixture bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/csharp-aspnet. VERIFIED: ASP.NET templates are relative — that fixture emits ROUTE nodes `'ANY api/users'` and `'GET {id}'`, and `index_route_node` drops them at graph/src/lib.rs:1228 (`&& path.starts_with('/')`). CORRECTION: the review's "the entire C# server side is unreachable from every client language" is overstated — a positive control I ran (C# `[HttpGet("/api/v2/orders/{id}")]` + TS `fetch`) scores HTTP_CALLS 2/2 = 1.00 today, so only the conventional shape (controller `[Route]` prefix + relative action template) is blind, which is exactly why the two shipped unit tests (csharp:824, :849 — both use leading-slash action templates) never caught it. VERIFIED: C# emits zero ENDPOINT nodes — a probe with a Refit interface, an `HttpClient` class and a minimal-API `Program.cs` produced 11 nodes and 0 ENDPOINTs. CORRECTION: the minimal-API scan is not missing, it is unreachable — `MapGet`/`MapPost`… already exist inside `check_route_attrs` (csharp:507-521) but top-level `app.MapGet(…)` parses as `global_statement`, which `visit_children` (csharp:60-84) drops; my Program.cs probe emitted zero ROUTEs. `push_client_endpoint` is real at code-domain/src/lib.rs:790 inside `pub mod endpoint` (:699) with signature `(repo, &ClientEndpoint, from, &mut Vec<Node>, &mut Vec<Edge>, &mut CodeNav, &mut HashSet<NodeId>) -> NodeId`; it needs an `endpoint_seen` field on the parser's `Acc` (java:84 is the precedent) — csharp/ruby/php/rust/elixir/scala all lack it. CORRECTION: `join_path` is not new — go already has a private copy (parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:1396, used :1111/:1307), elixir has `join_scope` (parsers/code/elixir/src/lib.rs:489, used :408/:422) and ruby inlines leading-slash normalisation (:675-679); Phoenix already composes scopes correctly (fixture elixir-phoenix-handled_by expects `/api/users` and reads 1.00), so Phoenix is the reference implementation, not a target. I measured every prefix-blind framework in one probe: Spring `@RequestMapping("/api/v1/users")` + `@GetMapping("/{id}")` → `GET /{id}`; Symfony `#[Route('/api/v1/users')]` class → `GET /{id}`; FastAPI `APIRouter(prefix=…)` → `GET /{id}`; Flask `Blueprint(url_prefix=…)` → `GET /<int:id>`; Rails `namespace :api do scope :v1` → `GET /users/:id`; Laravel `Route::prefix('api/v1')->group` → `GET /users/{id}` — and java + php show the same class-level double-emission as C#. Finally, ruby/php/rust/elixir/scala emit zero ENDPOINT nodes (grep for `push_client_endpoint` hits only dart/swift/go/java/python).

area_summaries.area: A5 — gRPC/.proto, GraphQL, WebSocket and EventBus resolvers
area_summaries.summary: Every claim in the brief checks out against the code, and three of them are understated. The `.proto` branch at `engine/src/lib.rs:318-335` builds a `module_id` it never materialises as a `Node`, calls `grpc::extract_grpc_service_nodes` (grpc.rs:54-79) which emits one GRPC_SERVICE per `service` block with a single INTENT cell and nothing else, then pushes into a separate `proto_parses` vec (:183, :333) that bypasses `stash_synthetic_parse` (:2016) entirely and is built through `build_python` at :446-450. A live dump of `bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/xcut-grpc-grpc_calls` confirms this: 4 nodes total, no MODULE for `user.proto`, `GRPC_SERVICE path=None`, no METHOD node for either rpc, and `package user;` nowhere in the graph. gRPC client needles (grpc.rs:98-106) are seven hard-coded suffix strings that all require `Service`/`Svc` before `Client(`/`Stub(`/`Grpc.newBlockingStub(`, so `Greeter`, `Auth`, `Users` produce no GRPC_CLIENT node in any language; grpc.rs:253-267 locks that in as intended behaviour. There is no gRPC server-impl detection anywhere in the workspace — a grep for `Unimplemented|RegisterService|BindService|ServiceBase|Servicer_to_server` across all `.rs` returns nothing. `build_grpc_service_index` (graph/src/lib.rs:1384-1402) keys on whatever follows `grpc:`, which is always the bare name. `names_match_graphql` (graph/src/lib.rs:1494-1499) is bidirectional substring, and `ws_paths_match` (:1535-1546) ends in an unconditional `(norm_c=="ws" || norm_h=="ws" || norm_h=="default")` wildcard plus byte-level (not segment-level) `ends_with`. The marker-parenting claim is worse than reported: dumps of all four xcut fixtures show GRPC_CLIENT, WS_CLIENT/WS_HANDLER, EVENT_EMITTER/EVENT_HANDLER and GRAPHQL_OPERATION/GRAPHQL_RESOLVER nodes with **zero incident structural edges** — `nav.record(..., Some(module_id))` (grpc.rs:149, websocket.rs:56/85, eventbus.rs:59/95) sets `parent_of` only, and no extractor except `services.rs:119` and `iac.rs:135` emits a parent edge at all, so a trace has no way in or out of a marker except the cross-edge. Finally, `CONTAINS` is not in `blast_carry_edges()` (graph/src/lib.rs:2167-2195), so the anchoring fix must use `USES`/`HANDLED_BY`, and `grade.py:90-111` has no negative-expectation support, so the three precision fixes in this area cannot be proven by any cell flipping until that lands first.

area_summaries.area: A6 — structural resolution depth (graph/src resolve_calls · resolve_refs · resolve_file · SharedSchemaResolver; code-domain CodeNav; per-parser heritage + field-type extraction)
area_summaries.summary: The review's structural claims are substantially correct and I reproduced every one of them as a measured 0.00 cell with throwaway fixtures graded through `repo_graph_py` 0.4.18. (1) Attribute resolution: `graph/src/lib.rs:572-591` (resolve_calls) and the identical branch at `:667-686` (resolve_refs) dispatch on `base_kind` ∈ {MODULE, CLASS, STRUCT} only, while `build_symbol_table` already registers PACKAGE children into `module_symbols` (`:238-243`) — so an Elixir `alias MyApp.Accounts` binds to a PACKAGE node and then every `Accounts.get_user(id)` dies; measured CALLS 0/1. (2) Receiver types: C#/Java emit `Attribute{base:"_userService"}` (`csharp:646-653`, `java:970-975`) and TypeScript ALWAYS emits `ComplexReceiver{receiver:"this.svc"}` because `this.svc` is a `member_expression` (`typescript:1165-1168`) — a pass that handles only `Attribute` fixes nothing in TS. Measured CALLS 0/1 for C#, TS and Java. There is nowhere in the codebase that records a field's declared type. (3) Heritage: TypeScript (`typescript:353-357`, `:369-373`) and Solidity (`solidity:465-466`) mint `NodeId::from_parts(.., "{module_qname}::{Base}")`, which is correct same-file (that is why `solidity-inherits_from` reads 1.00) and dangling cross-file; Dart (`dart:206`) mints a BARE-name id so Dart heritage is dangling even same-file. Measured 0.00 for all three cross-file plus Dart same-file; the dumps print `'Child' -> '?'`. Java/C#/Scala already go through `UnresolvedRef` + the `resolve_refs` global fallback (`graph:645-663`), which is the shape to copy. (4) TESTS is a MODULE-granularity post-pass (`engine:2159 emit_tests_edges`) whose affix rule (`:2307 strip_test_affixes`) is snake_case-only; `UserServiceTest` strips to itself and is `continue`d at `:2184`. Its gate `is_test_qname` (`:2284`) is shared with `is_test_fixture` (`:737`), which stamps the ORIGIN `test_fixture` provenance cell (`:685`) — so broadening it in place changes existing cells. (5) `resolve_ts_source` (`engine:2082`) returns None for any non-`.`-leading specifier, so `@core/auth.service` never binds; `tsconfig.json` is not even read (`.json` isn't in `detect_language`, `:756`). (6) Interface methods are never indexed: `build_symbol_table:245` registers `class_methods` only for CLASS/STRUCT parents, so the canonical `_userService.GetById()` against `IUserService` has no method table to land in even once receiver types exist. (7) `resolve_file` (`graph:2451`) and `resolve_frame` (`graph:2430`) match POSITION by basename; measured, `resolve('svc_b/utils.py','diff')` on a two-sub-project repo returns all four nodes from both `svc_a` and `svc_b`. (8) `SharedSchemaResolver` (`graph:1586`) iterates MODULE children only, so C#/PHP types under a namespace PACKAGE are invisible; measured SHARES_SCHEMA 0/1 across two C# repos. On `extra_hook`: none of these packets should be its first user — every fix here is language-uniform and belongs in the generic pass; the genuine candidates remain Python `SuperMethod` (hardwired to None at `graph:606`) and Go package-alias method lookup, neither of which is in this brief.

area_summaries.area: A7 — dependency injection / INJECTS edges across languages
area_summaries.summary: INJECTS (edge_category id 8, `code-domain/src/lib.rs:206`, ALL-table entry at `:294`, PPR weight 2.0 at `graph/src/lib.rs:2309`, blast-carry member at `graph/src/lib.rs:2180`) is NOT unemitted — it is emitted today by THREE parsers, not the "0 full / 2 partial" the review's matrix row claims. TypeScript emits it for Angular-decorated constructor DI (`parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs:222` DI_DECORATORS = Component/Injectable/Directive/Pipe, `:228` collect_constructor_injects, called at `:218`); Java emits it for Spring-stereotype constructors and `@Autowired/@Inject/@Resource` fields (`parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:472` SPRING_STEREOTYPES, `:483` INJECT_ANNOTATIONS, `:574` emit_constructor_injects gated by `is_bean` at `:164`, `:599` emit_field_inject); C# emits it for explicit `constructor_declaration` on name-suffix/attribute-gated classes (`parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:193` is_di_class, `:253` emit_ctor_injects, gated at `:201-205`). I ran grade.py on all four DI fixtures: `ts-angular-di`, `angular-injects`, `java-spring-injects` and `csharp-aspnet` each read INJECTS 1/1 (1.00). The resolution side is already fully generic and language-agnostic: every parser's `FileParse.refs` flows through `merge_parses` (`graph/src/lib.rs:172-186`) into `resolve_refs` (`graph/src/lib.rs:627`), which for `CallQualifier::Bare` tries module import bindings → same-module symbols → `unique_global_function` (`graph/src/lib.rs:747`), with INJECTS explicitly allowed into that global fallback at `graph/src/lib.rs:654`. `build_symbol_table` (`graph/src/lib.rs:240`) registers children of both MODULE and PACKAGE parents, so namespace-scoped C#/PHP types resolve by bare name. Consequence: **every packet below is parser-side only — no graph-crate change, no new NodeKind/CellType, no extra_hook needed, and no dependency on A6 receiver-type inference**, because every DI shape reads a *declared* type off the AST. The real blind shapes are: Angular's `inject()` function form and NestJS `@Controller` classes (the TS class-body loop at `:207-211` visits only `method_definition`, so `public_field_definition` is never read, and `Controller` is absent from DI_DECORATORS); Lombok `@RequiredArgsConstructor` and JSR-330/Dagger/Guice `@Inject` constructors in Java (ctor injection fires only when the class carries a Spring stereotype, and `injectable_type_name` at `:545` returns None for every `generic_type`, so `Provider<T>`/`Optional<T>` are dropped); C# primary constructors and `[FromServices]` (`class_declaration`'s primary-ctor `parameter_list` is a named child, confirmed in the 0.23.5 node-types, and is never read; `visit_method` at `:316` never touches parameters); FastAPI `Depends()` (python's `collect_calls_in` runs on the function *body* only, `parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs:571`, and `collect_type_refs` at `:1228` reads only the `type` field — the `value` field holding `Depends(get_db)` is untouched); PHP constructor injection (`visit_class` at `:133` walks only `method_declaration` and reads no parameters at all); Go wire/fx; Scala class parameters. Finally, the review's liveness framing is wrong in an important way I verified by dump: `entrypoint_reachable` (`engine/src/lib.rs:1731`) walks forward carry edges from entrypoint-kind nodes, but the Angular COMPONENT/SERVICE nodes are *overlay* nodes minted by the string-scanning extractor (`parsers/code/extractors/src/angular.rs:76`) with `parent=None`, and the `angular-injects --dump` shows them carrying ZERO edges — the INJECTS edge hangs off the ts-parser CLASS node of the same qname. In Java/C# the chain ROUTE-HANDLED_BY→METHOD dead-ends because DEFINES is not a carry edge. So INJECTS edges alone flip nothing to live; A7.8 is the packet that makes them matter.

area_summaries.area: A8 — walker scoping, gitignore semantics, project roots, scope filter
area_summaries.summary: All four walker claims in review §2 #2 are real and I reproduced them empirically against main=6071d3b with `repo_graph_py.generate(dir, False)`. (1) `always_region` (engine/src/lib.rs:1003) has no bin/obj/.vs/TestResults: a synthetic tree with `Api.csproj` + `obj/Debug/net8.0/Api.AssemblyInfo.cs` + `bin/Debug/Api.g.cs` emitted MODULE+CLASS `PhantomAssemblyInfo`+METHOD `GeneratedNoise`, CLASS `PhantomBinClass`, and a phantom PACKAGE `Shop::Api::Generated` — 6 junk nodes out of 17, and zero REGION anchors. (2) `is_hard_skip` (engine/src/lib.rs:996) drops a `.git` entry by NAME at walk_dir:1100, before the `path.is_dir()` test at :1103, so the submodule's own directory is descended into: `libs/sdk/vendor_client.py` (guarded by a `.git` file) was parsed under the PARENT RepoId, and `generate_many([parent, parent/libs/sdk])` then produced two `VendorClient` CLASS nodes and two `send` METHODs differing only in qname — exactly the pick_primary duplicate class. (3) `load_gitignore_dirs` (engine/src/lib.rs:1019) reads only the root file, drops globs/negations and matches the final component at any depth: a root `/build` collapsed BOTH `build/` and `src/build/` (two REGION nodes both nav-named `build`), while `dist-*` was ignored entirely and `dist-x/d.py` was parsed. (4) grep confirms zero sub-project notion anywhere. The `.git`-file `gitdir:` parser really does exist, at cli/src/main.rs:1160 (`resolve_gitdir_file`), used only by install-hooks. store already depends on repo-graph-code-domain (store/Cargo.toml:9) so a shared `code_domain::walk_gating` needs no new dep edge, and code-domain has a precedent inline module (`pub mod endpoint`, code-domain/src/lib.rs:699). crates.io is reachable (index.crates.io returns `ignore` 0.4.33; only 5 crates would be new to Cargo.lock). The fixture corpus is 71 dirs (not 49), and critically NONE of them contains a bin/obj/.git/.vs/TestResults/build/dist dir or a `.gitignore`, and only `fixtures/go-imports/go.mod` is a manifest — so these packets change zero existing fixture cells.

area_summaries.area: A9 — architecture summary / service map (`graph::cross_links` → `engine::service_map` → pyo3 → `glia arch`)
area_summaries.summary: The raw material is real and the aggregator is provably dead. `cross_stack_trace` at engine/src/lib.rs:1828 already labels every hop with a mechanism (`edge_category::name(e.category)`, :1863) and a `cross_service` flag derived from a `NodeId → RepoId` map (:1838-1843), and `MergedGraph` (graph/src/lib.rs:823-826) holds `cross_edges` separately from per-repo `edges`. The only aggregator is `print_mermaid` (cli/src/main.rs:367-406): it builds `repo_labels: BTreeMap<u64,String>` from `format!("repo_{}", g.repo.0)` (:372-376) and skips every link whose endpoints share a repo at :394. `cmd_analyze` (:297-311) calls `generate_one`, so there is exactly one RepoId and the skip fires on 100% of links. Measured: `glia analyze bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/xstack-ts-go-http --format summary` reports `cross-edges: 2` while `--format mermaid` emits three lines and zero `-->`; on the real monorepo `glia analyze /home/ivy/Code/quokka-stack --format summary` reports **53 cross-edges** (34 HTTP_CALLS, 6 WS_CONNECTS, 2 GRPC_CALLS) and `--format mermaid` still emits one hash-labelled node and zero links. The human repo label is genuinely lost: `RepoId::from_canonical` (core/src/lib.rs:64-69) xxhashes `file://{repo_path}` (engine/src/lib.rs:77-78, :122) and `GenerateResult` (engine/src/lib.rs:32-37) carries only `merged/total_nodes/total_edges/parse_errors`. The critic's correction holds and is now corpus-backed: quokka-stack's top-level segments are `quokka_web` (Angular), `quokka_android` (Dart), `turps` (Go+proto), `tools`, `scripts`, `features`, `docs` — the right v1 decomposition. The one place the review is materially wrong is node→file resolution: ENDPOINT and ROUTE nodes carry **no POSITION cell at all** (measured — every ENDPOINT/ROUTE row from `nodes_json()` has `path=None`, so `engine::locate_node` at :1969-2002 already returns `None`), and while ENDPOINT_HIT (cell 6) always carries `file` (code-domain/src/lib.rs:736-751), ROUTE_METHOD (cell 5) carries `file` in only **two** of sixteen emitters — Go (parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:1411-1438) and ts_routes (parsers/code/extractors/src/ts_routes.rs:112-116); python/java/csharp/rust/ruby/php/scala/elixir/swift/dart/clojure/react/angular/vue all emit `CellPayload::Text(<METHOD>)` with no file. So the packet needs a three-tier file resolver (POSITION → hit/method cell → adjacency via HANDLED_BY/CALLS), which is why the honest LOC is ~825, not ~330. Two further constraints shape the design: `graph` has no serde and deliberately hand-rolls JSON scanning (graph/src/lib.rs:1255-1258), so the serialisable shape and all cell parsing belong in engine; and `NodeId` is `Hash+Eq` but not `Ord` (core/src/lib.rs:20-23), so all ordering must go through `id.0`.

area_summaries.area: A10 — contract-file ingestion (OpenAPI/Swagger, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, Avro/proto messages, JSON contracts, tRPC)
area_summaries.summary: Every "none" row in review §3 "Contract-file and project-shape rows" verifies. `.yml|.yaml` is admitted at the walker by `is_bypass_path` (engine/src/lib.rs:1182-1194) and reaches the yaml branch at engine/src/lib.rs:199-236, which calls exactly three extractors — cron, config, iac — and `continue`s; there is no `openapi:`/`asyncapi:` sniff anywhere in the tree (grep for openapi/swagger/asyncapi/avsc/pact/trpc over all .rs returns zero functional hits). `.json` is dropped at walk_dir:1132 (`detect_language(rel)` is None for json) EXCEPT `package.json`/`composer.json`, which `is_manifest_path` (parsers/code/extractors/src/packages.rs:85-97) admits and the manifest branch at engine/src/lib.rs:266-289 consumes. `.graphql`/`.gql` are absent from `detect_language` (engine/src/lib.rs:756-785), and the graphql extractor already has a working SDL field scanner (`sdl_field_name`, parsers/code/extractors/src/graphql.rs:228-241) that no file ever reaches. `.proto` IS routed (engine:316-335) but emits only GRPC_SERVICE nodes with an INTENT cell (parsers/code/extractors/src/grpc.rs:53-77) — no message/enum nodes, no package, no POSITION, and the proto FileParse (engine:328-333) carries no MODULE node at all, so every service node has a dangling nav parent. No extractor in the repo emits a POSITION cell (grep `cell_type::POSITION` over parsers/code/extractors/src returns nothing), which is why the review's "no ROUTE/ENDPOINT carries POSITION" holds — I confirmed it live: `python3 grade.py fixtures/py-flask-handled --dump` shows `[ROUTE] 'GET /users' path=None`. That same dump pins the Flask ROUTE qname to the LEGACY shape `"GET /users"`, indexed by `index_route_node`'s second branch (graph/src/lib.rs:1199-1234), so a contract op pairs through `lookup_route_with_prefix_strip` (graph/src/lib.rs:1309-1332) with `/api/v1` stripping already working. AsyncAPI pairs onto `queue_producer:<topic>`/`queue_consumer:<topic>` (queues.rs:146/177, graph:1436-1459) but NOT through QueueStackResolver itself, which only walks producer→consumer. One finding the review's contract section misses: tRPC client calls are not invisible, they are mis-extracted — `"useQuery("` is in graphql.rs:9-19 OPERATION_PATTERNS, `extract_gql_operation_name` returns None without a `gql\`` tag, and the fallback at graphql.rs:79 mints `graphql_op:useQuery`, which `names_match_graphql` (graph:1494-1500, bidirectional substring) then pairs to any resolver named "Query".

area_summaries.area: A11 — service-hostname pairing and constant/env folding
area_summaries.summary: Both rows read "none" and I reproduced both failures end-to-end on main (6071d3b) with throwaway fixtures graded through bench/substrate-gap/grade.py. (1) Folding: parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs:1026-1045 `classify_template` replaces every `${expr}` with the literal marker `${…}`, discarding the expression text, so `this.http.get(BACKTICK${environment.apiUrl}/usersBACKTICK)` mints `endpoint:GET:${…}/users`, which normalise_http_path (graph/src/lib.rs:1278-1304) collapses to `/{}/users` and never pairs — probe measured HTTP_CALLS 0.00 with a matching Go `route:/users` present. Worse than the review says: the TS parser never calls `code_domain::endpoint::url_to_path` (code-domain/src/lib.rs:761) at all, so a plain absolute URL keeps its authority in the qname (`endpoint:GET:http://users-service:8080/users`, verified) and normalises to `/http:/users-service:8080/users` — every TS absolute-URL client is 0.00 today. On queues, queues.rs:196 finds only the FIRST needle occurrence and extract_first_string_literal (queues.rs:202-220) returns None on an identifier, so `producer.send({topic: TOPIC})` falls back to framework_tag (queues.rs:145/174) and mints `queue_producer:kafka` — reproduced. (2) Hostname pairing: the review's "ConfigResolver discards env VALUES" is misplaced — the discard is in the EXTRACTOR (scan_compose_environment config.rs:390 splits on `=` and keeps only the key; scan_k8s_env config.rs:354 reads only `name:`), and build_nodes (config.rs:103-142) mints CONFIG_KEY with `cells: vec![]`, so ConfigResolver (graph/src/lib.rs:1743) never sees a value. The infra side half-works: a compose file inside a scanned dir does yield `infra:service:users-service` INFRA_RESOURCE nodes (iac.rs:325-400), but only `image:` is read — `build:`/`build.context:` is never parsed, so the compose-service → source-directory link the join needs does not exist. Route ownership is the other half: routes carry no repo/service attribution, and I verified a hard blocker the review does not mention — ROUTE identity is path-only (`route:/users`), so two services in ONE repo serving the same path collapse into a single node with two HANDLED_BY edges, making monorepo host disambiguation structurally impossible until ROUTE qnames carry an owner. Multi-repo (generate_many) disambiguation IS achievable because RepoId separates the route nodes. The shared mechanism A2/A3 need is a repo-scope literal-constant table: engine/src/lib.rs:176 build_graphs_for_repo already holds every (path, source) of the repo in deterministic sorted order (walk_dir sorts at engine:1096), exactly where read_go_module_prefix (engine:165) already gathers a cross-file fact, and it threads into apply_cross_cutting_extractors (engine:363/860) which is the one place every text extractor runs. One hazard found: apply_cross_cutting_extractors runs INSIDE the cache-miss branch (engine:352-370) and its output is what `c.put` caches, so any cross-file fold must be applied outside that branch or a cached file will never see a changed constant.

area_summaries.area: A12 — producer/consumer message-type contracts (review §2 #6, §6 Batch B rank 12)
area_summaries.summary: Verified the review's A12 anchors against main (6071d3b) with reads plus live probes through the installed `repo_graph_py` 0.4.18 wheel. The core claims hold: queue nodes are constructed with `cells: vec![]` at `parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs:152` (consumer) and `:183` (producer); `cell_type::MESSAGE_TYPE = 17` is genuinely free (`code-domain/src/lib.rs:357` holds `IMPORTS = CellTypeId(16)`, the highest, and no `CellTypeId(17)` exists anywhere in the tree); the `ALL` table at `code-domain/src/lib.rs:362-379` is the only decode source (`py/src/lib.rs:489 cell_type_names`) and the round-trip test at `code-domain/src/lib.rs:922` iterates it; and no store bump is needed — `store/src/lib.rs:44 FORMAT_VERSION = 1` gates the container header while `core/src/lib.rs:145 Cell { kind: CellTypeId(u32), payload }` is layout-generic, and all 30 in-repo `cell_type::` uses are `==` filters with no exhaustive match. Three claims are wrong or incomplete. (1) Queue nodes do NOT reach the graph with empty cells: `engine/src/lib.rs:365 attach_imports_cell` stamps an IMPORTS cell on every node after the extractors, so a probed Go NATS producer carries `[(16, '["example.com/demo/gen",...]')]` — what is genuinely missing is POSITION (`path: None`, so `locate_node` at `engine/src/lib.rs:1969` returns `file=None` for every queue node). (2) "Every C# type sits under a namespace PACKAGE node → structurally blind" is half right: only BLOCK namespaces nest types under the PACKAGE (`parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:120-124`); file-scoped `namespace X;` leaves types as MODULE children, and I measured SHARES_SCHEMA = 1 for a file-scoped pair vs 0 for the identical block-scoped pair. The same MODULE-children blindness (`graph/src/lib.rs:1586`) also hits c_cpp, php, ruby, elixir and terraform, not just C#. (3) The A2 dependency is harder than "topic literals": `signals_present` (`queues.rs:122`) is case-SENSITIVE, so `using Confluent.Kafka;` matches neither `"kafka"` nor `"confluent"` — a realistic Confluent .NET publisher emits ZERO queue nodes unless a lowercase `kafka` token is present, and Java Spring Kafka (`@KafkaListener` + `ConsumerRecord<K,V>`) matches no needle at all (probed: 0 queue nodes). So the `ConsumerRecord`/`KafkaTemplate` half of `extract_message_type_near` is unreachable for Java until A2 lands. Finally, `bench/substrate-gap` has no cell dimension at all (`grade.py:89-112` only grades `expect_nodes`/`expect_edges`), so a prerequisite harness packet is needed before any MESSAGE_TYPE fixture can record a 0.00 baseline; and the parse cache stores the `FileParse` AFTER the extractors (`engine/src/lib.rs:363` then `:370 c.put(...)`) with `CACHE_VERSION = CARGO_PKG_VERSION` (`engine/src/cache.rs:22`), so a persisted 0.4.18 `parse_cache.bin` will keep serving cell-less queue nodes until the workspace version bumps.

area_summaries.area: A13 — data, infra, config, secrets, flags, migrations, CLI
area_summaries.summary: The review's Data/infra bullet is accurate on every claim I checked, but under-states two of them. (1) DATA_ENTITY keys mismatch on TWO independent axes, not one: the PREFIX (Java alone emits a bare simple name at parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:274-275; the extractor at parsers/code/extractors/src/data_entities.rs:68, python:932, go:867 and ruby:370 all emit `data_entity:<flavor>:<x>`) and the NAME (ruby:370 uses the MODEL constant `User`; python/go/extractor use the TABLE `users`). `DbResolver` (graph/src/lib.rs:1640-1658) indexes on the verbatim qname string, so Java↔Python↔Ruby never join. (2) The k8s CronJob bug is worse than "keeps the last schedule": `extract_k8s_cronjob` (parsers/code/extractors/src/cron.rs:158-200) never splits on `---` at all, so `current_image`/`current_command` bleed across documents and one node can pair the last CronJob's schedule with a *Deployment's* command — while iac.rs:206 DOES split, so the same file yields per-doc INFRA_RESOURCEs and one mashed CRON_JOB. Confirmed verbatim: `DbResolver` filters on `node_kind::DATA_ENTITY` only (graph/src/lib.rs:1648) so DATABASE(23)/CACHE(24)/BLOB_STORE(25)/SEARCH_INDEX(26)/EMAIL_SERVICE(27) never pair; `CliInvocationResolver` (graph/src/lib.rs:1903-1928) exact-matches `cli_invoke:<tool>` against `cli:<name>` where declarations are subcommands (cli.rs:88-103) and invocations are binaries (cli.rs:173-203) — and the list form `subprocess.run(["tool","migrate"])` extracts nothing at all because `extract_quoted` needs a quote as the first char; terraform emits `<module_qname>::<type>.<name>` (terraform/src/lib.rs:112-113) vs iac.rs:111 `infra:<kind>:<name>`, so `IacResolver` (graph/src/lib.rs:1794) can't even pair terraform-to-terraform unless two repos share a .tf path; all four config define-side scanners (config.rs:262/335/354/390) return `Vec<String>` names and `build_nodes` (config.rs:103-143) creates CONFIG_KEY nodes with `cells: vec![]`, so the values die in the scanner, not the resolver. Secrets/flags: a workspace grep for vault/secretsmanager/launchdarkly/unleash/flagsmith/openfeature returns two doc comments (config.rs:10,32) and zero code. Migrations: `.sql` is in neither `detect_language` (engine/src/lib.rs:756-786) nor `is_bypass_path` (engine/src/lib.rs:1182-1193), and walk_dir (engine/src/lib.rs:1132-1137) reads a file only if one matches — the bytes are never read; Django/Alembic/Rails migrations ARE read but their DDL is a DSL that `has_sql_context` (data_entities.rs:126) rejects, and `scan_sql_tables` (data_entities.rs:144) has no `TABLE` keyword so `CREATE TABLE x` names nothing even when read. ORM coverage is exactly `__tablename__`, `db_table`, mongoose, DynamoDB TableName, `.collection()`, Beanie and Cypher (data_entities.rs:313-333, 366-560) — no JPA @Table, EF Core, GORM, Prisma, TypeORM, Eloquent, ActiveRecord `table_name`, or Django implicit table. The "6 eval cells" count is exact: go-accesses-data·ACCESSES_DATA, java-spring·ACCESSES_DATA, py-accesses-data·ACCESSES_DATA, ruby-rails·ACCESSES_DATA, terraform·DEPENDS_ON, terraform·INFRA_REFERENCES. Two hazards the review misses shape the plan: grade.py raises ValueError on a category/kind absent from the `ALL` tables (grade.py:88-99), so a new-category fixture cannot record a 0.00 baseline until the registry entry lands; and `blast_carry_edges()` (graph/src/lib.rs:2167-2195) already carries SHARES_DATA_ENTITY / READS_CONFIG / DEFINES_CONFIG, so provider-level pairing must NOT reuse SHARES_DATA_ENTITY or every `blast_radius` answer silently widens.

area_summaries.area: A14 — Kotlin (review §3 headline + §6 Batch C rank 14)
area_summaries.summary: The review's core claim is CONFIRMED at `engine/src/lib.rs:771` — `"java" | "kt" => Some("java")` routes every `.kt` file through `tree-sitter-java`, and there is no `parsers/code/kotlin` crate (`ls parsers/code/` shows 21 dirs, none Kotlin). But "emit almost nothing" understates the failure: I graded a real 2-file, ~50-line Kotlin sample with `grade.py --dump` and it emitted 4 nodes / 2 edges — one MODULE per file, plus exactly those declarations whose header happens to be valid Java (`open class BaseService {`, `interface Auditable {`) and their DEFINES edges. It is a silent SUBSET, not garbage: no node had a wrong name. Everything Kotlin-shaped vanished — `class UserService : BaseService()`, `class UserController(private val userService: UserService)`, every `fun`, every call, every heritage link (measured: CALLS 0/2, DEFINES 0/1, IMPORTS 0/1, INHERITS_FROM 0/1, IMPLEMENTS 0/1). Some things DO work by accident and are load-bearing: `scan_ktor_routes` (`parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:708`) is a plain source-text scan, so Ktor `get("/path") { }` yields correct ROUTE nodes from Kotlin files today (measured 2/2), and the dotted import resolver produced a real `IMPORTS web→UserService` edge at 1.00 in the Spring fixture. The false-confidence claim is measured-confirmed: `coverage()` on a pure-Kotlin repo returns exactly two rows, both `language: "*"` (CALLS, HTTP_CALLS, both `edges_found: 0`), because `ext_to_language` (`engine/src/lib.rs:1653-1670`) has no `"kt"` arm and `COVERAGE_CAVEATS` (`engine/src/lib.rs:1556-1593`) has no Kotlin — or even Java — entry. I also tested the brief's question "should routing simply STOP": NO. `walk_dir` (`engine/src/lib.rs:1132`) only reads a file when `detect_language(path).is_some()`, so an unrouted extension yields 0 nodes / 0 edges — I verified by renaming the probe to `.kts` (already unrouted) and `coverage()` came back byte-identical to the routed case while the Ktor ROUTEs disappeared. Stopping makes the blind spot LESS visible and deletes working edges. Finally, the grammar: the crate literally named `tree-sitter-kotlin` (0.3.8) pins `tree-sitter >= 0.21, < 0.23` and cannot be used; `tree-sitter-kotlin-ng` 1.1.0 (tree-sitter-language 0.1, same 0.1.7 already in `Cargo.lock`) compiled and parsed clean against tree-sitter 0.26 in a scratch crate, and I dumped its AST for every shape the packets need.

The existing harness is smaller and healthier than the brief states: `bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/` holds **71** fixture dirs with a key.json (not 49 — `results.jsonl` records 1–13 all say `fixtures 71`, and BLINDSPOTS.md:3 says a stale 69), and `python3 run.py --no-log` today prints `BLIND SPOTS (recall 0.00): 0` across all 71. Grading is nearly free — 1 ms per fixture measured — so a 500-cell matrix run is sub-second and needs no perf design. The pyo3 surface needed for a three-level grade already shipped in 0.4.18: `nodes_json` (py/src/lib.rs:74), `edges_json` (:118), `node_cells(id) -> [(cell_type_id, payload)]` (:164) and the three decode tables `kind_names`/`category_names`/`cell_type_names` (:474/:482/:489) — **A15 needs zero Rust and zero rebuild**. The key structural problem is that grade.py's `expect_nodes` conflates "a node of the right kind exists" with "it carries the identifying literal" (one lenient substring match at grade.py:65), so the review's `◐ partial` and `· none` are scored identically today; and there is no way at all to express a phantom that must *not* exist, which means every precision fix in the merged plan currently has no eval gate. Live probes settled the derivation design: python/kafka emits `queue_producer:orders` (literal captured) but `queue_consumer:kafka` (literal lost, because `extract_topic_near` at queues.rs:196 finds the *import line* first) and therefore **no** QUEUE_FLOWS edge — the textbook `partial`; csharp/kafka with canonical `Confluent.Kafka` emits **zero** queue nodes (`signals_present` at queues.rs:120 is case-sensitive and there is no capitalised `.Subscribe` needle) — a `none`, not the review's `◐`; and python/mqtt captures the topic and routes it, but via `EVENT_EMITTER/EVENT_HANDLER/EVENT_FLOWS` rather than the queue kinds, which forces a `via` field into the cell record. The same mqtt probe exposed an unlisted precision bug: `graphql.rs:9-19` `OPERATION_PATTERNS` contains ungated `"client.subscribe("` and `"request("`, and the probe minted a phantom `GRAPHQL_OPERATION 'client.subscribe'`. New matrix fixtures must live in a **separate `matrix/` tree**, because run.py's `discover()` (run.py:29-30) globs `fixtures/*` and deliberately-failing fixtures there would destroy the committed `0 blind spots` invariant. Finally, `.gitignore:36` is a single-file rule (`bench/substrate-gap/results.jsonl`), so a committed `results-latest.json` and `COVERAGE.md` need no .gitignore edit.

area_summaries.area: A16 — remaining §1 pre-existing items + §0 documentation/state cleanup
area_summaries.summary: All eight items are real and still open on 6071d3b, but three of the review's framings are wrong in ways that change the packet. (1) The php cell: `python3 bench/substrate-gap/grade.py fixtures/php-laravel-calls` reads `CALLS 1/2 (0.50)` today — the miss is `index -> greet`.
