The doc-linker at `engine/src/lib.rs:531` is confirmed: its precision hole is the silent lowest-NodeId tie-break at :548-556, and `bench/doc-link/check.sh` is the existing precision gate (5 DOCUMENTS edges, `PaymentGateway.charge` and `OrderService.place_order` being the two qualified mentions). `escape_json` (py/src/lib.rs:335-341) misses every control char below 0x20 except \n\r\t, and `result.parse_errors` is read once at :366-374 for an all-empty guard and then dropped; py is `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` with pyo3 `extension-module` and has zero `#[test]`s, so the escaper must move to projection-text to be testable. Every §0 doc claim checks out: WP-0 was committed as e230e69/efba1af, tags v0.4.15–v0.4.18 all exist, `run.py --no-log` today prints no MISSING NODES block at all (and the last results.jsonl record, engine 0.4.17, already had `missing_nodes: 0`), `py/Cargo.toml` has zero parser deps while `engine/Cargo.toml:15-33` has all 20, and `dev-notes/issues_surfacing_now.md:3` is explicitly "cycle 2.0-gpu-14b". Finally: the engine has exactly ONE stderr marker on HEAD (`[incremental]`, engine/src/lib.rs:64 and :396) — every `[walk]`/`[arch]` marker the review quotes is a proposal, so each packet below introduces its marker from scratch.

packets.title: PARSER_STAMP: a content-derived build identity folded into CACHE_VERSION
packets.rationale: Today a parser or extractor fix merged without a workspace version bump is invisible to every incremental consumer. `ParseCache::load` (engine/src/cache.rs:147-155) accepts any sidecar whose stored string equals `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` = "0.4.18", and the pyo3/MCP default is incremental (py/src/lib.rs:353). I confirmed the on-disk consequence: /home/ivy/Code/glia/.ai/repo-graph/parse_cache.bin begins `06 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 | 30 2e 34 2e 31 38` = bincode length-6 string "0.4.18". Ship a parser fix, rebuild the wheel, and every file whose bytes did not change keeps serving the pre-fix FileParse — while bench/substrate-gap (grade.py:74, cold builds) reports the cell flipped to 1.00. Every other packet in this programme is a parser/extractor change, so this lands first or the whole programme is unverifiable in production. A second payoff: the recorded stamp is the direct cure for the known `maturin build reuses a stale .so` failure (dev-notes memory feedback_maturin_stale_wheel) — with A1.6 the installed wheel can be asked which code it contains.
entry_points: engine/src/cache.rs:22 — `const CACHE_VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");` becomes `repo_graph_stamp::BUILD_STAMP`
engine/src/cache.rs:61 — the `version: String` field of `ParseCache` (first serialized field; its bincode encoding is what the gate test decodes) is renamed `stamp`
engine/src/cache.rs:81 — `version: CACHE_VERSION.to_string()` in `Default for ParseCache` follows the rename

engine/src/cache.rs:147-155 — `ParseCache::load`: the silent `Ok(c) if c.version == CACHE_VERSION => c, _ => ParseCache::new()` gains an explicit mismatch arm that prints the fired_on marker before discarding
engine/src/lib.rs:395-398 — the existing `[incremental] reused … (parse cache)` eprintln gains `, stamp=<BUILD_STAMP>` so the always-on line carries grep-proof
engine/src/lib.rs:29-30 — next to `pub mod cache; pub use cache::{CacheStats, ParseCache};` add `pub use repo_graph_stamp::BUILD_STAMP;` so cli/py reach the stamp without a new direct dependency
Cargo.toml:55 — the `members` list (currently ends `"py",`) gains `"stamp",`
.github/workflows/wheels-py.yml:17-24 — the PR `paths` filter gains `stamp/**`, `engine/**`, `store/**` (all three are missing today)
packets.implementation:
DESIGN CHOICE, with the three options weighed as the brief asks.
(a) A const built from parser crate versions — REJECTED. Parser crates carry independent hand-set versions (parsers/code/python/Cargo.toml:3 = 0.4.3, parsers/code/extractors/Cargo.toml:3 = 0.4.9), so this needs per-crate bump discipline in 21 places and still misses code-domain/graph/engine. It is audit #4's failure mode multiplied by 21.
(b) A hand-bumped constant with a CI check — REJECTED. The CI check needs a reference value, i.e. it needs (c) anyway, and it fails open on every local build.
(c) A build.rs content hash — CHOSEN. No discipline required, exact, content-addressed so it is reproducible across machines and checkouts, and measured cost is trivial: the input set is 45 files / 1,317,434 bytes today and hashes in ~11 ms (measured with sha256sum; FNV-1a is faster). `.gmap` is write-once rebuild-whole-file, so an over-invalidation costs exactly one full rebuild — the asymmetry strongly favours hashing broadly.

WHERE IT LIVES. Both `engine` (parse cache) and `store` (manifest, packet A1.2) need the value. `store` depends on core/code-domain/graph only and `engine` dev-depends on `store`, so it cannot live in engine. Putting the build.rs in `core` or `graph` would rebuild the entire downstream DAG on every source edit. So: a new leaf crate `stamp/` (package `repo-graph-stamp`, publish=false, `version.workspace = true`, NO dependencies and NO build-dependencies) whose only job is to carry the const. Recompile cascade on a parser edit is then stamp (≈nothing) + store; engine/cli/py already rebuild.

stamp/build.rs (~85 LOC, no external crates):
  const HASHED_ROOTS: &[&str] = &["core", "code-domain", "graph", "engine", "store", "parsers"];  // NOT py/cli/doc-sources (they cannot change .gmap or FileParse content, and including cli would invalidate every cache on a CLI tweak); NOT projection-text/activation (query-time projections, not stored bytes)
  const HASHED_FILES: &[&str] = &["Cargo.lock"];  // committed (git ls-files confirms), and the ONLY thing that captures a tree-sitter grammar bump, which changes parse output with zero .rs diff
  const MIN_INPUTS: usize = 30;
  Resolve the workspace root as `Path::new(&env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")?).parent()` — never from cwd, because maturin builds with `working-directory: py` (.github/workflows/wheels-py.yml:50).
  Collect, under each root, every file whose path contains a `src` component and ends in `.rs`, plus every `Cargo.toml`; skip any path containing a `target` component. Key each input by its root-relative path rendered with `/` separators from `Path::components()` (never `Display`, so Windows produces the same key). Strip `\r` bytes from the contents before hashing so a CRLF checkout hashes identically.
  Sort inputs by key, then feed a 64-bit FNV-1a: for each input, absorb key bytes, a 0 byte, the length as 8 LE bytes, then the contents. Length framing prevents concatenation collisions. FNV-1a inline (12 LOC) is chosen over twox-hash so the crate has zero build-dependencies — a build-dependency compiles for the HOST target and would be built twice in the aarch64/manylinux cross matrix.
  If `inputs.len() < MIN_INPUTS`, write `cargo:warning=` lines and `std::process::exit(1)` — failing the build is correct, and it avoids a literal `panic!` per the no-panic rule. A silently-empty hash would be the exact hazard this packet exists to kill.
  Emit `cargo:rustc-env=GLIA_PARSER_STAMP={:016x}`, then one `cargo:rerun-if-changed=` per input file AND one per directory visited (directory mtime is what changes when a file is ADDED — without the dir lines a brand-new parser file would not retrigger the script), plus `cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs`.

stamp/src/lib.rs (~18 LOC): `pub const RELEASE: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");`, `pub const PARSER_STAMP: &str = env!("GLIA_PARSER_STAMP");`, `pub const BUILD_STAMP: &str = concat!(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), "+p", env!("GLIA_PARSER_STAMP"));` (concat! over env! is legal — both expand to literals), and `pub const VERSION_LINE: &str = concat!(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), " (build ", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), "+p", env!("GLIA_PARSER_STAMP"), ")");` for A1.6. Format is semver build metadata: `0.4.18+p3fa9c1d0b7e45a12`, fixed length, `+p` prefix so a human reads it as "release plus parser hash".

engine/src/cache.rs: add `repo-graph-stamp = { path = "../stamp" }` to engine/Cargo.toml; `const CACHE_VERSION: &str = repo_graph_stamp::BUILD_STAMP;` at :22 with the doc comment rewritten to explain that the release alone was the wrong granularity (keep the audit #4 history line). Rename the struct field `version` → `stamp` (:61, :81, :153) — bincode does not encode field names, so this costs nothing on the wire. Rewrite `load`'s match as three arms: stamp equal → reuse; `Ok(c)` → `eprintln!("[incremental] cache stamp mismatch (disk={} build={CACHE_VERSION}) — full reparse", c.stamp); ParseCache::new()`; `Err(_)` → `ParseCache::new()`.

engine/src/lib.rs:395-398: extend the format string to `"[incremental] reused {reused}, reparsed {reparsed}, evicted {} (parse cache, stamp={})", c.stats.evicted, crate::cache::CACHE_VERSION` — make `CACHE_VERSION` `pub(crate)` or read it via the new `pub use repo_graph_stamp::BUILD_STAMP`.

CLAUDE.md: one line in the Workspace Layout block — `stamp/              Build identity (PARSER_STAMP) — content hash of every graph-shaping source`.
packets.acceptance: New test `engine/tests/parser_stamp.rs::cache_stamp_binds_to_parser_sources_not_just_release`, which is authorable and RUNNABLE on pre-fix main 6071d3b (it uses only today's public API plus raw sidecar bytes, so it fails on an assertion, not a compile error). Steps: tempdir repo with two .py files → `generate_one_incremental(repo)` → read `<repo>/.ai/repo-graph/parse_cache.bin` → decode the leading bincode string (`len = u64::from_le_bytes(b[0..8])`, `stamp = str::from_utf8(&b[8..8+len])`; guard `len < 64` and ASCII-printable with an explicit message) → (1) `assert_ne!(stamp, env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), "on-disk cache stamp is the bare release version — a parser change cannot invalidate it")`; (2) `assert!(stamp.starts_with(concat!(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), "+p")))` and the 16-char tail is all lowercase hex; (3) positive control `assert!(!ParseCache::load(repo).is_empty())`; (4) flip ONE hex digit of the tail in place (same byte length, so the bincode framing stays valid), write the file back, and `assert!(ParseCache::load(repo).is_empty(), "parser component of the stamp is not part of the accept check")`. RECORDED PRE-FIX BASELINE: on 6071d3b assertion (1) fails with the on-disk value `"0.4.18"`. No substrate-gap fixture can prove this packet — grade.py builds cold by construction (grade.py:74,76), and no fixture can simulate a source-code change; the bench-visible artefact is A1.6's `build_stamp` in results.jsonl. Also: `cargo test --workspace` stays green (481 + the new test) with zero edits to existing tests, and `cargo check --workspace` from cold-build.rs stays inside a second of its current cost.

packets.risks: maturin's sdist may prune files that the git tree has, so a wheel built from sdist could carry a different stamp than one built from the same commit in git — harmless (one extra rebuild for anyone who switches) but it should be verified once by running `maturin sdist` and diffing the stamp against a git build. A1.4 also edits the engine/src/lib.rs:395-398 eprintln, so A1.4 must land after this packet (declared via depends_on) or the two agents collide on one line. packets.area: A1 — incremental build correctness (PARSER_STAMP, ParseCache determinism, generate_many cache, is_gmap_stale gating)

packets.title: Fold the same stamp into the .gmap manifest and is_gmap_stale
packets.rationale: The parse cache is only half the hazard. `is_gmap_stale` (store/src/lib.rs:937) is what the repo-graph MCP wrapper calls (py/src/lib.rs:468 `is_stale`) to decide load-vs-regenerate, and it accepts any manifest whose `engine_version` equals the bare release (store/src/lib.rs:951, written at :749; the live manifest at /home/ivy/Code/glia/.ai/repo-graph/manifest.json reads `"engine_version": "0.4.18"`). So even with A1.1 in place, a repo whose source files have not changed keeps serving a .gmap produced by pre-fix code — the graph is loaded whole from disk and the parse cache is never consulted. This is audit 2026-06-10 #5 and #9 ("a pre-gating engine's 23k-node junk graph survived the 0.4.16 upgrade") at finer granularity: #5 fixed upgrade-between-releases, this fixes change-within-a-release.
entry_points: store/src/lib.rs:641-655 — `pub struct Manifest`; add `build_stamp: String` with `#[serde(default)]` directly after `engine_version` (:651) so JSON field order stays readable

packets.title: ParseCache sidecar: BTreeMap entries + per-pid tmp file
packets.rationale: Two separate issues live at engine/src/cache.rs:73 and :175, and only one is a bug. The bug: `save` writes through a fixed `parse_cache.bin.tmp` (:175) and then renames it (:177). Two builds of the same repo at once — the repo-graph MCP server plus a `glia build`, which is a routine combination — interleave on that one path, and the rename publishes whichever partial byte sequence won. It is self-healing (a corrupt sidecar deserializes as Err and `load` returns an empty cache) but it silently throws away the cache and, with A1.1's marker, will look like a stamp problem. The hygiene: `entries: HashMap` (:73) means `bincode::serialize` walks a per-instance RandomState, so two runs over identical inputs produce different sidecar bytes. Its real value is that 'same input, same bytes' makes the sidecar diffable and content-addressable, which is what any future Engram `--since` diff will stand on.

packets.title: Bench guard: regrade every fixture through the incremental path and diff the matrix
packets.rationale: Honest framing (CODE_RULES §8): this closes no blind spot and flips no cell — it PASSES today and is a regression guard, and it should be scheduled last in the area. Its value is coverage of a gap the Rust tests cannot reach: `engine/tests/byte_identical.rs` proves incremental == clean for exactly ONE hand-written fixture (2 python files, 1 go file, 1 ts file, 1 markdown — byte_identical.rs:16-35), while bench/substrate-gap has 49 fixtures across 16 languages and 30 mechanisms, every one of which currently builds only cold (grade.py:74,76). Every packet in batches A/B/C is a parser or extractor change, and the failure this guards against — a cached FileParse that no longer matches what the changed parser would produce — is silent by construction. Running the whole fixture set through the cache is the cheapest broad proof that the cache is still transparent.

bench/substrate-gap/grade.py:55 — `os.environ.setdefault("GLIA_NO_PERSIST", "1")` gates the gmap write only (py/src/lib.rs:376-386); the parse-cache sidecar is written regardless, which is why the new script must copy fixtures to a tmpdir

packets.implementation:
New `bench/substrate-gap/incremental_check.py`, python3, no new dependencies, importing `grade_fixture` and `discover` from the existing modules so grading logic is never duplicated.
For each fixture directory:
  1. `shutil.copytree(fixture, tmp/<name>)` into `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` — NEVER build incrementally inside `bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/`, because the sidecar is written even under GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 and would pollute the committed tree (`.ai/repo-graph/` is gitignored at .gitignore:31-33, but a cache surviving between runs would silently de-hermeticise the matrix).
  2. Grade the copy COLD (today's path) → baseline `per_category` + `node_by_kind`.
  3. Grade the SAME copy twice more through the incremental path — once to warm the sidecar, once to read from it — and compare `per_category`/`node_by_kind`/`node_count`/`edge_count` against the baseline.
  4. Report any fixture whose warm result differs, with the differing cells.
Driving the incremental path: single-dir fixtures use `rg.generate(dir, True)` (already available); multi-dir fixtures use `rg.generate_many(dirs, True)` from packet A1.4 — so the script must feature-detect (`inspect`/try-except TypeError) and skip multi-dir fixtures with a printed SKIP line if the installed wheel predates A1.4, rather than crashing. Implement this by parameterising a local copy of grade.py's `build_graph` (about 8 lines) and calling grade.py's pure scoring helpers, not by editing grade.py — grade.py's hermetic cold path must not grow a mode switch that a future run could set wrongly.
Third pass matters: pass 2 populates the cache (every file `reparsed`), pass 3 is the one that actually reads it (every file `reused`). Assert on pass 3 and print `reused`/`reparsed` from the `[incremental]` marker if it can be captured, otherwise just state the invariant in the output.
Exit non-zero when any fixture diverges, so it can be wired into a pre-release check.
packets.acceptance: `python3 bench/substrate-gap/incremental_check.py` prints `[incremental-check] 49 fixtures, 0 divergent (cold vs warm)` and exits 0 against the current tree — the guard's baseline is PASS, and that must be recorded as such rather than dressed up as a flipped cell. Negative control that proves the guard can actually fail: run it against a fixture whose source file is edited between the warm and read passes WITHOUT changing its length (so the content hash changes and the file is correctly reparsed) — the check still passes; then force a false hit by hand-editing the copied sidecar's stored content_hash for one entry and confirm the script reports that fixture as divergent. Also assert hygiene: after a full run, `git status --porcelain bench/substrate-gap/fixtures` is empty and no `parse_cache.bin` exists anywhere under fixtures/.

packets.title: substrate-gap harness: forbid_edges (precision) + located (POSITION) assertions
packets.rationale: grade.py measures recall only (grade.py:97-111): every key.json can say 'this edge must exist', none can say 'this edge must NOT exist'. The whole point of A2 is that a topic-agnostic tag node pairs with everything, so the proof of the fix is an ABSENT edge. NEW FILE parsers/code/extractors/src/queue_topic.rs (~210 LOC, no new deps):

```rust
pub struct TopicHit { pub topic: Option<String>, pub offset: usize }  // offset = byte index of the needle
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub enum TopicRule {
    ArgLiteral,                      // first quoted literal inside positional arg #0
    ArgIndex(usize),                 // first quoted literal inside positional arg N
    Keyed(&'static [&'static str]),  // `topic: 'x'`, `Topic: "x"`, `topics = "x"`, `'topic' => 'x'`, `queue: :x`
    KeyedOrArg(&'static [&'static str]),
    NoIdentity,
}
pub const MAX_HITS_PER_NEEDLE: usize = 32;
pub fn scan(source: &str, needle: &str, rule: TopicRule) -> Vec<TopicHit>;
pub fn normalise_topic(raw: &str) -> Option<String>;
```

`scan` iterates `source.match_indices(needle).take(MAX_HITS_PER_NEEDLE)` (boundary-safe, no manual slicing arithmetic) and for each offset builds an ARG REGION: from the end of the needle skip ASCII whitespace; if the next byte is `(`, `{` or `[` walk forward with a bracket-depth counter that respects `'`/`"`/backtick quoting and `\` escapes, stopping at the matching close, at 2048 bytes, or at EOF. Truncate every slice with a local `fn clip(s: &str, n: usize) -> &str` that walks back to the nearest `is_char_boundary` (std's floor_char_boundary is unstable; NEVER slice on a raw index — CODE_RULES forbids panics in non-test code). Positional args are split on depth-0 commas of that region.
- ArgLiteral = first quoted literal inside positional arg #0 ONLY. This is the precision-critical choice: `producer.send(topicVar, "payload")` must yield None (today it does), while `consumer.subscribe(Arrays.asList("orders"))` and `FutureRecord::to("orders")` must yield the topic. ArgIndex(n) is the same over arg n (AMQP `basic_publish(exchange, routing_key)`).
- Keyed: `let lower = region.to_ascii_lowercase();` (ASCII-lowercasing is byte-length preserving, so indices map 1:1 back onto `region` — assert that with a debug_assert_eq on len). For each key find `key` optionally wrapped in quotes, then whitespace, then one of `:` `=` `=>` `:=`, then whitespace, then a literal (quoted, or a `:atom` / `` `backtick` `` — those forms are what the current scanner cannot read). First key wins, in table order.
- normalise_topic: trim whitespace and stray `,`/`)`/quotes/backticks, reject empty, reject len > 128, reject any interior `\n`. (A2.6 extends it with URL/ARN folding.)

Rewrite both emit loops as: gate check unchanged → `let hits = queue_topic::scan(source, needle, *rule);` → `let mut any = false;` → for each hit emit one node per NEW (topic, framework) key in the existing `seen` HashSet → if no hit produced a topic, emit the framework-tag node exactly once (A2.3 then makes that node unpairable). packets.title: Task-queue identity is the receiver/class, not the first string argument
packets.rationale: For Celery/Sidekiq/Dramatiq/Oban the join key is the TASK, and the first string argument is a payload. `send_email.delay("welcome@example.com")` emits `queue_producer:welcome@example.com` today (queues.rs:174 → :196) — a phantom topic minted from user data, which then pairs with nothing; meanwhile the worker side (`@shared_task`, `include Sidekiq::Worker`) finds no literal at all and collapses to `queue_*:celery` / `queue_*:sidekiq`, so producers and consumers of the SAME task never pair while every celery repo pairs with every other celery repo.
entry_points: parsers/code/extractors/src/queue_topic.rs — add three TopicRule variants and their handlers: Receiver (symbol chain immediately before the needle), DeclaredSymbol (first def-like identifier within 5 lines after), EnclosingSymbol (nearest class/module/defmodule above)
parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs:86-97 — the Celery/Sidekiq/Dramatiq/Oban producer rows switch from the implicit ArgLiteral to Receiver

parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs:47-57 — the @celery.task / @shared_task / @dramatiq.actor rows switch to DeclaredSymbol; `include Sidekiq::Worker` / `include Sidekiq::Job` / `use Oban.Worker` switch to EnclosingSymbol
packets.implementation:
queue_topic.rs (~70 LOC):
- `Receiver`: from the needle's byte offset walk BACKWARDS while the byte is in [A-Za-z0-9_$.] or the two-byte `::` (clip to char boundaries), take the resulting chain, split on '.'/'::' and keep the last non-empty segment. Reject language keywords (`return`, `await`, `self`, `this`, `new`) and anything that is not a valid identifier start. `tasks.send_email.delay(` → send_email; `HardWorker.perform_async(` → HardWorker.
- `DeclaredSymbol`: from the end of the needle's LINE, look at up to 5 following non-empty lines; for the first one containing any of `def `, `fn `, `func `, `function `, `void `, `public `, `class ` take the identifier that follows the keyword; otherwise take the first identifier followed by `(`. Skips stacked decorators (`@shared_task` over `@retry(...)` over `def send_email`) because it keeps scanning until a def-like line.
- `EnclosingSymbol`: walk backwards line by line (cap 200 lines) for `class X`, `module X`, `defmodule X`, `struct X`, `public class X`; return X.
All three return None rather than a partial guess; the caller then falls through to the A2.3 unresolved sentinel, which is the honest outcome.

queues.rs row changes (identity semantics documented in a block comment above the tables, because this is the one place where the qname is deliberately NOT a broker topic): `.delay(`/`.apply_async(` → Receiver; `.send(` (Dramatiq) → Receiver; `perform_async`/`perform_in` → Receiver; `Oban.insert` → Receiver; `@celery.task`/`@shared_task`/`@dramatiq.actor` → DeclaredSymbol; `include Sidekiq::Worker`/`include Sidekiq::Job`/`use Oban.Worker`/`use Oban.Pro.Worker` → EnclosingSymbol. Additionally add a CONSUMER row `sidekiq_options` Sidekiq [] Keyed(["queue"]) so an explicitly named Sidekiq queue also surfaces (both nodes may exist for one class — that is fine and documented).

Marker: `eprintln!("[queues] taskq rule={rule:?} symbol={sym} framework={framework:?} file={path}")`.

Tests: celery_delay_uses_receiver_not_payload (asserts `queue_producer:send_email` and asserts NOT `queue_producer:welcome`), shared_task_uses_def_name, decorator_stack_skips_to_def, sidekiq_perform_async_uses_class, sidekiq_worker_uses_enclosing_class, oban_insert_receiver.
packets.acceptance: xcut-queue-py-celery: QUEUE_PRODUCER 'queue_producer:send_email' 0/1→1/1, QUEUE_CONSUMER 'queue_consumer:send_email' 0/1→1/1, QUEUE_FLOWS 0.00→1.00. xcut-queue-rb-sidekiq: same for 'HardWorker'. Note the raw edge count stays 1 in both (today a bogus celery↔celery / sidekiq↔sidekiq edge exists) — the fixture grades the topic qname, exactly as the review's hazard note demands. Unit test celery_delay_uses_receiver_not_payload fails if the payload literal is used.

breaking.what_changes: Task-queue node qnames change meaning: `.delay('x')` stops minting `queue_producer:x` (a payload) and emits `queue_producer:<task symbol>`; `@shared_task` / `include Sidekiq::Worker` stop collapsing to `queue_consumer:celery` / `queue_consumer:sidekiq`. Every framework-tag pairing between unrelated celery/sidekiq repos disappears and is replaced by per-task pairing.
in_repo_consumers: parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs:269-275 producer_nodes — `send_email.delay('hello')` now yields queue_producer:send_email; the test asserts only the kind today, strengthen it to assert the qname

packets.risks: Receiver-walk on minified or single-line JS can pick up a long chain; the last-segment rule bounds it. EnclosingSymbol scanning 200 lines back is O(file) per needle — acceptable because the needle count per file is small, but cap it as specified. Shares queue_topic.rs with A2.1 (sequence) and the tables with A2.2/A2.4/A2.6.

packets.title: Cloud brokers (SQS/SNS, Pub/Sub, Azure Service Bus) + URL/ARN topic normalisation + coverage caveats
packets.rationale: sqs/sns reads ●0 ◐3 ·13, pubsub ●0 ◐1 ·15 and azure_sb ●0 ◐1 ·15 across the matrix: there is not one cloud-broker needle in either table (queues.rs:46-117). These are the default brokers for anything deployed on AWS/GCP/Azure, so the graph is blind to the dominant async mechanism in cloud-native repos. They also need normalisation the file-local brokers do not: the identity arrives as a queue URL (https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456789012/orders) or an ARN (arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:orders), and unless both sides fold to `orders` they will never join.
entry_points: parsers/code/extractors/src/queue_topic.rs — normalise_topic (added by A2.1) gains the URL/ARN/path folding branch, applied to every rule's output so the same fold serves all languages
parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs:46-117 — ~16 cloud rows across both tables using the Sqs/Sns/PubSub/AzureServiceBus variants A2.1 defined
engine/src/lib.rs:1556 — COVERAGE_CAVEATS gains the queue rows (there is not one QUEUE_FLOWS caveat today, so a silent queue blind spot is currently undeclared)
packets.implementation:
normalise_topic gains, in order: if the value parses as `arn:` + ≥5 colon segments → take the LAST colon segment (SNS topic / SQS queue name); else if it starts with `http://`/`https://` → take the last non-empty '/'-separated path segment (SQS queue URL); else if it contains '/' and starts with `projects/` → take the last segment (GCP fully-qualified topic/subscription path); else unchanged. Then the existing trim/length/newline gates. Document each fold with its literal shape in a comment — this is the function everyone will read to understand why `orders` came out of a URL.

New rows (needle, framework, lowercase gate, rule):
PRODUCERS: `.send_message(` Sqs ["boto3","botocore"] Keyed(["queueurl","queuename"]); `SendMessageCommand(` Sqs ["@aws-sdk/client-sqs"] Keyed(["queueurl"]); `.SendMessageAsync(` Sqs ["amazon.sqs","awssdk"] Keyed(["queueurl"]); `.sendMessage(` Sqs ["software.amazon.awssdk.sqs","aws-sdk"] Keyed(["queueurl"]); `.publish(` Sns ["boto3","aws-sdk","amazon.simplenotification"] Keyed(["topicarn"]); `PublishCommand(` Sns ["@aws-sdk/client-sns"] Keyed(["topicarn"]); `.topic(` PubSub ["@google-cloud/pubsub"] ArgLiteral; `.topic_path(` PubSub ["google.cloud"] ArgIndex(1); `CreateSender(` AzureServiceBus ["azure.messaging.servicebus"] ArgLiteral; `ServiceBusSender` AzureServiceBus ["azure.messaging.servicebus"] NoIdentity.
CONSUMERS: `.receive_message(` Sqs ["boto3"] Keyed(["queueurl"]); `ReceiveMessageCommand(` Sqs ["@aws-sdk/client-sqs"] Keyed(["queueurl"]); `.ReceiveMessageAsync(` Sqs ["amazon.sqs","awssdk"] Keyed(["queueurl"]); `.subscription(` PubSub ["@google-cloud/pubsub"] ArgLiteral; `.subscription_path(` PubSub ["google.cloud"] ArgIndex(1); `CreateProcessor(` AzureServiceBus ["azure.messaging.servicebus"] ArgLiteral. (@SqsListener and [ServiceBusTrigger] are A2.4's rows.)

packets.title: QueueStackResolver: broker-family gating + wildcard/pattern subscriptions
packets.rationale: The join key is the bare topic string (graph:1420, :1449), so it is kind-blind: a Sidekiq queue named 'jobs' pairs with a BullMQ queue named 'jobs' and a Kafka topic named 'events' pairs with an EventBridge bus named 'events' — false cross-service edges that blast_radius traverses. In the other direction the join is too strict: a Kafka consumer on `orders.*`, an AMQP binding `orders.#`, an MQTT `sensors/+/temp` and a NATS `orders.>` never match the concrete topics they actually receive, so every wildcard subscriber looks dead.
entry_points: graph/src/lib.rs:1413-1432 — resolve() gains family lookup + a wildcard fallback pass, and extends the A2.3 marker line with family_mismatch / wildcard counters

graph/src/lib.rs:1436-1457 — build_queue_index additionally records each consumer's family (read from the node's CODE cell written by A2.8) and collects wildcard consumers into a separate Vec so the exact-match hot path stays a HashMap lookup
parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs:10-24 — `family()` (defined in A2.1) is the single source of truth for the mapping; graph reads the string from the cell, never re-derives it
packets.implementation:
Family map (in queues.rs, A2.1): Kafka→"kafka"; RabbitMQ/Jms→"amqp"; Nats→"nats"; RedisList/RedisPubSub/BullMQ/Sidekiq→"redis"; Mqtt→"mqtt"; Sqs→"sqs"; Sns→"sns"; PubSub→"pubsub"; AzureServiceBus→"azuresb"; Celery/Dramatiq/Oban→"generic" (their broker is configuration, not code). Rule in the resolver: pair when the families are equal OR either side is absent/"generic". Absent MUST pair — graph/tests/stack_resolvers.rs builds nodes with `cells: vec![]` (:26-33) and those tests must keep passing unchanged.

Wildcards: `fn topic_matches(producer: &str, consumer_pattern: &str) -> bool` handling the three broker dialects, chosen by family: kafka uses a regex-ish `^...$` pattern string (treat a leading '^' as 'regex-like' and fall back to prefix-before-the-first-metacharacter matching — do NOT add a regex dependency); nats/amqp use '.'-segment matching where `*` matches exactly one segment and `>`/`#` matches one-or-more trailing segments; mqtt uses '/'-segment matching with `+` and `#`. Everything else is exact. Implement as a small segment-walk (~50 LOC) with no allocation beyond `split`. The resolver does the exact HashMap lookup first, then walks only the wildcard-consumer Vec — so cost is O(producers × wildcard_consumers), and wildcard consumers are rare. Guard against a pathological pattern by requiring at least one literal (non-metacharacter) segment: a bare `*`, `#` or `>` subscription pairs with nothing and increments a `skipped_catchall` counter (this is the WebSocket resolver's documented bug, do not repeat it here).

Edge confidence for a wildcard match is `weakest(producer, consumer)` downgraded one step to Weak — a pattern match is an inference, not a literal identity.

Marker: extend A2.3's line to `[queues] resolver paired=N skipped_unresolved=N family_mismatch=N wildcard=N skipped_catchall=N`.

Tests in graph/tests/stack_resolvers.rs: queue_resolver_requires_matching_family (kafka producer 'jobs' + redis consumer 'jobs' with family cells → no edge), queue_resolver_pairs_when_family_absent (the existing cell-less shape → edge, protecting the three existing tests), queue_resolver_nats_wildcard (producer 'orders.created' + consumer 'orders.*' → one Weak edge), queue_resolver_ignores_catchall ('>' alone → no edge).
packets.acceptance: New fixture xcut-queue-wildcard: QUEUE_FLOWS 0.00→1.00 for orders.created→orders.* with forbid_edges keeping billing.* at 0 violations. Rust tests: queue_resolver_requires_matching_family asserts cross_edges.is_empty(); queue_resolver_pairs_when_family_absent asserts exactly 1 edge (proves the three pre-existing resolver tests at graph/tests/stack_resolvers.rs:88,109,232 still pass untouched). The marker prints family_mismatch≥1 on the family test.

breaking.what_changes: QUEUE_FLOWS edges between same-named topics on different broker families are deleted (e.g. a Sidekiq 'jobs' consumer no longer pairs with a Kafka 'jobs' producer). New Weak edges appear for wildcard subscriptions. Nodes without a family cell keep today's behaviour exactly.
in_repo_consumers: graph/tests/stack_resolvers.rs:88-106, :109-126, :232-260 — unchanged in content but they are the regression guard for the absent-family path; add the four new tests next to them
bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/xcut-queue-queue_flows/key.json and -probe/key.json — both sides are NATS, same family, unaffected; re-grade in the same commit

packets.risks: Reading the family out of a JSON CODE cell in the resolver is stringly-typed; keep the parse in one helper and treat any parse failure as 'family absent' (pair), never as a panic. Same 50-line region as A2.3 — strict sequencing. If A2.8 slips, this packet degrades to wildcard-only (still shippable; drop the family half).

packets.title: Queue nodes get POSITION + per-site provenance + a module edge; locate_node reads the first POSITION
packets.rationale: Queue nodes are emitted with `cells: vec![]` (queues.rs:152, :183), so `glia blast-radius` and `glia trace` return file=None for every producer and consumer (locate_node, engine:1986-1998), `position_file` (engine:703) sees nothing, and `languages_present` (engine:1629) cannot count a C#-only queue repo. They also have no in-repo edge at all (QueueNodes has no `edges` field, :125-128), so nothing links the topic back to the file that publishes to it — and when two files publish the same topic, merge_nav (graph:207-215) overwrites the parent pointer and one of them vanishes from the graph entirely.
entry_points: parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs:125-128 — QueueNodes gains `pub edges: Vec<Edge>` (mirroring CronNodes, cron.rs:29-33)
parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs:148-153 and :179-184 — the Node literals gain a POSITION cell and a CODE cell, and a CONTAINS edge from module_id is pushed

engine/src/lib.rs:1986-1998 — locate_node breaks out of the cell loop on the first POSITION, aligning it with position_file (:703) and projection_text::node_position (projection-text:552)

packets.implementation:
queue_topic.rs: add `pub fn line_of(source: &str, offset: usize) -> usize { source[..offset].bytes().filter(|b| *b == b'\n').count() }` (0-indexed, tree-sitter convention per CODE_RULES §4 and parsers/code/docs/src/lib.rs:24; the slice is safe because offset comes from match_indices).

queues.rs: collect every hit for a (topic, framework) — not just the first — into a `Vec<(usize /*line*/, ())`. Emit:
- ONE POSITION cell, `CellPayload::Json(format!(r#"{{\"file\":\"{}\",\"start_line\":{},\"end_line\":{}}}\"#, escaped_path, line, line))` for the FIRST site, using the same escaping helper shape as cron.rs escape_json (:100) — reuse it by lifting it into queue_topic.rs rather than copying.
- ONE CODE cell `{"framework":"Kafka","family":"kafka","sites":[{"file":"src/a.ts","line":11},…]}` capped at 16 sites. This is the cell A2.7 reads for the family, and it is what preserves multi-file provenance after merge_parses (graph:177-186) appends cells from every file that publishes the topic. Use cell_type::CODE (already in the ALL table, code-domain:132-149) — NO new CellTypeId is needed for this packet.
- ONE `Edge { from: module_id, to: id, category: edge_category::CONTAINS, confidence: Medium }` per file, so every publishing file is linked even though the topic node is shared. CONTAINS is deliberate: it is excluded from blast_carry_edges (graph:2163-2195), so linking the module does NOT fan the blast radius back out through the whole file — the QUEUE_FLOWS edge stays the semantic path.

engine: swap the two `run!` calls to `run_with_edges!`; in locate_node add `break;` after the first POSITION is parsed (the loop currently lets the last cell win — see corrections).

packets.title: Broker pub/sub leaves eventbus.rs: Redis pub/sub, MQTT and NATS stop minting Weak EVENT_* nodes
packets.rationale: eventbus.rs:15 `("publish(", true)` is completely ungated, so `nc.publish(`, `channel.publish(`, `redis.publish(` and `client.publish(` all mint a Weak EVENT_EMITTER, and `.subscribe(` (:23) mints a Weak EVENT_HANDLER. Two failures follow: broker traffic is classified as an in-process event bus (EVENT_FLOWS, not QUEUE_FLOWS, so `glia trace` labels the mechanism wrong), and NATS/RabbitMQ producers DOUBLE-emit — the existing xcut-queue-queue_flows fixture carries a phantom EVENT_EMITTER:orders alongside its real QUEUE_PRODUCER:orders. Redis pub/sub and MQTT have no queue needle at all, so they only exist in this degraded form.
entry_points: parsers/code/extractors/src/eventbus.rs:9-18 and :20-28 — the pattern tables gain a third tuple field: a broker-suppression flag for the ambiguous needles ("publish(", ".subscribe(", ".on(")
parsers/code/extractors/src/eventbus.rs:30-64 and :66-100 — both emit fns compute a `broker_present` bool once from a shared signal list and skip the flagged patterns when it is true
parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs:46-117 — Redis pub/sub and MQTT rows so the traffic lands as QUEUE_* instead of vanishing
packets.implementation:

packets.implementation:
Add two OPTIONAL key.json fields, both defaulting to `[]` so all 71 existing fixtures are untouched:

`expect_absent_edges`: list of `{"category": "HTTP_CALLS", "from"?: str, "to"?: str, "note"?: str}`. `from` and `to` are OPTIONAL; an omitted field is a wildcard. This matters: the A3.4 fixture's nav ROUTE and its ENDPOINT share the display name `GET /dashboard`, so a from/to-qualified assertion is ambiguous — the honest assertion there is 'no HTTP_CALLS edge of any shape exists in this fixture'.

`expect_absent_nodes`: list of `{"kind": "ROUTE", "name": str, "note"?: str}`.

In `grade_fixture`, after the `edge_results` loop (grade.py:111), add:
```python
absent_results = []
for exp in key.get('expect_absent_nodes', []):
    kind_id = _KIND_BY_NAME.get(exp['kind'])
    if kind_id is None: raise ValueError(...)
    present = any(n['kind'] == kind_id and _node_matches(n, exp['name']) for n in nodes)
    absent_results.append({**exp, 'what': 'node', 'violated': present})
for exp in key.get('expect_absent_edges', []):
    cat_id = _CAT_BY_NAME.get(exp['category'])
    if cat_id is None: raise ValueError(...)
    present = False
    for e in edges:
        if e['category'] != cat_id: continue
        fr, to = by_id.get(e['from']), by_id.get(e['to'])
        if not fr or not to: continue
        if exp.get('from') and not _node_matches(fr, exp['from']): continue
        if exp.get('to')   and not _node_matches(to, exp['to']):   continue
        present = True; break
    absent_results.append({**exp, 'what': 'edge', 'violated': present})
```
Return `'absent': absent_results` and `'absent_violations': sum(r['violated'] for r in absent_results)` from the result dict.

`_print_verbose`: after the `edges:` block print an `absent:` block, `OK `/`XX ` per row, then the marker line `[gap] absent-checks: {len} asserted, {violated} violated`.

`run.py`: collect `(framework, note-or-category)` for every violated row into a `false_positives` list; after the `MISSING NODES` block (run.py:74-77) print `FALSE POSITIVES (absent-check violations): N` and one bullet each, then the same `[gap]` marker summed over all fixtures. Add `"absent_violations": [...]` to the jsonl record at run.py:81-88 (append-only history stays valid; older records simply lack the key).

README.md: add the two fields to the schema block at :30-46 with a one-paragraph note that recall cells measure extraction and absent-checks measure precision, and that a precision fix's baseline is 'N violations before, 0 after'.

No Rust touched. No existing recall cell can change — the new code only reads fields that no current key.json has.

packets.title: Tiered route matching: ANY wildcard, symmetric+configurable prefix strip, ${base} fold, suffix fallback
packets.rationale: `lookup_route_with_prefix_strip` (graph:1309) is one exact HashMap hit plus an endpoint-side-only strip of up to two leading API_PREFIXES segments. Three consequences, all verified: (a) the nine parsers that emit method `"ANY"` for method-agnostic server routes (Rails `resources`, Spring class-level `@RequestMapping`/`@Controller`, Laravel `Route::any`, Akka `path("x")`, Go `HandleFunc`, Clojure `ANY`, plus csharp/django which need rank-4 first) produce routes that can never match any client verb; (b) a client calling `/users` against a server mounted at `/api/users` never pairs, because the strip only ever removes prefixes from the client side, and the prefix list is a hardcoded 7-entry const (graph:1307) with a code comment admitting it; (c) `` `${environment.apiUrl}/users` `` — the single most common Angular/React client shape — normalises to `/{}/users`, `API_PREFIXES` has no `{}` entry, and the loop breaks on the first non-prefix segment. Every one of these is a dead cross-stack edge in a real polyglot repo.

The suffix tier is the larger risk and is double-gated — leading-`{}` required AND abandoned above 3 candidates. If the multi-service fan-out shows up in a real corpus, the first dial to turn is dropping tier 6 entirely; keep it behind a single `if` so that is a one-line revert. packets.title: Client request-path normalisation for TypeScript and Dart (host + query strip)
packets.rationale: Go (go:795), Java (java:1051), Python (python:1189) and Swift (swift:333) all route their client URL literal through `endpoint::url_to_path` (code-domain:761) before minting the ENDPOINT, so `http://api.example.com/users?x=1` becomes `/users`. TypeScript does not: `classify_path_arg` (typescript:1005) returns the literal verbatim, so `fetch('https://api.example.com/users?active=1')` mints `endpoint:GET:https://api.example.com/users?active=1`, which `normalise_http_path` turns into the nonsense key `/https:/api.example.com/users?active=1` — permanently unpairable. Dart is worse and differently broken: dart:570 `if !path.starts_with('/') { return; }` silently DROPS the endpoint entirely for an absolute URL, so a `dio.post('https://api/users')` produces no node at all. Absolute base URLs and query strings are the default shape in mobile and SPA clients, so this is a large recall hole in the two most client-heavy languages.

Add three pub fns to `pub mod endpoint` in code-domain/src/lib.rs, immediately before `pub fn url_to_path` (:760).

1) `pub fn join_path(prefix: &str, path: &str) -> String` — an exact port of parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:1396-1409, verbatim semantics so the go route tests cannot move: empty prefix returns `path.to_string()`; `path == "/"` returns `prefix.to_string()`; otherwise `let p = prefix.trim_end_matches('/')` and `format!("{p}{path}")` when path starts with `/`, else `format!("{p}/{path}")`.

2) `pub fn join_scope(stack: &[String], path: &str) -> String` — an exact port of parsers/code/elixir/src/lib.rs:489-507: push each non-empty stack entry, prepending `/` if the entry does not start with one and trimming its trailing `/`; then prepend `/` to `path` if absent; push `path`; if the result is empty return `"/"`.

packets.implementation:
Replace the text scan with an AST attribute walk. Confirmed against tree-sitter-c-sharp 0.23.5 node-types.json: `class_declaration` / `interface_declaration` / `method_declaration` each carry `attribute_list` as a direct NAMED CHILD (not a field); `attribute_list` -> `attribute` (field `name`: identifier | qualified_name | generic_name) -> child `attribute_argument_list` -> `attribute_argument` -> `expression`. String literal kinds are `string_literal` (child `string_literal_content`), `verbatim_string_literal`, `raw_string_literal`.

NEW `fn own_attributes<'a>(node: TsNode<'a>, src: &'a [u8]) -> Vec<(String, Option<String>)>` — iterate `node.children(&mut node.walk())`, keep `attribute_list`, then its named `attribute` children; return (simple attribute name with any namespace qualifier and generic args stripped, first string-literal argument if present). Reading only the node's OWN attribute_list children is what kills the duplication by construction: a class's attribute_list contains `[ApiController]`/`[Route]`, never the methods' `[HttpGet]`.

NEW `fn attr_string_arg(attr: TsNode, src: &[u8]) -> Option<String>` — find `attribute_argument_list`, take the first `attribute_argument` whose `expression` is one of the three literal kinds, return its inner text (for `string_literal` read the `string_literal_content` child; for verbatim/raw trim the delimiters). Positional only — a named `Name = "x"` argument (`element` has a `name` field) is skipped.

NEW `fn controller_route_prefix(type_node: TsNode, src: &[u8], type_name: &str) -> String` — from `own_attributes`, take the first attribute named `Route` with a string arg; substitute tokens (below); return `""` when absent.

NEW `fn substitute_route_tokens(tmpl: &str, type_name: &str, action_name: &str) -> String` — case-insensitively replace `[controller]` with `type_name.strip_suffix("Controller").unwrap_or(type_name).to_ascii_lowercase()` and `[action]` with `action_name.to_ascii_lowercase()`. Also accept the `{controller}`/`{action}` spellings. No unwrap: use `strip_suffix(..).unwrap_or(type_name)` which is total.

REWRITTEN `fn check_route_attrs(node, src, file_rel, handler_id, repo, class_prefix: &str, type_name: &str, action_name: &str, acc) -> usize` (returns the count for the marker):
  - For each own attribute whose name is one of HttpGet/HttpPost/HttpPut/HttpDelete/HttpPatch/HttpHead/HttpOptions: `let tmpl = arg.unwrap_or_default();` then `let tmpl = substitute_route_tokens(&tmpl, type_name, action_name);` then apply ASP.NET's real override rule — `let full = if tmpl.starts_with('/') || tmpl.starts_with("~/") { endpoint::abs_path(tmpl.trim_start_matches('~')) } else { endpoint::abs_path(&endpoint::join_path(class_prefix, &tmpl)) };` and `emit_route(method, &full, handler_id, repo, acc)`.
  - An attribute named `Route` on a METHOD composes the same way but with method "ANY".

packets.title: C# minimal-API top-level routes: walk global_statement and re-home the Map* scan as an AST invocation scan
packets.rationale: The `MapGet`/`MapPost`/… scan already exists at parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:507-521 but is unreachable for the shape it was written for: `check_route_attrs` is only called from :218 (class) and :351 (method), and a top-level `app.MapGet("/health", …)` in Program.cs parses as `global_statement` (confirmed in tree-sitter-c-sharp 0.23.5 node-types.json), which `visit_children` (:60-84) drops through its `_ => {}` arm. MEASURED: a Program.cs with three top-level `app.Map*` calls emits ZERO ROUTE nodes. Minimal APIs are the default template for new .NET services, so this is the whole server surface for a modern C# repo.
entry_points: parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:60 — `fn visit_children` : add a `"global_statement"` match arm alongside using_directive/namespace_declaration/type decls
parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:81 — `_ => {}` : the arm that currently swallows every top-level statement
parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:507 — `for method_name in &["MapGet", "MapPost", ...]` : the existing text-based Map* scan inside check_route_attrs; move it out into an AST scanner
parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:525 — `fn emit_route` : reused unchanged
parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:600 — `fn collect_calls_in` : the existing invocation_expression stack walk to model the new scanner on

parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:36 — `visit_children(root, src, file_rel_path, module_qname, module_id, module_id, repo, &mut acc);` : the single entry from parse_file; module_id is the HANDLED_BY fallback target
packets.implementation:
NEW `fn scan_minimal_api_routes(node: TsNode, src: &[u8], file_rel: &str, enclosing: NodeId, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId, acc: &mut Acc) -> usize`. Stack walk exactly like `collect_calls_in` (:600-620): for each `invocation_expression`, take `child_by_field_name("function")`; if it is a `member_access_expression` whose `name` child text is one of MapGet/MapPost/MapPut/MapDelete/MapPatch/MapHead/MapOptions, read `child_by_field_name("arguments")` -> first `argument` -> `expression`; accept only `string_literal` (read its `string_literal_content` child), `verbatim_string_literal` or `raw_string_literal`. Method = `name.trim_start_matches("Map").to_ascii_uppercase()`. Path = `endpoint::abs_path(&literal)`. Emit via the existing `emit_route(&method, &path, handler_id, repo, acc)` (:525).

Handler target: the second argument decides. If it is a `lambda_expression` / `anonymous_method_expression`, use `enclosing` (module_id at top level) as the HANDLED_BY target — same convention php's module-scoped route scanners use. If it is a bare `identifier` or a `member_access_expression` (a method group, e.g. `app.MapGet("/health", HealthHandler.Get)`), push an `UnresolvedRef { from: route_id, from_module: module_id, qualifier: CallQualifier::Bare(name) | CallQualifier::Attribute { base, name }, category: edge_category::HANDLED_BY }` and let the graph bind it — the shape parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:449-455 already uses. `emit_route` currently always pushes a HANDLED_BY Edge, so for the method-group case call a new `emit_route_no_handler`-style helper or emit the route node inline; do NOT emit both an Edge and a Ref for one route.

Also handle `MapControllers()`/`MapGroup("/api")`: for `MapGroup`, record the literal as a prefix and join it onto Map* calls found inside the returned chain's lambda body via `endpoint::join_path`. Keep this to the single-expression chain form (`app.MapGroup("/api").MapGet("/x", …)`) plus the lambda-body form; anything else falls back to no prefix. If this pushes the packet over 120 LOC, drop MapGroup and leave a `// TODO(A4.2b) MapGroup prefix` marker — the fixture does not exercise it.

In `visit_children` (:60) add: `"global_statement" => { n += scan_minimal_api_routes(child, src, file_rel, module_id, module_id, repo, acc); }` — note `visit_children`'s params already include `file_rel`, `module_id` and `repo` (:60-69). Also call `scan_minimal_api_routes` from `visit_method` (after the `collect_calls_in` at :348) so `Configure(IApplicationBuilder app)`-style registration keeps working, then DELETE the Map* block from `check_route_attrs` (:507-521) so there is exactly one implementation.

MARKER, emitted once from `parse_file` (:9-48) after `visit_children` returns, when the accumulated count > 0: `eprintln!("[csharp-minimal-api] {n} top-level Map* routes in {file_rel_path}");`. Thread the count back on `Acc` as a `minimal_api_routes: usize` field rather than changing visit_children's return type, to keep the diff small.

NEW unit tests: `minimal_api_top_level_routes_emit` (three top-level `app.Map*` calls -> `GET /health`, `POST /orders`, `GET /orders/{id}`) and `minimal_api_method_group_handler_emits_ref` (asserts one HANDLED_BY UnresolvedRef with `Attribute { base: "HealthHandler", name: "Get" }`).

packets.title: C# client ENDPOINT emission: Refit interface attributes + HttpClient call sites via push_client_endpoint
packets.rationale: MEASURED: a C# probe containing a Refit interface (`[Get("/api/users/{id}")]`), an `HttpClient` consumer (`_http.GetAsync(...)`, `_http.PostAsJsonAsync(...)`) and a minimal-API Program.cs emits 11 nodes and 0 ENDPOINT nodes. `grep -rn push_client_endpoint --include=*.rs` hits only dart/swift/go/java/python — C# is absent. Every .NET service that calls another service is therefore invisible to HttpStackResolver (graph/src/lib.rs:1131), so cross-service impact and trace stop dead at the C# boundary in exactly the direction (client -> server) the answer primitives are built for.
entry_points: code-domain/src/lib.rs:790 — `pub fn push_client_endpoint(repo: RepoId, ep: &ClientEndpoint, from: NodeId, nodes: &mut Vec<Node>, edges: &mut Vec<Edge>, nav: &mut CodeNav, seen: &mut HashSet<NodeId>) -> NodeId` : the real signature; emits one ENDPOINT node with a single cell_type::ENDPOINT_HIT Json cell, records nav, pushes a CALLS edge from `from`

code-domain/src/lib.rs:760 — `pub fn url_to_path` : the universal precision gate — returns None for any string that is neither `/`-leading nor a `scheme://` URL, which is what keeps `dict.GetAsync("key")` out
parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:50 — `#[derive(Default)] struct Acc` : add `endpoint_seen: std::collections::HashSet<NodeId>` (java:84 is the precedent)

packets.implementation:
Add `endpoint_seen: std::collections::HashSet<NodeId>` to `Acc` (:50-58) — it derives Default so nothing else moves.

PART 1 — Refit (~80 LOC). NEW `fn check_refit_attrs(node: TsNode, src: &[u8], file_rel: &str, from: NodeId, repo: RepoId, is_interface_member: bool, acc: &mut Acc) -> usize`, called from `visit_method` (:316). Reuse `own_attributes` from A4.1. Attribute names Get/Post/Put/Delete/Patch/Head/Options with a string argument map to the verb. PRECISION GATE: only fire when `is_interface_member` is true — Refit and RestEase contracts are always interfaces, and gating on that makes collision with any class-based `[Get]` attribute impossible. `visit_type_decl` (:127) already knows its own kind (`node_kind::INTERFACE` at :145), so pass a bool down through the body loop at :195-215 into `visit_method`. Path: `url_to_path(&literal)?` (Refit templates are `/`-leading or absolute URLs), then build `ClientEndpoint { method, path, file: file_rel.to_string(), line: pos.row + 1, col: pos.column + 1, confidence: Confidence::Strong }` from the ATTRIBUTE node's `start_position()`, and call `push_client_endpoint(repo, &ep, from /* the interface METHOD node id */, &mut acc.nodes, &mut acc.edges, &mut acc.nav, &mut acc.endpoint_seen)`. Note `[Get("/api/users/{id}")]` needs no interpolation handling — `{id}` is collapsed to `{}` by normalise_http_path (graph/src/lib.rs:1281) and matches a server `/api/users/{id}` directly.

PART 2 — HttpClient (~120 LOC). NEW `fn collect_client_endpoints_in(body: TsNode, src: &[u8], from: NodeId, repo: RepoId, file_rel: &str, acc: &mut Acc) -> usize`, called from `visit_method` right after the `collect_calls_in` at :348. Stack walk like :600-620, skipping nested `class_declaration`/`lambda_expression`/`local_function_statement`/`anonymous_method_expression` the same way. For each `invocation_expression` whose `function` is a `member_access_expression`, map the `name` text to a verb:
  GetAsync|GetStringAsync|GetByteArrayAsync|GetStreamAsync|GetFromJsonAsync -> GET
  PostAsync|PostAsJsonAsync -> POST
  PutAsync|PutAsJsonAsync -> PUT
  PatchAsync|PatchAsJsonAsync -> PATCH
  DeleteAsync|DeleteFromJsonAsync -> DELETE
Then read the first argument's expression; accept `string_literal` / `verbatim_string_literal` / `raw_string_literal` (plain, Confidence::Strong) or `interpolated_string_expression` (Confidence::Medium). Pass the result through `url_to_path` and DROP on None — that single gate is what stops `cache.GetAsync("user:42")` and `dict.GetAsync(key)` from minting endpoints.
Also handle `new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "/users")`: an `object_creation_expression` whose `type` text ends in `HttpRequestMessage`, verb from the first argument's trailing member name (`HttpMethod.Get` -> GET), path from the second argument. ~25 LOC; include it, `SendAsync` is the idiomatic shape for anything with custom headers.

NEW `fn interpolated_path(n: TsNode, src: &[u8]) -> String` (~25 LOC) — for an `interpolated_string_expression` (children `string_content` and `interpolation`, confirmed in node-types.json), concatenate `string_content` text verbatim and push the literal `"${…}"` for each `interpolation`. Mirrors parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs:1101-1118 and parsers/code/swift/src/lib.rs:386-400.

MARKER, once per file from `parse_file` (:9-48) when the total > 0, with a per-source split so a regression in either half is visible: `eprintln!("[csharp-http-client] {n} endpoints (refit={r} httpclient={h}) in {file_rel_path}");`. Carry the three counters on `Acc`.

packets.title: Spring/Micronaut/JAX-RS class-level prefix composition (java) + AST annotation read to kill the duplicate class scan
packets.rationale: MEASURED on a Spring controller with `@RequestMapping("/api/v1/users")` + `@GetMapping("/{id}")`: the emitted route is `GET /{id}` and there is a stray `ANY /api/v1/users`, so the real endpoint `/api/v1/users/{id}` exists nowhere in the graph and cannot pair with any client. The same probe shows `HANDLED_BY 'GET /{id}' -> 'UserController'` alongside `-> 'get'` because `check_route_annotations` is called on the class at parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:190 with `let text = text_of(node, src)` (:630) and `text.find(prefix)` then matches the methods' own annotations. bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/java-spring-handled/key.json literally documents this as '(class prefix NOT composed - bug)'.
entry_points: parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:620 — `fn check_route_annotations(node, src, _file_rel, handler_id, repo, acc)` : rewritten to read only the declaration's own annotations
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:630 — `let text = text_of(node, src);` : THE defect — the whole class body is searched
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:648 — `for (prefix, method) in &patterns { if let Some(pos) = text.find(prefix) ... }` : first-occurrence text search over that body
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:190 — `check_route_annotations(node, src, file_rel, id, repo, acc);` (class-level, end of visit_type_decl) : becomes prefix collection + own-annotation emission
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:229 — `check_route_annotations(node, src, file_rel, id, repo, acc);` (method-level, end of visit_method) : gains the class prefix
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:686 — `fn emit_route` : unchanged signature, now receives composed absolute paths
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:1482-1485 — micronaut_routes asserts `GET /things` / `PUT /things/{id}` / `DELETE /things/{id}` / `ANY /api` : the three relative ones MUST be rewritten to `/api/...`
packets.implementation:
Confirmed against tree-sitter-java 0.23.5 node-types.json: `class_declaration` carries a `modifiers` child, and `modifiers` has `annotation` / `marker_annotation` children; `method_declaration` carries `annotation` / `marker_annotation` either directly or via `modifiers`. `annotation` has a `name` field (identifier | scoped_identifier) and a required `arguments` field (`annotation_argument_list`, whose children include `expression` and `element_value_pair`). `marker_annotation` is the no-argument form (`@PostMapping`) and has only `name`.

NEW `fn own_annotations<'a>(node: TsNode<'a>, src: &'a [u8]) -> Vec<(String, Option<String>)>` — collect the node's direct `annotation`/`marker_annotation` children plus those inside its direct `modifiers` child; return (simple name with any `scoped_identifier` package qualifier stripped, first string literal found in `annotation_argument_list`). Prefer an `element_value_pair` whose `key` is `value` or `path` when present, else the first bare `string_literal`; reuse the existing `extract_annotation_string` for the literal-unquoting step so its escape handling is not re-derived.

NEW `fn class_route_prefix(type_node: TsNode, src: &[u8]) -> String` — first of `@RequestMapping` (Spring) / `@Controller` (Micronaut) / `@Path` (JAX-RS) with a string arg, else `""`.

REWRITE `check_route_annotations` to take `class_prefix: &str` and read `own_annotations` instead of `text`, preserving the existing verb tables at :632-647 and the JAX-RS `@Path` + `@GET/@POST/...` combination at :667-682 (for JAX-RS the method verb still comes from a sibling marker annotation on the SAME method, which `own_annotations` now gives exactly). Compose with `let full = if tmpl.starts_with('/') { endpoint::abs_path(&tmpl) } else { endpoint::abs_path(&endpoint::join_path(class_prefix, &tmpl)) };`. IMPORTANT: also handle the marker form — `@PostMapping` with no arguments currently emits NOTHING (measured); under a class prefix it must emit `POST <class_prefix>`. Keep emitting the class-level `@RequestMapping`/`@Controller`/`@Path` as its own `ANY <abs_path(prefix)>` route so the existing assert at :1485 (`ANY /api`) stays green.

In `visit_type_decl` (:87-191) compute `let class_prefix = class_route_prefix(node, src);` before the body loop and thread it into each `visit_method(...)` and into the :190 call. In `visit_method` (:193-230) add a `class_prefix: &str` parameter and pass it at :229.

MARKER, from `visit_type_decl` when the composed count > 0: `eprintln!("[java-routes] composed {n} action routes under '{class_prefix}' in {file_rel}");` (`file_rel` is a parameter of visit_type_decl, :90).

TEST EDITS (same commit): parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:1482 `GET /things` -> `GET /api/things`; :1483 `PUT /things/{id}` -> `PUT /api/things/{id}`; :1484 `DELETE /things/{id}` -> `DELETE /api/things/{id}`; :1485 `ANY /api` unchanged. `spring_routes` (:1430-1452) has no class-level mapping — VERIFIED unchanged. `webflux_functional_routes` (:1519), `javalin_routes` (:1547) and `ktor_routes` (:1489) go through `scan_webflux_routes`/`scan_javalin_routes`/`scan_ktor_routes` (source-level scanners, not annotations) — VERIFIED unchanged.

packets.title: Symfony class-level #[Route] prefix composition (php) + AST attribute read to kill the duplicate class scan
packets.rationale: MEASURED: a Symfony controller with a class-level `#[Route('/api/v1/users')]` and a method `#[Route('/{id}', methods: ['GET'])]` emits `GET /{id}` — the real path `/api/v1/users/{id}` is absent — plus a stray `ANY /api/v1/users`, plus a duplicate `HANDLED_BY 'GET /{id}' -> 'UserController'` because `check_route_attrs` is called on the class at parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:172 and text-scans the class body (:314). PHP is one of only two languages with http_srv at ● in the coverage matrix, so the Symfony half of that rating is overstated today.
entry_points: parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:313 — `fn check_route_attrs(node, src, handler_id, repo, acc)` : rewritten to read the `attributes` FIELD instead of node text
parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:314 — `let text = text_of(node, src);` : THE defect — the class body is scanned
parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:317 — `while let Some(rel) = text[search_from..].find("#[Route(")` : the loop that re-finds every method attribute at class level
parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:172 — `check_route_attrs(node, src, id, repo, acc);` (class-level, end of visit_class) : becomes prefix collection + own-attribute emission
parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:310 — `check_route_attrs(node, src, id, repo, acc);` (method-level, end of visit_method) : gains the class prefix
parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:598 — `fn emit_route_strong` : unchanged signature, now receives composed absolute paths
parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:325 — `let methods = parse_methods_kwarg(attr_text);` : keep; the `methods: ['GET','POST']` kwarg parse is orthogonal and must survive the rewrite
packets.implementation:
Confirmed against tree-sitter-php 0.24.2 node-types.json: `class_declaration` and `method_declaration` both have an `attributes` FIELD of type `attribute_list`; `attribute_list` -> `attribute_group` -> `attribute` (children name | qualified_name | relative_name, plus a `parameters` field of type `arguments`). So `node.child_by_field_name("attributes")` is the clean AST path — unlike C#, where attribute_list is a plain named child.

NEW `fn own_attributes<'a>(node: TsNode<'a>, src: &'a [u8]) -> Vec<(String, TsNode<'a>)>` — walk `attributes` -> `attribute_group` -> `attribute`, return (simple attribute name with any `\App\...` qualifier stripped, the attribute node so the existing `extract_first_string` / `find_attr_end` / `parse_methods_kwarg` helpers can run over its own text only).

NEW `fn class_route_prefix(class_node: TsNode, src: &[u8]) -> String` — first own attribute named `Route` with a string argument.

REWRITE `check_route_attrs` to take `class_prefix: &str` and iterate `own_attributes` instead of scanning `text`. Per `Route` attribute: extract the path with the existing `extract_first_string`, extract methods with the existing `parse_methods_kwarg` over `text_of(attr, src)` (now correctly scoped to that one attribute, which also fixes the current `find_attr_end(...).unwrap_or(text.len() - start)` fallback at :322 reaching past the attribute), then `let full = if path.starts_with('/') { endpoint::abs_path(&path) } else { endpoint::abs_path(&endpoint::join_path(class_prefix, &path)) };` and emit via `emit_route_strong` exactly as today (ANY when methods is empty, one route per method otherwise). Symfony's real rule is prefix-always (an action template is never absolute-overriding), but keeping the `starts_with('/')` escape hatch is harmless and matches how the existing tests are written.

At the class level keep emitting the controller's own `#[Route]` as `ANY <abs_path(prefix)>` so nothing that exists today disappears.

In `visit_class` (ending :173) compute `class_prefix` before the body loop at :163-170 and thread it into every `visit_method(...)` at :167 and into the :172 call. `visit_method` gains a `class_prefix: &str` parameter and passes it at :310.

MARKER, from visit_class when composed count > 0: `eprintln!("[php-routes] composed {n} attribute routes under '{class_prefix}' in {file_rel}");`.

NEW tests after `symfony_route_no_methods_is_any` (:907-923): `symfony_class_route_prefix_composes` (asserts `GET /api/v1/users/{id}`, `POST /api/v1/users` from `#[Route('', methods: ['POST'])]` — note the empty-path case must produce the prefix, not `POST `) and `symfony_class_scan_does_not_duplicate_action_routes`. VERIFIED: the existing tests `symfony_route_methods_list` (:880-903) and `symfony_route_no_methods_is_any` (:907) have NO class-level `#[Route]`, so their asserts at :898-901 and :922 are unchanged.

breaking.what_changes: Symfony ROUTEs under a class-level #[Route] change qname and NodeId (`GET /{id}` -> `GET /api/v1/users/{id}`; `POST ` from an empty action template -> `POST /api/v1/users`). packets.title: Laravel Route::prefix / Route::group prefix composition (php)
packets.rationale: MEASURED: `Route::prefix('api/v1')->group(function () { Route::get('/users/{id}', ...); Route::post('/users', ...); });` emits `GET /users/{id}` and `POST /users` — the `/api/v1` prefix is dropped entirely. `scan_laravel_routes` (parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:432) is a flat substring scan with no nesting awareness, and the code even documents the gap at :505-506 ('`$app->group(...)` prefix tracking is skipped — consistent with the Laravel scanner not tracking `Route::prefix(...)`'). Grouped routes are the default organisation of every non-toy Laravel API, so this is most of the Laravel server surface.
entry_points: parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:432 — `fn scan_laravel_routes(source, module_id, repo, acc)` : gains a prefix-range pre-pass

parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:442-458 — `while let Some(rel) = source[search_from..].find(needle)` : the verb loop; `start` is already a byte offset into `source`, which is exactly the key the prefix lookup needs
parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:447 — `let route_id = emit_route_medium(method, &path, module_id, repo, acc);` : path becomes the composed one
parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:464-490 — the `Route::resource(` / `Route::apiResource(` loops : must compose too
parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:505-506 — the comment documenting the skipped group tracking : delete it, the gap is closed
parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:620 — `fn emit_route_medium` : unchanged
parsers/code/elixir/src/lib.rs:371-402 — `scan_phoenix_routes` scope_stack : the reference design for range-scoped prefixes
packets.implementation:
Because `scan_laravel_routes` is a byte-offset substring scanner (not an AST walk), the clean design is a pre-pass that produces byte RANGES rather than a stack.

NEW `fn laravel_prefix_ranges(source: &str) -> Vec<(usize, usize, String)>` (~70 LOC). Scan for two forms:
  a) `Route::prefix('X')` — read the literal with the existing `extract_first_string`, then find the next `function` keyword after it, then its opening `{`, then its MATCHING `}` by brace counting that SKIPS braces inside single/double-quoted strings and `//` / `#` / `/* */` comments. Range = (open_brace_index, close_brace_index).
  b) `Route::group([...], function () { ... })` — read the array literal up to the first `,` at depth 0, look for `'prefix' =>` or `"prefix" =>` inside it and take the following string; then the same function-body range.
Also accept the chained builder form `Route::middleware(...)->prefix('X')->group(...)` by searching for `->prefix(` in addition to `Route::prefix(`. Nested groups are handled naturally: ranges nest, and the lookup below concatenates every containing range in outer-to-inner order.

NEW `fn prefix_at(ranges: &[(usize, usize, String)], offset: usize) -> String` — collect every range whose (start..end) contains `offset`, sort by `start` ascending (outermost first), and fold with `endpoint::join_path`. Returns `""` when none contain the offset.

In `scan_laravel_routes`, compute `let ranges = laravel_prefix_ranges(source);` once at the top, then at each emit site replace `&path` with `&endpoint::abs_path(&endpoint::join_path(&prefix_at(&ranges, start), &path))` where `start` is the already-computed byte offset of the path literal (:445, :467, :481). Do the same in the `Route::resource` / `Route::apiResource` loops.

Do NOT touch `scan_slim_routes` (:508) in this packet — the `$app->group('/api', ...)` gap is real but Slim has no fixture and the LOC belongs in a follow-up; update the comment at :505-506 to say so precisely.

MARKER, at the end of scan_laravel_routes when ranges is non-empty and routes were emitted: `eprintln!("[php-routes] laravel {n} routes under {g} prefix groups in {file_rel}");` — `scan_laravel_routes` does not currently take `file_rel`; add the parameter (its single call site is in `parse_file`, which has it).

NEW tests after `laravel_route_resource` (:948-966): `laravel_route_prefix_group_composes` (asserts `GET /api/v1/users/{id}` and `POST /api/v1/users`), `laravel_route_group_array_prefix_composes` (the `Route::group(['prefix' => 'api'], function () { ... })` form), `laravel_route_outside_group_unaffected` (a `Route::get('/health', ...)` after the closing brace stays `GET /health` — this is the regression lock for the range arithmetic). VERIFIED: the existing `laravel_route_facade` (:926-945), `laravel_route_resource` (:948), `laravel_route_handled_by_array_callable` (:967), `laravel_route_handled_by_string_callable` (:992) and `laravel_route_closure_handler_emits_no_ref` (:1011) sources contain no groups, so their asserts are unchanged.
packets.acceptance: NEW fixture bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/php-laravel-prefix flips HANDLED_BY 0.00 -> 1.00 and HTTP_CALLS 0.00 -> 1.00 (record the 0.00 baseline first; measured today the routes are `GET /users/{id}` / `POST /users`). bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/php-laravel-handled_by stays 1.00 (no group in that source). `cargo test -p repo-graph-parser-php` green with zero existing-assert edits plus 3 new tests. `cargo test --workspace` 0 failing.

Routes outside any group are unchanged. No edges removed; the HANDLED_BY UnresolvedRefs pushed at :449-455 keep their `from` = the (now differently-named) route id.

fixtures.purpose: Prove Route::prefix/group composition, including one control route declared outside the group. Baseline 0.00 on HANDLED_BY (composed name absent) and HTTP_CALLS.
fixtures.source_sketch: server/routes/web.php — `<?php use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route; Route::prefix('api/v1')->group(function () { Route::get('/users/{id}', [UserController::class, 'show']); Route::post('/users', [UserController::class, 'store']); }); Route::get('/health', [HealthController::class, 'index']);`. server/app/Http/Controllers/UserController.php — `<?php namespace App\Http\Controllers; class UserController { public function show($id) {} public function store() {} }` (needed so the HANDLED_BY ref resolves to a real method). client/api.ts — `export async function show(id: string){ return fetch(`/api/v1/users/${id}`); }`.

packets.title: FastAPI APIRouter(prefix=) and Flask Blueprint(url_prefix=) composition (python)
packets.rationale: MEASURED: `router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/users")` + `@router.get("/{id}")` emits `GET /{id}`, and `bp = Blueprint("users", __name__, url_prefix="/api/v1/users")` + `@bp.route("/<int:id>")` emits `GET /<int:id>` — both drop the prefix. `check_route_decorator` (parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs:1640) takes the path straight from the decorator's first string argument (:1661-1665) with no knowledge of the receiver. Python is the strongest-rated language in the matrix (http_srv ●) so this gap is invisible in the ratings, but every FastAPI service that splits routers across modules loses its real paths.

parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs:1665 — `emit_route(m, &path, handler_id, repo, acc);` : path becomes the composed one

packets.implementation:
NEW `fn scan_router_prefixes(root: TsNode, src: &[u8], acc: &mut Acc)` (~60 LOC), called from `parse_file` immediately after `scan_model_tables` (:59) so it runs before any decorator is visited (module-level routers are conventionally assigned above the handlers, but a pre-pass makes order irrelevant — the same reason scan_model_tables exists, see its comment at :56-58).

Walk the root's named children for `expression_statement` -> `assignment` with a single `identifier` left side and a `call` right side. Take the call's function text; if it ends in `APIRouter`, read the `prefix=` keyword argument; if it ends in `Blueprint`, read the `url_prefix=` keyword argument. In tree-sitter-python the argument_list child is `keyword_argument` with `name` and `value` fields; accept a `string` value only. Store `acc.router_prefixes.insert(lhs_name, prefix)`. Reuse the existing `first_string_literal` / string-unquoting helper near :1790-1820 rather than writing a new one.

Also handle the FastAPI include form so a router defined in the same file as its mount composes: `app.include_router(router, prefix="/api")` — a top-level `call` whose function ends in `include_router`, first positional arg an identifier naming a known router, `prefix=` keyword. Fold it onto that router's existing prefix with `endpoint::join_path`. Cross-FILE include_router is explicitly OUT of scope (the parser sees one file; that needs a graph-crate pass) — say so in a comment so the next reader does not think it was missed.

In `check_route_decorator` (:1640), after computing `head` (:1655), derive the receiver: `let receiver = head.rsplit_once('.').map(|(r, _)| r.trim()).unwrap_or("");` then `let prefix = acc.router_prefixes.get(receiver).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("");` and compose: `let full = endpoint::abs_path(&endpoint::join_path(prefix, &path));`. Pass `full` to `emit_route` at :1665. When there is no prefix, `join_path("", p)` returns `p` unchanged and `abs_path` only normalises a missing/duplicated leading slash — so `@app.get("/users")` is byte-identical to today.

Note `check_route_decorator` currently takes `acc: &mut Acc`, so the map is already reachable — no signature change at :490 or :565.

packets.implementation:
Replace the explicit-stack walk at :417-428 with a recursive `fn walk_rails(n: TsNode, src: &[u8], prefix: &str, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId, acc: &mut Acc)`.

For each node: if `n.kind() == "call"`, read its `method` field text. When it is `namespace` or `scope`, compute the segment this block contributes and recurse into the call's block child with the extended prefix; otherwise call `try_emit_rails_route(n, src, prefix, module_id, repo, acc)` and recurse into children with the SAME prefix.

Segment rules (Rails semantics):
  - `namespace :api do` -> segment `"api"` (a namespace also scopes the controller module, which we do not model — note it).
  - `scope :v1 do` / `scope '/v1' do` -> segment from the first positional symbol or string.
  - `scope path: '/v1' do` -> segment from the `path:` keyword pair; `scope module: 'x'` / `scope as: 'y'` contribute NO path segment (return `""`).
  - Anything else with a block -> recurse with the prefix unchanged.
The block child is a `do_block` or `block` named child of the `call` node; recurse into it with `endpoint::join_path(prefix, &segment)` when the segment is non-empty.

In `try_emit_rails_route`, compose at each of the three emit sites: the `root` arm (:447-456) emits `emit_rails_route("GET", &endpoint::abs_path(prefix_or_root), ...)` where an empty prefix still yields `"/"`; the `resources`/`resource` arm (:458-466) emits `endpoint::abs_path(&endpoint::join_path(prefix, &format!("/{name}")))`; the verb arm (after :497) emits `endpoint::abs_path(&endpoint::join_path(prefix, &path))`.

In `emit_rails_route` (:668) replace the inline `let path = if path.starts_with('/') { path.to_string() } else { format!("/{path}") };` at :675-679 with `let path = endpoint::abs_path(path);` — behaviourally identical for every current input, one fewer copy.

MARKER, from `scan_rails_routes` when any route was emitted under a non-empty prefix: `eprintln!("[ruby-routes] composed {n} rails routes under {s} scopes in {file_rel}");` — `scan_rails_routes` does not take `file_rel` today; add the parameter (single call site in parse_file, which has it).
