packets.title: grade.py `expect_absent_edges` — precision cells for edge-removal fixes
packets.rationale: Three packets in this area (A5.4 gRPC ambiguity, A5.5 GraphQL substring, A5.6 WebSocket wildcard) are pure precision fixes: they REMOVE wrong edges and add none. bench/substrate-gap measures recall only — grade.py:99-111 iterates `expect_edges` and scores found/expected — so a fix that deletes a false pairing produces no cell movement at all and is indistinguishable from doing nothing. Without this there is no falsifiable gate for half the area, and the house rule ('a fix is proven when its cell flips 0.00 → 1.00') cannot be honoured.
entry_points: bench/substrate-gap/grade.py:19-34 — the key.json schema docstring; add the `expect_absent_edges` block here so authors see it
bench/substrate-gap/grade.py:97-111 — the `expect_edges` recall loop; the new absent loop goes immediately after it, reusing `_CAT_BY_NAME`, `by_id` and `_node_matches` unchanged
bench/substrate-gap/grade.py:113-121 — `per_cat` rollup; absent results roll into the SAME dict under a `"!" + category` key so run.py picks up the column with no change to its matrix code
bench/substrate-gap/grade.py:131-140 — the returned dict; add `"absent_recall": absent_results`
bench/substrate-gap/grade.py:158-175 — `_print_verbose`; add an `absent:` block mirroring the `edges:` block
bench/substrate-gap/run.py:41-66 — the matrix builder already iterates `res["per_category"]` keys generically and sorts them, so `!GRAPHQL_CALLS` columns appear with zero changes; verify only
bench/substrate-gap/README.md:28-46 — the fixture-shape section where the new key goes
packets.implementation:
In grade.py, after the `expect_edges` loop, add:

```python
    # ---- precision: edges that MUST NOT exist ----
    absent_results = []
    for exp in key.get("expect_absent_edges", []):
        cat_id = _CAT_BY_NAME.get(exp["category"])
        if cat_id is None:
            raise ValueError(f"{fixture_dir.name}: unknown category {exp['category']!r}")
        present = False
        for e in edges:
            if e["category"] != cat_id:
                continue
            fr, to = by_id.get(e["from"]), by_id.get(e["to"])
            if fr and to and _node_matches(fr, exp["from"]) and _node_matches(to, exp["to"]):
                present = True
                break
        absent_results.append({**exp, "found": not present})
```

`found` is deliberately inverted: a forbidden edge that is still present scores 0, so the cell reads 0.00 at baseline and 1.00 once the pairing is removed — the same polarity as every other cell, so run.py's `if v["recall"] == 0.0: blind.append(...)` at run.py:64-65 needs no change.

Roll up into the existing `per_cat` dict under a distinct column label so the matrix stays one table:

```python
    for r in absent_results:
        c = "!" + r["category"]
        slot = per_cat.setdefault(c, {"expected": 0, "found": 0})
        slot["expected"] += 1
        slot["found"] += 1 if r["found"] else 0
    # (the existing `for slot in per_cat.values(): slot["recall"] = ...` at
    #  grade.py:119-120 must run AFTER this block, not before)
```

Note the ordering constraint: the recall computation at grade.py:119-120 currently runs immediately after the positive rollup — move the absent rollup above it rather than adding a second recall pass.

Add `"absent_recall": absent_results` to the returned dict. In `_print_verbose`, after the `edges:` block:

```python
    if res.get("absent_recall"):
        print("  absent (must NOT exist):")
        ok = sum(1 for r in res["absent_recall"] if r["found"])
        for r in res["absent_recall"]:
            mark = "OK " if r["found"] else "XX "
            print(f"    {mark} {r['category']:<14} {r['from']!r} -x-> {r['to']!r}  — {r.get('note','')}")
        print(f"  [absent] {res['framework']}: {ok}/{len(res['absent_recall'])} forbidden edges correctly absent")
```

run.py needs nothing beyond a `--no-log` re-run to confirm the `!CAT` columns render; `results.jsonl` gains the new per_category keys automatically (append-only, so history stays diffable). README gains a short paragraph under 'Fixture shape' documenting `expect_absent_edges` and stating that its cell reads 0.00 while the forbidden edge exists.

No Rust changes. No new fixture — this packet ships the mechanism; A5.4/A5.5/A5.6 ship the fixtures that use it.
packets.acceptance: `python3 bench/substrate-gap/run.py --no-log` still prints exactly 49 fixtures with 0 blind spots (no regression), AND a scratch fixture with `expect_absent_edges` naming an edge that demonstrably exists produces a `!<CATEGORY>` column reading 0.00 plus a `[absent] <fw>: 0/1 forbidden edges correctly absent` line on stdout; the same key with a nonexistent edge reads 1.00. Verified by running `python3 grade.py fixtures/xcut-graphql-graphql_calls` after temporarily adding `expect_absent_edges: [{"from":"getUser","to":"getUser","category":"GRAPHQL_CALLS"}]` (must read 0.00) and then `{"from":"nope","to":"nope",...}` (must read 1.00).

breaking.what_changes: Additive key.json field; fixtures without `expect_absent_edges` behave identically. results.jsonl gains new per_category keys but is append-only, so old records stay readable.

packets.risks: The rollup must be inserted BEFORE grade.py:119-120's recall computation or the new columns come back with `recall` unset and run.py's `f"{v['recall']:.2f}"` at run.py:63 raises TypeError inside the per-fixture try/except, silently dropping the fixture from the matrix.

packets.rationale: TypeScript is the only language where the receiver shape is EXCLUSIVELY ComplexReceiver: `this.api.fetchUser(1)` parses as a member_expression whose object is itself a member_expression, so extract_call_qualifier falls to the `_` arm (typescript:1165-1168) and emits `ComplexReceiver{receiver:"this.api"}`. packets.implementation:
Add `fn collect_field_types(body: TsNode, src: &[u8], class_id: NodeId, acc: &mut Acc)` next to collect_constructor_injects (:228). Two sources, both off the class body:

(1) Constructor parameter properties. Find the `method_definition` whose `name` is `constructor` (identical to :240-246), take its `parameters`, and for each `required_parameter`/`optional_parameter`: read `child_by_field_name("type")` -> the wrapping `type_annotation` -> its first named child (identical to :258-266); skip `predefined_type`; run `heritage_type_name` for the simple name. Then read `child_by_field_name("pattern")` for the field name (an `identifier`; skip destructuring patterns — if the node kind is not `identifier`, continue). Call `acc.nav.record_field_type(class_id, param_name, type_name)`. Do this for EVERY param, not only accessibility-modified ones: a plain `constructor(api: ApiService)` that assigns `this.api = api` is the same shape and over-recording a name that is never used as a receiver costs nothing.

(2) Typed class fields. Walk the body's named children for `public_field_definition` (tree-sitter-typescript's class property node); read `child_by_field_name("name")` for the field name and `child_by_field_name("type")` -> type_annotation -> first named child for the type; same predefined_type skip and `heritage_type_name` normalisation. Guard: if the grammar returns a different node kind on this tree-sitter version the loop simply finds nothing — verify with the fixture, and if `public_field_definition` does not appear, fall back to matching any body child that exposes both a `name` and a `type` field and is not a `method_definition`.

Wire it at :219, right after `collect_constructor_injects(...)`, so both Angular-decorated and plain classes are covered. No graph-crate change: A6.2a's pass already handles the ComplexReceiver shape via `receiver_field`.

No new marker — the packet's proof is A6.2a's `[recv]` line firing on a TypeScript-only fixture (nothing else in that repo can produce a receiver-typed binding).

packets.title: tsconfig `paths` aliases in TS/JS import resolution
packets.rationale: `resolve_ts_source` (engine:2082) returns None for any specifier that does not start with `.`, treating `@core/auth.service`, `@app/shared`, `~/lib/x` and `src/foo` as external packages. Every Angular CLI, Nx, Next.js and Vite project uses path aliases by default, so their entire intra-repo import graph is invisible — the same class of blindness the substrate-gap v1 map recorded as `ts-imports` IMPORTS 0.00 before Fix 3, just via a different door. Measured: a fixture with `baseUrl: "./src"` and `"@core/*": ["app/core/*"]` produces 6 nodes and FOUR edges, all DEFINES — IMPORTS 0/1, and tsconfig.json is not even read (`.json` is absent from detect_language, engine:756).
entry_points: engine/src/lib.rs:2084-2086 — `if !spec.starts_with('.') { return None; }` in resolve_ts_source: the exact line that drops every alias
engine/src/lib.rs:165 — `fn read_go_module_prefix(root: &Path) -> String`, the exact precedent for reading a manifest off the repo root outside the walker (tsconfig.json never reaches `files`)
engine/src/lib.rs:176-181 — `fn build_graphs_for_repo(files, repo, go_module_prefix, cache)`; gains a `ts_aliases: &TsAliases` parameter

engine/src/lib.rs:86 and :125 — the two call sites of build_graphs_for_repo (generate_one_inner and generate_many), each of which already has `root` in scope and already calls read_go_module_prefix on the line above

engine/src/lib.rs:440 — `repo_graph_graph::build_typescript(repo, ts_family, resolve_ts_source)`: the fn-pointer becomes a closure capturing the alias table (build_typescript is generic over `R: Fn(&str,&str)->Option<String>`, graph:107-113, so no signature change)
engine/src/lib.rs:2065-2073 — `path_to_qname`, which the alias mapping must produce output compatible with (`with_extension("")` then `/`->`::`)
graph/src/lib.rs:456-461 and :478-484 — resolve_imports_ts does a STRICT `module_by_qname` lookup with no fallback, so an alias that maps to a non-existent qname is a silent no-op, never a wrong edge
packets.implementation:
1) `struct TsAliases { base_url: String, entries: Vec<(String, String)> }` where each entry is (pattern, first-target), patterns sorted longest-literal-prefix first for deterministic matching.

2) `fn read_tsconfig_paths(root: &Path) -> TsAliases`, modelled on read_go_module_prefix (:165). Read `root/tsconfig.json` (then `tsconfig.base.json` as a second try — Nx's convention); strip `//` line comments and `/* */` blocks before parsing (tsconfig is JSONC and serde_json rejects comments); `serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>` (serde_json is already an engine dependency); pull `compilerOptions.baseUrl` (default ".") and each key/first-array-element of `compilerOptions.paths`. Never unwrap — every step is `.ok()`/`.and_then`, returning `TsAliases::default()` on any failure. Ignore `extends` chains in v1 and say so in the doc comment.

3) `fn resolve_ts_source_aliased(from_module: &str, specifier: &str, aliases: &TsAliases) -> Option<String>`: delegate to the existing `resolve_ts_source` for `.`-leading specifiers (unchanged path, zero regression risk); otherwise, for each (pattern, target) in order: if the pattern ends in `/*`, match the specifier's prefix and substitute the remainder into the target's `*`; else require an exact match. Join `base_url` + the substituted target, normalise `./`, strip a trailing `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.jsx`, then `path_to_qname`. Return the first hit; None if nothing matched.

4) Thread it: `let ts_aliases = read_tsconfig_paths(&root);` beside each `read_go_module_prefix(&root)` (engine:80 and :123), pass `&ts_aliases` into build_graphs_for_repo, and at :440 call `repo_graph_graph::build_typescript(repo, ts_family, |from, spec| resolve_ts_source_aliased(from, spec, ts_aliases))`. Leave the `_`-arm call at :432 on `resolve_relative_source` (dart/swift/c_cpp/solidity) untouched.

5) Marker in read_tsconfig_paths, on non-empty: `eprintln!("[tsconfig] {} path aliases (baseUrl={})", entries.len(), base_url);`

Explicit v1 limitations to put in the doc comment: only the FIRST entry of each `paths` array is used; no `extends` chain; no implicit `index.ts` resolution (which today's relative resolver also lacks, so behaviour stays consistent).
packets.acceptance: (1) `python3 bench/substrate-gap/grade.py fixtures/ts-tsconfig-paths` flips IMPORTS 0.00 -> 1.00 (baseline measured today: 6 nodes, 4 edges, all DEFINES, no IMPORTS edge at all). (2) The shipped `ts-imports` and `ts-imports-rel` fixtures MUST stay at 1.00 — relative resolution is delegated unchanged. (3) Unit tests in engine/src/lib.rs's test module: `resolve_ts_source_aliased("src::app::feature::page", "@core/auth.service", &aliases) == Some("src::app::core::auth.service".into())`; an unmatched bare specifier (`"@angular/core"`) returns None; a `.`-leading specifier returns exactly what `resolve_ts_source` returns. (4) A JSONC test: a tsconfig with `// comment` lines still parses. (5) stderr shows `[tsconfig] 2 path aliases (baseUrl=./src)`. (6) `cargo test --workspace` green.

breaking.what_changes: Additive IMPORTS edges (category 3) in TS/JS/Angular/React/Vue repos that use path aliases. Relative imports go down the identical code path as today. `build_graphs_for_repo` gains a parameter but it is a private fn in the engine crate — no pyo3 or CLI signature changes. A bogus alias cannot create a wrong edge: resolve_imports_ts (graph:459/:481) does a strict module_by_qname lookup and silently skips a miss.

packets.risks: (a) Monorepos put tsconfig.json per package, not at the repo root; v1 reads the root only, so an Nx workspace with per-app tsconfigs gets partial coverage. That is the same limitation as read_go_module_prefix (engine:164-175, root go.mod only) and the review already tracks it under §2/project_roots — say so in the doc comment rather than solving it here. (b) JSONC comment stripping must not corrupt a `//` inside a string literal (e.g. a URL in a comment-adjacent value); write a tiny state-machine stripper that tracks string context, or accept the risk and note it — tsconfig `paths` values never contain `//`. (c) Multi-entry `paths` arrays (a fallback chain) silently use the first entry; a repo relying on the second will just not bind, never mis-bind.

packets.title: resolve_file / resolve_frame prefer a path-suffix match over a bare basename
packets.rationale: `resolve_file` (graph:2451) and `resolve_frame` (graph:2430) compare only `basename(POSITION.file) == basename(query)`. In any monorepo or multi-service repo — the exact shape glia's cross-stack primitives exist for — `utils.py`, `index.ts`, `models.py`, `handler.go` and `Services.cs` appear in every sub-project, so a diff or stacktrace naming one file seeds nodes from all of them. Measured: on a repo with svc_a/utils.py and svc_b/utils.py, `PyGraph.resolve('svc_b/utils.py','diff',20)` returns 4 nodes — including svc_a::utils and svc_a::utils::a_helper, from a file the caller never named. This silently poisons `glia resolve`, `glia blast-radius` seeding, and repo-graph's find(diff) with cross-service noise, and it is a precision bug (wrong answers), not a coverage gap.

packets.title: SharedSchemaResolver sees types under a namespace PACKAGE
packets.rationale: SharedSchemaResolver indexes candidate schema types by walking `children_of` for MODULE nodes only (graph:1584-1590). In C# and PHP every type sits under a namespace PACKAGE node, not directly under the file MODULE — measured on the csharp-aspnet dump: `[DEFINES] 'Services'(PACKAGE) -> 'User'` and `[CONTAINS] 'Services'(MODULE) -> 'Services'(PACKAGE)`. So the resolver is structurally blind to C# and PHP, and a polyglot stack whose contract types are C# DTOs shares zero schema. Measured directly: two C# repos each declaring `OrderDto` under a namespace give SHARES_SCHEMA 0/1 across a generate_many boundary. The review flags this only in passing (as a reason to defer §6 message_contracts); it is the same PACKAGE-blindness class as A6.1 and costs ~50 LOC.

packets.title: TypeScript family: Angular `inject()` field form + NestJS/`@Inject()` constructor DI
packets.rationale: Two of the three dominant TS DI shapes are blind. (a) Angular 14+ `private api = inject(ApiService)` is now the officially recommended form and is the default in every standalone-component codebase; it produces nothing at all because visit_class's body loop (parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs:207-211) matches only `method_definition`, so `public_field_definition` is never visited — the TS parser emits no field nodes and reads no field initialisers. (b) A NestJS backend is 100% blind: DI_DECORATORS (:222) is `["Component","Injectable","Directive","Pipe"]`, so `@Controller('users') class UsersController { constructor(private users: UsersService) {} }` — every Nest controller and GraphQL resolver — fails has_di_decorator (:285) and emits zero INJECTS, even though ts_routes already mints the ROUTE nodes for those same controllers (parsers/code/extractors/src/ts_routes.rs:243-250). Fixing (b) is a two-element array edit; fixing (a) is the first time this parser reads a class field.

packets.area: A7 — dependency injection / INJECTS edges across languages

packets.title: Java: Lombok generated constructors, records, JSR-330/Dagger/Guice `@Inject`, and DI-wrapper generics
packets.rationale: Java DI is green only for the 2015-era shape. Three modern shapes are blind. (a) Lombok `@RequiredArgsConstructor` + `private final FooService foo;` — the dominant Spring Boot idiom since Boot 2 — has no `constructor_declaration` at all and no `@Autowired` on the field, so it misses both gates (parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:164 `is_bean` guards the ctor path, :609 `INJECT_ANNOTATIONS` guards the field path). (b) Dagger/Guice `@Inject` on a *constructor* in a class with no Spring stereotype emits nothing: `emit_field_inject` (:599) checks annotations only on `field_declaration`, and the constructor branch (:168-176) checks `is_bean` instead of the constructor's own modifiers. (c) `injectable_type_name` (:545) matches only `type_identifier` and `scoped_type_identifier` and returns None for every `generic_type`, so `Provider<PaymentGateway>`, `Lazy<Foo>`, `ObjectProvider<Bar>` and `Optional<Baz>` — the standard Dagger/Spring lazy-dependency wrappers — are dropped. Records (`record_declaration` has a `parameters` field, verified in tree-sitter-java 0.23.5 node-types) are also unreachable because the body loop at :166-185 only sees `constructor_declaration`.

packets.risks: Lombok inference is a semantic model of a code generator, not of the AST: a class with `@RequiredArgsConstructor(access = AccessLevel.PRIVATE)` plus a hand-written factory still gets INJECTS refs. That is the intended (generous) direction — an over-emitted ref only becomes an edge if the bare type resolves uniquely. The `static`/`final` modifier check must tokenize (`mods.split_ascii_whitespace().any(|t| t == "static")`), never substring-match. The `generic_type` unwrap must keep the `inner.len() != 1` guard or `Map<String, FooService>` starts minting edges. Kotlin files route to this same parser (engine/src/lib.rs:770 maps `"kt"` to `"java"`) and will misparse — out of scope, already covered by the review's Kotlin caveat item.

packets.title: C#: primary-constructor injection and `[FromServices]` parameter injection
packets.rationale: C# 12 primary constructors are now the default ASP.NET Core template shape (`public class UsersController(IUserService svc) : ControllerBase`) and produce zero INJECTS: the emitter is gated on `child.kind() == "constructor_declaration"` inside the class-body loop (parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:201-205), but a primary constructor's `parameter_list` is a named child of `class_declaration`/`record_declaration` itself — confirmed in the tree-sitter-c-sharp 0.23.5 node-types, whose `class_declaration` children are exactly [attribute_list, base_list, modifier, parameter_list, preproc_if_in_attribute_list, type_parameter_constraints_clause, type_parameter_list] and whose `fields` are only `body` and `name`. Worse, `visit_type_decl` returns early at :194-196 when there is no `body`, so a bodyless primary-ctor record is abandoned before anything is read. Separately `[FromServices]` per-action injection is invisible because `visit_method` (:316) never looks at `parameters` at all. `[FromServices]` also has the best liveness payoff in the whole area: the ref hangs off the METHOD, which IS already reached by the ROUTE -HANDLED_BY-> METHOD chain, so it flips services live with no A7.8 needed.

packets.title: Python: FastAPI `Depends()` dependency injection
packets.rationale: FastAPI is the single most common Python DI mechanism and it is completely invisible. `visit_function` calls `collect_calls_in` on the function BODY only (parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs:571), so `Depends(get_db)` sitting in a parameter default is never walked as a call; and `collect_type_refs` (:1228-1248) reads only the `type` field of `typed_parameter`/`typed_default_parameter`, never the `value` field that holds the `Depends(...)` call. Result: a handler and its dependency provider are two disconnected FUNCTION nodes, and `glia trace` / `blast_radius` on a FastAPI app stops dead at the handler. This is the one language where the fix also immediately fixes liveness with no engine change: `@app.get("/x")` already mints a ROUTE with a HANDLED_BY edge to the handler (check_route_decorator at :1640-1666 → emit_route at :1749-1768), ROUTE is an entrypoint kind (engine/src/lib.rs:1713), and both HANDLED_BY and INJECTS are carry edges — so ROUTE → handler → get_db becomes live end to end.
entry_points: parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs:571 — `collect_calls_in(body, src, func_id, None, repo, file_rel, acc);` proves only the body is walked; parameter defaults are untouched

In the `Annotated[T, Depends(f)]` spelling the pairing (handler → f) may ALREADY carry a USES edge from emit_type_idents (parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs:1259-1268, which walks every identifier in the annotation including the ones inside the Depends call); the new INJECTS edge is a second edge of a different category on that pairing, and graph/src/lib.rs:802 push_edge does not dedupe across categories. packets.title: PHP: Symfony/Laravel constructor injection (including promoted properties)
packets.rationale: PHP has no INJECTS emission of any kind, and the parser reads no parameters anywhere: `visit_class` (parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:133) walks the class body for `method_declaration` only (:164-170) and hands each to `visit_method` (:275), which never touches `parameters`. Symfony autowiring and Laravel's container both resolve constructor type-hints, and PHP 8 constructor property promotion (`public function __construct(private readonly UserRepository $users) {}`) makes the dependency list a single, unambiguous, fully typed node — `property_promotion_parameter` carries required `type` and `visibility` fields (verified in tree-sitter-php 0.24.2 node-types), which is a stronger DI signal than anything C# or Java offers. packets.title: Go: wire / fx / dig provider-set registration as INJECTS
packets.rationale: HONEST ASSESSMENT FIRST: Go's AST gives NO type-directed DI signal. There are no annotations, and the idiomatic `func NewUserHandler(svc *UserService) *UserHandler` constructor is syntactically indistinguishable from any other function — recognising it would require return-type-to-struct inference, which is A6's job and out of scope here. What IS unambiguous and AST-visible is explicit container registration: `wire.Build(NewA, NewB)`, `wire.NewSet(...)`, `fx.Provide(...)`, `fx.Invoke(...)`, `fx.Supply(...)`, `dig.Provide(...)`. Those argument identifiers are not calls, so `classify_call` (parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:632) ignores them entirely and `collect_calls_in` (:598-630) descends past them without emitting anything — the provider graph of every wire/fx service is currently invisible. Ranked MATRIX, not C: this yields injector→provider edges, not consumer→service edges, so it is a weaker signal than the other six packets. It is included because the brief asks and because it is the ONLY tractable Go DI shape.
entry_points: parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:598-630 — `fn collect_calls_in` already visits every `call_expression` and already calls two sibling detectors on each (`try_detect_go_endpoint` at :617, `try_detect_go_data_access` at :623); the new `try_detect_go_provider_set` is a third, added on the next line
parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:632-657 — `fn classify_call` shows that only the `function` field is inspected; the `arguments` of `wire.Build(...)` are never read, which is why this is blind

parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:377 — `fn visit_function` is where `from` (the enclosing FUNCTION node id) comes from; `collect_calls_in` is called with that id, so the INJECTS ref's `from` is the injector function, which is the semantically correct source
parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:1363 — the parser's only existing `acc.refs.push(UnresolvedRef { … })` (a HANDLED_BY route ref) is the idiom to copy
packets.acceptance: New fixture `bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/go-wire-di` cell `INJECTS` 0.00 → 1.00, baseline via `python3 run.py` first. Unit tests: `cargo test -p repo-graph-parser-go wire_build_emits_injects_refs_for_each_provider non_container_selector_call_emits_no_injects`. Grep: `python3 grade.py fixtures/go-wire-di 2>&1 | grep -o 'go-provider=[0-9]*'` prints `go-provider=2`. Regression: `fixtures/go-calls`, `go-imports`, `go-handled-by`, `go-accesses-data`, `xstack-go-http`, `xstack-ts-go-http` all stay 1.00.

breaking.what_changes: Additive; Go emits no INJECTS today. Semantic caveat to document in the fixture note: the `from` node is the injector FUNCTION and the `to` node is a provider FUNCTION, so these INJECTS edges read 'registers a provider', not 'consumes a service'. Anyone reasoning over INJECTS edge semantics across languages needs to know the Go ones are a different relation.

packets.risks: Gating on the bare selector base (`wire`/`fx`/`dig`) is a convention bet — a repo that imports `go.uber.org/fx` under a different alias is missed, and a local variable named `fx` with a `Provide` method would false-fire. Both fail safely (no edge / an unresolvable ref). Decide up front whether `collect_calls_in` gets an eighth parameter or `Acc` gets a `module_id` field, and prefer the Acc field (the TypeScript parser's documented precedent) — that choice is the only thing in this packet that could conflict with a concurrently-scheduled Go packet from another area.

packets.title: Scala: gated class-parameter injection, implicit/using parameter lists, and Macwire `wire[T]`
packets.rationale: HONEST ASSESSMENT FIRST: Scala's AST gives excellent type information — `class_parameter` carries a required `name` and a `type` field, and `parameter` likewise (verified in tree-sitter-scala 0.25.1 node-types) — but it gives NO reliable DI marker. Every case class, every value object and every DI-managed service share the same `class Foo(bar: Baz)` shape, so emitting unconditionally would flood the graph. Two markers are genuinely tractable: an `implicit`/`using` parameter list (which is literally the language's DI mechanism) and Macwire's `wire[T]`. Beyond that a name-suffix gate is the only option, exactly as for C# and PHP. Today the Scala parser reads no parameters at all — `visit_function` (parsers/code/scala/src/lib.rs:196) resolves only `name` and `body`, and `visit_type_def` (:94) emits heritage refs at :160 but never touches `class_parameters`. Ranked MATRIX: real but low-confidence, and Scala is a thin slice of the corpus.
entry_points: parsers/code/scala/src/lib.rs:94 — `fn visit_type_def`; the class node id and parent id are both in scope, and :160 shows the existing `acc.refs.push(UnresolvedRef { … })` heritage idiom to copy exactly
parsers/code/scala/src/lib.rs:196-231 — `fn visit_function` reads only `name` and `body`; the implicit/using parameter-list scan is added after the nav record
parsers/code/scala/src/lib.rs:169 — `fn visit_body_members` is where `lazy val x = wire[Foo]` would be reached for the Macwire shape
parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:225-248 — `fn is_di_class`'s suffix-gate structure is the template (Scala has no annotation the grammar exposes as a field)
packets.implementation:
All changes inside parsers/code/scala/src/lib.rs.

(1) Gate. `fn is_scala_di_class(name: &str, head_text: &str) -> bool`: true when `name` ends with one of `["Service", "Controller", "Repository", "Handler", "Manager", "Module", "Component", "Dao", "Client"]`, OR when `head_text` (the class declaration text up to the first `{`, or the whole node when there is none) contains `@Inject` (Play/Guice's `class Foo @Inject() (bar: Baz)` — the annotation sits between the name and the parameter list and the grammar does not surface it as a field, so a text check is the pragmatic route and must be documented as such), OR when the `class_parameters` text begins with `(implicit ` or `(using `.

(2) Class parameters. In `visit_type_def`, after the heritage refs at :160:

```rust
if let Some(params) = node.child_by_field_name("class_parameters")
    && is_scala_di_class(name, head_text)
{
    emit_param_injects(params, src, id, parent_id, acc);
}
```

`fn emit_param_injects(params, src, from, module_id, acc)` iterates `params.named_children()`, keeps `class_parameter` (and `parameter` for the function form), reads `child_by_field_name("type")`, and runs it through `scala_injectable_type_name`. Push `UnresolvedRef { from, from_module: module_id, qualifier: Bare(name), category: INJECTS }` + `di_stats::record(DiShape::ScalaCtor)`, deduped by a local HashSet.

(3) `fn scala_injectable_type_name(ty: TsNode, src: &[u8]) -> Option<String>`: accept `type_identifier` directly; for `generic_type` take the head child's text; for `stable_type_identifier` (`pkg.Foo`) take the trailing `.` segment; return None for every other kind (`function_type`, `tuple_type`, `infix_type`, `compound_type`, `wildcard` — all ambiguous). Reject the Scala value types `Int Long Short Byte Double Float Boolean Char String Unit Any AnyRef AnyVal Nothing Option Seq List Map Set Future` (Option/Future/Seq are wrappers, not beans; unlike Java there is no single canonical DI wrapper worth unwrapping in Scala, so keep it simple and reject).

(4) Implicit/using parameter lists on methods. In `visit_function` after the nav record at :224-225: if `node.child_by_field_name("parameters")` exists and its raw text (`text_of(params, src).trim_start()`) starts with `(implicit` or `(using`, call `emit_param_injects` with the FUNCTION id as `from`. The `implicit`/`using` keyword is an anonymous token inside `parameters` in tree-sitter-scala 0.25.1 (the node-types show `parameters` fields as `{}` with `parameter` among its children), so a text check on the parameter-list node is the correct and only route — document that in the comment.

(5) Macwire. In `visit_body_members` (:169), when a member's text matches `wire[` followed by an identifier and `]`, push an INJECTS ref from the enclosing type/module to that identifier. Implement as a small text scan over the member node's text (`wire[Foo]` is not a distinct grammar node) with the extracted name run through `scala_injectable_type_name`'s denylist. Record `DiShape::ScalaCtor`. Keep it to ~15 LOC; if it proves fiddly, drop it — the fixture does not depend on it.

Add `use repo_graph_code_domain::di_stats::{self, DiShape};`.

Two unit tests: `scala_service_class_params_emit_injects_refs`, `scala_case_class_emits_no_injects` (`case class Money(amount: Int, currency: Currency)` must emit nothing — no suffix match, no implicit list).
packets.acceptance: New fixture `bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/scala-di` cell `INJECTS` 0.00 → 1.00, baseline via `python3 run.py` first. Unit tests: `cargo test -p repo-graph-parser-scala scala_service_class_params_emit_injects_refs scala_case_class_emits_no_injects`. Grep: `python3 grade.py fixtures/scala-di 2>&1 | grep -o 'scala-ctor=[0-9]*'` prints `scala-ctor=1`. Regression: `fixtures/scala-calls`, `scala-imports`, `scala-inherits_from` stay 1.00.

breaking.what_changes: Additive; Scala emits no INJECTS today.

packets.risks: Lowest-confidence packet in the area, by design. The `@Inject` and `implicit`/`using` detection are text checks against node text rather than grammar fields, because tree-sitter-scala 0.25.1 exposes neither as a field — this must be written as a documented, deliberate exception, not slipped in. The suffix gate will both over- and under-fire on real Scala (ZIO/cats-effect layered apps name almost nothing `…Service`). Schedule this last; if it turns out noisy on a real repo, the honest outcome is to ship only the implicit/using and Macwire halves and drop the suffix gate. Do not spend effort on cake-pattern self-types — the grammar makes them tractable but the payoff does not justify the LOC.

packets.title: Liveness: entrypoint qname-twins and enclosing-type propagation, so INJECTS edges actually flip `live`
packets.rationale: The whole stated motivation for A7 — 'with INJECTS missing, liveness false-flags every @Injectable service as dead' — does not hold, and the language packets alone will not fix it. I verified two independent breaks. (1) In the TS family the entrypoint-kind node is an OVERLAY: parsers/code/extractors/src/angular.rs:76 maps `@Injectable(`→SERVICE and `@Component(`→COMPONENT, and those nodes are recorded with `parent=None` (code-domain/src/lib.rs:679 only writes children_of for Some), so they have no edges at all — `grade.py fixtures/angular-injects --dump` shows COMPONENT 'UsersComponent' and SERVICE 'UserService' in the 9 NODES and in none of the 8 EDGES. The INJECTS edge is CLASS→CLASS, and CLASS is not an entrypoint kind (engine/src/lib.rs:1708-1724). There is also no HANDLED_BY from any TS route extractor (grep for HANDLED_BY in parsers/code/extractors/{ts_routes,angular,react}.rs returns nothing), so the ROUTE path is closed too. (2) In Java/C# the chain ROUTE -HANDLED_BY-> METHOD dead-ends, because DEFINES is deliberately excluded from blast_carry_edges (graph/src/lib.rs:2166-2174) and nothing walks METHOD→enclosing CLASS. Hand-tracing fixtures/csharp-aspnet: entrypoints = the two ROUTE nodes, reachable = {ROUTEs, GetUser}; UsersController and IUserService are both dead. So today, and after every language packet above, INJECTS contributes exactly zero to the `live` flag. Two small, policy-consistent additions close both breaks.
entry_points: engine/src/lib.rs:1708-1724 — `fn is_entrypoint(kind, name)` accepts ROUTE/GRPC_SERVICE/WS_HANDLER/EVENT_HANDLER/CLI_COMMAND/COMPONENT plus main/test* FUNCTION|METHOD; the qname-twin seeding is added in the caller, not here

engine/src/lib.rs:1731-1756 — `pub fn entrypoint_reachable(merged)`: the seed loop at :1740-1747 and the BFS at :1748-1754 (`if e.from == node && carry.contains(&e.category) && live.insert(e.to)`) are the two places that change

engine/src/lib.rs:1727-1730 — the doc comment already states the policy this packet extends: 'Conservative (generous entrypoint set) to avoid false-dead flags — the failure mode the handoff warns about'

graph/src/lib.rs:2166-2192 — `pub fn blast_carry_edges()` deliberately excludes DEFINES/CONTAINS/IMPORTS; this packet does NOT change that list, it adds a separate containment step inside liveness only
parsers/code/extractors/src/angular.rs:76 — `("@Injectable(", node_kind::SERVICE)` is where the parentless overlay nodes originate
code-domain/src/lib.rs:679-682 — `if let Some(p) = parent { … }` is why a `parent=None` overlay node never enters children_of or parent_of
engine/src/lib.rs:1779 — `let live = entrypoint_reachable(merged);` inside blast_radius_by_qname is the single consumer
cli/src/main.rs:650 — `let live = if a.live { "●" } else { "⊘" };` is the only in-repo display consumer
packets.acceptance: Four engine unit tests above: `cargo test -p repo-graph-engine qname_twin_seeds_class_from_component_overlay method_liveness_propagates_to_owning_class unrelated_class_stays_dead defines_still_does_not_carry`. End-to-end proof, which grade.py cannot express (it grades nodes/edges only, never `live`): on a repo built from bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/angular-injects, `glia blast-radius <repo> users.component::UsersComponent --json` must show `"live": true` on the UserService hit AFTER this packet and `"live": false` before; record the before value first. Marker: the new `[live]` line prints `twins=1` on that fixture and `twins=0 owners=0` on a fixture with no overlay nodes and no methods (e.g. py-imports). `cargo test --workspace` stays green.

breaking.what_changes: The `live` field on `BlastAnswer` (engine/src/lib.rs:1700, surfaced as `live` in the pyo3 `blast_radius` rows and as the ●/⊘ glyph in the CLI) flips from false to true for two populations that are genuinely reachable but were being reported as dead: (a) every AST CLASS node that shares a qname with a framework overlay COMPONENT/SERVICE/DIRECTIVE/PIPE/GUARD node, plus everything downstream of it; (b) every CLASS/STRUCT/INTERFACE that owns a route-reachable METHOD, plus everything downstream. This also changes what `glia blast-radius --live-only` and `PyGraph.blast_radius(live_only=True)` return — strictly more rows. Direction is one-way (never true→false), and it is the direction the function's own doc comment at engine/src/lib.rs:1729 asks for ('Conservative (generous entrypoint set) to avoid false-dead flags'). Flagged loudly because it silently changes the value of an existing output field on every repo.
in_repo_consumers: cli/src/main.rs:650 — `let live = if a.live { "●" } else { "⊘" };` renders the flag; no code change needed, output changes
engine/src/lib.rs:1783 — `.filter(|h| !live_only || live.contains(&h.id))` in blast_radius_by_qname; no code change needed, result set grows

No test asserts liveness anywhere in the workspace — `grep -rn 'entrypoint_reachable\|is_entrypoint' --include='*.rs' .` returns hits only in engine/src/lib.rs, and no bench/substrate-gap key.json grades `live`. So there is nothing to update in the same commit; the four new unit tests are the first coverage this function has ever had.

packets.risks: The real risk is over-generosity: if enclosing-type propagation were combined with a downward walk it would mark whole files live and the flag would stop meaning anything. The `unrelated_class_stays_dead` test exists specifically to hold that line — do not add a MODULE level, and do not add DEFINES to blast_carry_edges. The qname-twin seeding assumes an overlay node and its AST twin genuinely share a qname; verified for Angular (`grade.py fixtures/angular-injects --dump` shows both COMPONENT 'UsersComponent' and CLASS 'UsersComponent' at qname `users.component::UsersComponent`), so confirm the same for react.rs and vue.rs overlays before relying on it there. An architecturally cleaner alternative — making the overlay extractors emit an edge to the AST node instead of a detached twin — is a much larger change across parsers/code/extractors/ and is deliberately NOT this packet; if that lands later, the twin seeding becomes redundant and can be removed. Also note this packet is independent of A6: it needs no type inference.

packets.title: code_domain::walk_gating — one shared gate for the engine walker and store::is_gmap_stale; gated dotnet bin/obj collapse; nested .git becomes a REGION anchor that is never descended into
packets.rationale: Measured on main today, not inferred. A synthetic .NET tree (`Api.csproj`, `Program.cs`, `obj/project.assets.json`, `obj/Debug/net8.0/Api.AssemblyInfo.cs`, `bin/Debug/Api.g.cs`) produces 17 nodes of which 6 are generated junk: MODULE `obj::Debug::net8.0::Api.AssemblyInfo`, CLASS `PhantomAssemblyInfo`, METHOD `GeneratedNoise`, MODULE `bin::Debug::Api.g`, CLASS `PhantomBinClass`, and a phantom PACKAGE `Shop::Api::Generated` — every one of them ranked and located by blast_radius/resolve as if it were authored C#. Zero REGION anchors are emitted for either dir. packets.title: Full gitignore semantics via the `ignore` crate MATCHER (nested files, negation, anchoring, globs) — never its walker
packets.rationale: Measured on main: a repo whose root `.gitignore` is `/build`, `dist-*`, `!dist-keep` produces exactly the wrong three outcomes. `src/build/builder.py` is COLLAPSED even though `/build` is anchored to the root (a second REGION node appears at `region:src/build`, and the two REGION nodes share the nav name `build` — the pick_primary collision class again). `dist-x/d.py` is PARSED because `load_gitignore_dirs` (engine/src/lib.rs:1024-1031) skips any line containing `*`, `?` or `[`. And nothing below the root is read at all, so a monorepo sub-project's own `.gitignore` is invisible. The current parser also keeps only the FINAL path component (`src/generated` -> `generated`), so any dir named `generated` anywhere in the tree is collapsed. This is the highest-precision-per-LOC item in the area and it is a matrix-provable one: the CALLS edge inside `src/build/builder.py` reads 0.00 today because neither endpoint node exists. On the brief's explicit question — YES, the `ignore` crate's WALKER conflicts with the region-anchor model and must not be used: `ignore::WalkBuilder` prunes ignored directories and yields only files, giving no hook to RECORD a collapsed directory as a REGION anchor (its `filter_entry` closure cannot distinguish "collapse and record" from "skip"); it defaults to `hidden(true)`, which would silently drop `.ai/` docs and `.github/`; it wants a real `.git` for `info/exclude` and global excludes, which bench fixtures do not have; and its parallel mode would destroy the `entries.sort_unstable_by_key(|e| e.file_name())` ordering at engine/src/lib.rs:1095 that the 2026-06-10 audit installed to make shard bytes reproducible. Only `ignore::gitignore::{Gitignore, GitignoreBuilder}` is used.

packets.implementation:
Add three public items to `graph/src/lib.rs`, placed directly after `MergedGraph::all_edges` (:847).

1. `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct CrossLink { pub from: String, pub to: String, pub mechanism: &'static str, pub channel: String, pub count: usize, pub confidence: Confidence, pub example_from_qname: String, pub example_to_qname: String }`. No serde derive (graph has no serde).

2. `pub fn channel_of(qname: &str, name: &str) -> String` — the identifying literal a link travels over. Match on qname prefix, in this order, returning the first hit:
   - `endpoint:` → `parse_endpoint_qname(qname)` → `format!("{method} {path}")`
   - `queue_producer:` / `queue_consumer:` → the suffix (the topic)
   - `grpc_client:` → the suffix (the service name)
   - `graphql_op:` / `graphql_resolver:` → the suffix
   - `ws_client:` → the suffix (the path)
   - `event_emit:` → the suffix (the event name)
   - `cli_invoke:` → the suffix (the tool name)
   - `data_entity:` → the suffix (`<flavor>:<name>`, already unique — DbResolver keys on the full qname, :1655)
   - `config:` / `cron:` / `infra:` / `route:` → the suffix
   - fallback → `name.to_string()`, and if `name` is empty, `qname.to_string()`.
   Use `strip_prefix` (not `split_once`) so a topic containing `:` survives intact.

3. `pub fn cross_links(merged: &MergedGraph, key_of: &dyn Fn(NodeId) -> Option<String>) -> (Vec<CrossLink>, usize)`.
   - Build `qname_of: HashMap<NodeId, (&str, &str)>` (qname, name) by iterating `merged.graphs` then `g.nav.qname_by_id` **via `g.nodes` order** (CODE_RULES §3: never iterate a HashMap; iterate `g.nodes`, look each id up in `nav`). This map is lookup-only.
   - Fold `merged.cross_edges` into `BTreeMap<(String, String, &'static str, String), Agg>` where the tuple is `(from_key, to_key, edge_category::name(e.category), channel)` and `Agg { count: usize, confidence: Confidence, example_from: String, example_to: String }`. `confidence` folds with `weakest`; the example qnames are set once on first insert (BTreeMap iteration order + first-wins = deterministic).
   - When `key_of(e.from)` or `key_of(e.to)` returns `None`, increment an `unplaced` counter and skip the edge.
   - **Symmetric mechanisms** (`SHARES_SCHEMA`, `SHARES_DATA_ENTITY`, `SHARES_CRON_SCHEDULE`, `SHARES_CONFIG`, `SHARES_INFRA_REF`, `SHARES_DEPENDENCY`) are emitted pairwise A→B and never B→A by the resolvers (graph/src/lib.rs:1612-1623 and the five clones), but the pair order depends on index order within a `HashMap` bucket. Normalise them: if the category is in a small `const SYMMETRIC: &[EdgeCategoryId]` slice, swap the two keys so `from_key <= to_key` before inserting. This is what makes the output stable across processes.
   - Return `(map.into_iter().map(...).collect(), unplaced)`. BTreeMap gives sorted, deterministic output — no post-sort needed.
   - Do NOT filter `from_key == to_key` here; that is presentation policy and belongs to the caller (engine).
   - No `unwrap()`/`panic!()`: every lookup is `Option`-handled, `channel_of` is total.

Add `#[cfg(test)] mod` cases next to the existing `parse_endpoint_qname_splits_method_and_path` test at :2721.

1. `channel_of_reads_every_resolver_prefix` — `channel_of("endpoint:GET:/users", "GET /users") == "GET /users"`; `channel_of("queue_producer:orders.v2", "kafka") == "orders.v2"`; `channel_of("grpc_client:Greeter", "Greeter") == "Greeter"`; `channel_of("UserDto", "UserDto") == "UserDto"` (fallback).

4. `cross_links_normalises_symmetric_and_counts_unplaced` — a SHARES_SCHEMA edge B→A with `key_of` returning `Some("a")`/`Some("b")` lands as `from == "a"`, `to == "b"`; a second edge whose `from` maps to `None` leaves `links.len() == 1` and `unplaced == 1`.

**engine/src/arch.rs (new, ≈270 LOC incl. doc comments and 5 unit tests).**

`pub fn node_file(n: &Node) -> Option<&str>` — three tiers, first hit wins:
  T1 `cell_type::POSITION` → `serde_json::from_str::<Value>(s)` → `v["file"].as_str()` (mirror :1637-1642 exactly, including accepting both `CellPayload::Json` and `CellPayload::Text`).
  T2 `cell_type::ENDPOINT_HIT` (6) or `cell_type::ROUTE_METHOD` (5), and only when the payload parses as a JSON object → `v["file"].as_str()`. A `Text("GET")` payload fails `from_str` cleanly and falls through; do NOT `unwrap`.
  Returns a borrowed `&str` tied to the node, so callers copy into the index.

`fn file_index(merged: &MergedGraph) -> (HashMap<NodeId, String>, usize)` — pass 1 runs `node_file` over `merged.graphs[..].nodes[..]` in declaration order. Pass 2 is the adjacency fallback for the remainder: iterate `merged.graphs[i].edges` in order, then `merged.cross_edges`, and for each edge where exactly one endpoint is resolved, push `(resolved_file.clone(), other_id.0)` into `cand: HashMap<NodeId, Vec<(String, u64)>>` for the unresolved endpoint. Restrict the fallback to `edge_category::{HANDLED_BY, CALLS, DEFINES, CONTAINS}` so a cross-service HTTP_CALLS edge can never drag a ROUTE into the client's directory (this is the bug that would otherwise make every Angular repo one service). Then for each unresolved node sort its candidate vec by `(file, id)` — `NodeId` has no `Ord` (core/src/lib.rs:20-23), sort on `id.0` — and take the first. One pass only; do not iterate to a fixpoint (a second hop would drag REGION/DOC nodes around). Everything still unresolved counts into `unlocated`.

`pub enum ServiceKeying { PerRepo, TopLevelDir, ProjectRoots(Vec<String>) }` with `pub fn name(&self) -> &'static str` → `"per_repo" | "top_level_dir" | "project_roots"`.

`pub fn default_keying(merged: &MergedGraph) -> ServiceKeying` — `PerRepo` when `merged.graphs.iter().map(|g| g.repo.0).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>().len() >= 2`, else `TopLevelDir`. **`ProjectRoots` is implemented but never selected in v1** (see A8 note below).

`fn service_of(file: &str, repo: u64, keying: &ServiceKeying, labels: &BTreeMap<u64,String>) -> String`:
  - `PerRepo` → `labels.get(&repo).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| format!("repo{repo}"))`.
  - `TopLevelDir` → `file.split('/').next()` when the file has a `/`, else `"(root)"`.
  - `ProjectRoots(roots)` → longest `root` such that `file == root || file.starts_with(&format!("{root}/"))`; ties broken by byte length then lexicographic; no match → fall through to the `TopLevelDir` rule. When `labels.len() >= 2`, prefix the result with `"{label}/"` for `TopLevelDir` and `ProjectRoots` so two merged repos that both have a `web/` stay distinct.

`#[derive(serde::Serialize)] pub struct ServiceSummary { pub id: String, pub repo: String, pub languages: Vec<&'static str>, pub files: usize, pub nodes: usize, pub routes: usize, pub endpoints: usize, pub cli_commands: usize, pub queue_consumers: usize, pub inbound: usize, pub outbound: usize }` — `languages` from `crate::ext_to_language` over the service's distinct files, sorted+deduped; `routes`/`endpoints`/`cli_commands`/`queue_consumers` counted from `g.nav.kind_by_id` against `node_kind::{ROUTE, ENDPOINT, CLI_COMMAND, QUEUE_CONSUMER}`.

`#[derive(serde::Serialize)] pub struct ServiceLink { pub from: String, pub to: String, pub mechanism: &'static str, pub channel: String, pub count: usize, pub confidence: &'static str, pub example_from_qname: String, pub example_to_qname: String }` — built 1:1 from `graph::CrossLink`, with `Confidence` mapped by a local `match` (`Strong|Medium|Weak` → `"strong"|"medium"|"weak"`, same table as py/src/lib.rs:82-86).

`#[derive(serde::Serialize)] pub struct ServiceMap { pub keying: &'static str, pub services: Vec<ServiceSummary>, pub links: Vec<ServiceLink>, pub self_links: usize, pub unlocated_nodes: usize }`.

`pub const FLOW_MECHANISMS: &[EdgeCategoryId]` = HTTP_CALLS, GRPC_CALLS, QUEUE_FLOWS, GRAPHQL_CALLS, WS_CONNECTS, EVENT_FLOWS, CLI_INVOKES — the directional ones. Everything else (the six `SHARES_*`) is a co-ownership signal, included in `links` but flagged by mechanism so the CLI can hide it by default.

`pub fn service_map(merged, repo_labels) -> ServiceMap` = `service_map_with(merged, repo_labels, &default_keying(merged))`.

`pub fn service_map_with(merged, repo_labels, keying) -> ServiceMap`: build `file_index`; build `svc_of: HashMap<NodeId, String>` by mapping each located node through `service_of` (the node's repo comes from `g.repo.0` of the graph it was found in); call `repo_graph_graph::cross_links(merged, &|id| svc_of.get(&id).cloned())`; drop links where `from == to`, counting them into `self_links`; accumulate per-service summaries into a `BTreeMap<String, ServiceSummary>` (sorted output, no HashMap iteration); set `inbound`/`outbound` from the surviving links; emit the marker with `eprintln!`. Return.

No `unwrap()`/`panic!()` anywhere: `serde_json::from_str` is `.ok()`-ed, every map read is `Option`-handled.

**How this meets A8's `project_roots` (explicit, per brief).** `ServiceKeying::ProjectRoots(Vec<String>)` ships in v1 fully implemented and unit-tested; only `default_keying` refuses to select it. When A8 lands its manifest-root pre-pass (package.json/go.mod/Cargo.toml/pyproject/pom/gradle/*.csproj/pubspec/mix.exs) and surfaces the repo-relative root dirs on `GenerateResult`, the switch is exactly three edits: (a) thread `project_roots` into `default_keying`, (b) return `ProjectRoots(roots)` when any repo has ≥2 roots, (c) pass the roots through `service_map`. `cross_links`, `ServiceMap`, `ServiceSummary`, the pyo3 method and the CLI renderer are all untouched because they never see a key's provenance — they see a `String` id and a `keying` name. Two consequences to plan for now: the service **id values change** for any monorepo whose roots are deeper than one segment (`apps/web` replaces `apps`), so `ServiceMap.keying` is serialised precisely so a consumer can tell which rule produced the ids; and the `TopLevelDir` fallback stays as the per-file default inside `ProjectRoots` so a file under no manifest root is still placed rather than dropped.

packets.rationale: A repo's own openapi.yaml / swagger.yaml / Swashbuckle-generated spec is read by the walker today (is_bypass_path admits every .yml|.yaml, engine:1182-1188) and then handed to exactly three extractors — cron, config, iac (engine:205-236) — none of which knows what `paths:` means. The declared API surface of the service is therefore invisible: nothing in the graph says GET /users is specified, so `docs-for` on a route returns nothing, no drift between spec and implementation is visible, and SDD slice 1b has no substrate. This is the node half; A10.2 is the edge half.

packets.implementation:
NEW parsers/code/extractors/src/contracts.rs. Public surface:
```rust
pub struct ContractNodes { pub nodes: Vec<Node>, pub edges: Vec<Edge>, pub nav: CodeNav }
pub struct ContractCounts { pub files: usize, pub openapi: usize, pub asyncapi: usize, pub pact: usize }
pub fn extract_yaml_contracts(source: &str, path: &str, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId) -> ContractNodes
```
`extract_yaml_contracts` sniffs then dispatches; in this packet only the OpenAPI arm exists (A10.3 adds asyncapi). Sniff = scan the first 64 lines for a line at indent 0 starting `openapi:` or `swagger:`; miss → return empty ContractNodes (this is the fast path every other .yaml in the repo takes, so keep it allocation-free).

Scanner (`fn scan_openapi(source) -> Vec<Op>` where `Op { method: String, path: String, raw_path: String, operation_id: Option<String>, line: u32 }`), line-based, no yaml crate:
1. base prefix: if a line at indent 0 is `servers:`, take the first `- url: <v>` beneath it; if a line at indent 0 is `basePath: <v>` (Swagger 2) take that. Strip quotes. If `<v>` contains `://`, keep only the path component (find the third `/` after the scheme's `//`; none → empty). If it contains `{` (templated server) → base = "". Trim a trailing `/`.
2. find the line at indent 0 equal to `paths:`. Record the indent of its first non-blank child as I1. Walk forward: a non-blank line at indent 0 ends the block. A line at indent I1 whose key (text before the first `:`) starts with `/` → current path (strip quotes). A line at indent > I1 whose key is in `["get","put","post","delete","patch","head","options","trace"]` (case-insensitive) → open an operation at that line (indent I2). While inside (indent > I2), `operationId: <v>` → op id. `parameters:`/`$ref:` keys are ignored by construction because the method allowlist gates emission.
3. Cap at 2000 ops per file; no unwrap/panic anywhere — every `split_once`/`strip_prefix` is a `let ... else { continue }`.

Emission, per op: `full = join(base, path)` collapsing `//` to `/` and guaranteeing a leading `/`; `qname = format!("contract::{stem}::{METHOD}:{full}")` where `stem` is the file stem (`openapi`); `name = format!("{METHOD} {full}")`. Node kind is **node_kind::DOC_SECTION (42, existing)** — deliberately NOT a new kind: it makes `governing_docs`/`glia docs-for` (engine:1939-1964) return contract ops for free, engram-export already maps DOC_SECTION → Content::Proposition (engram-export/src/lib.rs:535-541), and pyo3 decodes it today. Cells, in this order (match build_docs_graph:1497-1501):
  CODE  Text("{METHOD} {full}" + operation_id.map(|i| format!(" — {i}")).unwrap_or_default())
  POSITION Json({"file":"<path>","start_line":<op line, 0-indexed>,"end_line":<op line>})  // CODE_RULES §4 shape; 0-indexed per build_docs_graph
  ORIGIN Json({"provenance":"contract","source":"openapi","method":"GET","path":"<full>","raw_path":"<path>","operation_id":"<id or omitted>"})
The ORIGIN cell is the discriminator every downstream pass keys on (A10.2/A10.3 read `provenance=="contract"`), and `tag_synthetic_provenance` (engine:650-697) skips any node that already has an ORIGIN cell, so nothing overwrites it. `nav.record(id, &name, &qname, node_kind::DOC_SECTION, Some(module_id))`. Local `esc()` helper (`\\` then `\"`) for every JSON string, copied from build_docs_graph:1412-1414. `edges` stays empty (the module CONTAINS relation is carried by the nav parent, exactly as queues/graphql/grpc do).

Engine wiring, inside the existing yaml branch: add `let contract_out = repo_graph_code_extractors::contracts::extract_yaml_contracts(source, path, module_id, repo);`, add `|| !contract_out.nodes.is_empty()` to the stash condition at 231-234, and append `contract_out.nodes` / `.edges` / `.nav` to the three vec! lists. Declare `let mut contracts = ContractCounts::default();` next to `reused`/`reparsed` (engine:187-189) and bump `contracts.files += 1; contracts.openapi += contract_out.nodes.len();` when non-empty — declare ALL FOUR counter fields now so A10.3/A10.8 only increment and never rewrite the marker string. After the file loop, next to the `[incremental]` eprintln (engine:396-399): `if contracts.openapi + contracts.asyncapi + contracts.pact > 0 { eprintln!("[contract] files={} ops={} (openapi={} asyncapi={} pact={})", ...); }`.

Unit tests in contracts.rs `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (same convention as grpc.rs:158+): (a) non-OpenAPI yaml (a k8s Deployment) yields zero nodes; (b) `servers: - url: /api/v1` + `paths: /users: get:` yields qname `contract::spec::GET:/api/v1/users` with raw_path `/users`; (c) an absolute server url `https://api.example.com/v1` folds to base `/v1`; (d) a templated server `https://{host}/v1` folds to base ""; (e) `parameters:` at path-item level emits nothing.

packets.title: MESSAGE_TYPE node kind + protobuf message/enum declarations with POSITION
packets.rationale: A .proto is the shared contract between every service that speaks it, but glia keeps only the service name (grpc.rs:53-77). The `message User {}` block — the thing the generated Java/Go/Python class is derived from — is invisible, so a generated `User` class in two repos looks like two unrelated CLASSes and is_schema_type (graph:1887-1897) will not pair them either (it needs a Schema/DTO/Request-style name hint). packets.implementation:
Registry first (code-domain/src/lib.rs): MESSAGE_TYPE = NodeKindId(45) with a doc comment stating the qname convention `message:<flavor>:<name>` (flavor = proto | avro | jsonschema), mirroring DATA_ENTITY's flavor scheme at code-domain:76-83, plus its ALL entry. No other registry touches.

NEW parsers/code/extractors/src/schemas.rs (deliberately NOT grpc.rs — Batch A rank 6 owns the proto/service path and moves it to stash_synthetic_parse; keeping message extraction in a separate module makes the two land without conflict):
```rust
pub struct SchemaNodes { pub nodes: Vec<Node>, pub nav: CodeNav }
pub fn extract_proto_messages(source: &str, path: &str, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId) -> SchemaNodes
```
Line scanner: track `package <pkg>;` at indent 0 (strip the trailing `;`). Track brace depth. A line whose trimmed form starts with `message ` or `enum ` and contains `{` opens a declaration; its name is the token between the keyword and `{`. Maintain a stack of enclosing message names so a nested message emits `Parent.Child`. Ignore `map<..>` fields and `oneof` blocks (they contain no `message` keyword at line start). Skip anything inside a `//` comment line. Dedupe on the qualified name.
qname = `message:proto:{pkg}.{Name}` when a package exists, else `message:proto:{Name}`. name = the bare `Name` (so grade.py's lenient name match and cross-language reasoning both work). Cells: POSITION Json({"file":path,"start_line":<decl line 0-indexed>,"end_line":<matching close-brace line>}) — this is the first POSITION cell any extractor emits, so `locate_node` (engine:1969+) returns a real file/line for these nodes; and ORIGIN Json({"provenance":"contract","source":"proto","package":"<pkg>"}), which keeps tag_synthetic_provenance (engine:650-697) from re-tagging them. `nav.record(id, name, qname, node_kind::MESSAGE_TYPE, Some(module_id))`.

Engine: inside the existing `if lang == "proto"` branch, after `let svc_nodes = ...`, add `let msgs = repo_graph_code_extractors::schemas::extract_proto_messages(source, path, module_id, repo);` and build the FileParse as `nodes: svc_nodes.nodes.into_iter().chain(msgs.nodes).collect()` with `merge_nav`'d navs (merge_nav is already in scope at engine:2060). Counters `proto_files`/`proto_messages` + marker next to [incremental].

Unit tests in schemas.rs: (a) the exact bytes of fixtures/xcut-grpc-grpc_calls/server/user.proto yield MESSAGE_TYPEs `message:proto:user.GetUserRequest` and `message:proto:user.User`; (b) a nested `message Outer { message Inner {} }` yields `Outer` and `Outer.Inner`; (c) `enum Status {}` yields a MESSAGE_TYPE; (d) a commented-out `// message Ghost {` yields nothing.

packets.rationale: tRPC is the default RPC layer for Next.js/T3 and it is not merely missing — it is actively mis-read. `useQuery(` is a GraphQL operation pattern (graphql.rs:9-19), and a tRPC line has no `gql\`` tag, so extract_gql_operation_name returns None and graphql.rs:79 mints `graphql_op:useQuery`, which names_match_graphql then pairs to any `Query` resolver by substring. Registry: RPC_PROCEDURE = NodeKindId(46) (qname `rpc:<router>.<procedure>`), RPC_CALL = NodeKindId(47) (qname `rpc_call:<router>.<procedure>`), both with ALL entries. IDs 45 is MESSAGE_TYPE (A10.5) — if A10.5 has not landed, still use 46/47 and leave 45 reserved, so the two packets never collide on an id.

NEW parsers/code/extractors/src/trpc.rs:
```rust
pub struct TrpcNodes { pub nodes: Vec<Node>, pub nav: CodeNav }
pub fn extract_trpc_procedure_nodes(source: &str, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId) -> TrpcNodes
pub fn extract_trpc_call_nodes(source: &str, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId) -> TrpcNodes
pub fn is_trpc_client_line(line: &str) -> bool   // used by graphql.rs
```
Procedures. Gate the whole scan on the file containing one of `createTRPCRouter`, `t.router(`, `= router({`, `initTRPC` — otherwise return empty (the cheap gate every extractor in this crate uses). Then, line-based:
1. A line matching `<ident> = createTRPCRouter({` | `<ident> = router({` | `<ident> = t.router({` (after an optional `export `/`const `/`let `) opens a router. Namespace = ident with a trailing `Router` stripped and the first char lowercased; `appRouter`/`rootRouter`/`_app` → empty namespace. Track brace depth from that line to know where the router literal ends.
2. Inside, a line whose trimmed form matches `<key>:` → remember the pending key and its line; if that line, or any of the next 6 lines within the router, contains `.query(`, `.mutation(` or `.subscription(`, emit a procedure. This look-ahead is what handles the ubiquitous multi-line `publicProcedure.input(z.object({...})).query(...)` chain.
3. A line matching `<key>: <ident>Router,?` inside a router is a sub-router mount: if `<ident>Router` is defined in the SAME file, re-key its procedures under `<parent-ns>.<key>`. Cross-file mounts fall back to the defining const's own namespace (the T3 convention makes these agree); document the limitation in the module doc comment.
qname `rpc:<ns>.<proc>` (or `rpc:<proc>` with no namespace), name `<ns>.<proc>`, kind RPC_PROCEDURE, Confidence::Strong, cells: POSITION Json({file omitted — the extractor has no path; use the key line as start/end and let the engine's module POSITION carry the file}) — simpler and consistent with every other extractor: emit NO POSITION here and leave locate fallback to Batch A rank 3. (Decision: no POSITION in this packet; A10.5's POSITION work is on nodes whose extractor already receives `path`.)
Client calls. Scan for a receiver root in `["trpc", "api", "client"]` followed by `.` then 1-3 dotted identifier segments then one of `.useQuery(`, `.useMutation(`, `.useSuspenseQuery(`, `.useInfiniteQuery(`, `.query(`, `.mutate(`. The dotted middle is the procedure path. Reject when the segment immediately before the hook is `useUtils`/`useContext`, and reject `.invalidate(`/`.setData(` (cache ops, not calls). qname `rpc_call:<path>`, name `<path>`, kind RPC_CALL, Confidence::Medium (the receiver root is a convention, not a proof). Dedupe per file with a HashSet, push in encounter order.

graphql.rs precision guard: in extract_graphql_operation_nodes' pattern loop (graphql.rs:74-92), skip the line when `crate::trpc::is_trpc_client_line(trimmed)` — i.e. the line matches the client shape above. `is_trpc_client_line` requires BOTH a known receiver root with ≥2 dotted segments AND one of the hook suffixes, so `useQuery(GET_USERS)` (the existing unit test at graphql.rs:303-307) and `useQuery(GET_USER, { variables })` (fixtures/xcut-graphql-graphql_calls/client/query.ts:13) are untouched — both were checked.

Engine: inside the existing TS-family gate (engine:908-915, the one guarding ts_routes), add `run!(trpc::extract_trpc_procedure_nodes(source, module_id, repo));` and `run!(trpc::extract_trpc_call_nodes(source, module_id, repo));`, plus `trpc` to the `use repo_graph_code_extractors::{...}` list at engine:868-871. Counters + marker.

Unit tests in trpc.rs: (a) a T3 `export const userRouter = createTRPCRouter({ list: publicProcedure.query(...), byId: publicProcedure.input(z.object({id: z.string()})).query(...) })` yields `rpc:user.list` and `rpc:user.byId`; (b) `appRouter = createTRPCRouter({ user: userRouter })` in the same file re-keys nothing (namespace already `user`); (c) `api.user.list.useQuery()` yields `rpc_call:user.list`; (d) `utils.user.list.invalidate()` yields nothing; (e) is_trpc_client_line is false for `const { data } = useQuery(GET_USERS);`. Plus a regression test in graphql.rs asserting that `trpc.user.list.useQuery()` no longer emits any GRAPHQL_OPERATION while `useQuery(GET_USERS)` still does.

packets.implementation:
New file parsers/code/extractors/src/constants.rs. No new crate dependency (extractors already has serde/serde_json; none is needed — this is a line scanner in the same style as config.rs and queues.rs).

Public API:
  #[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
  pub struct ConstTable { by_key: std::collections::BTreeMap<String,String>, files: usize, conflicts: usize }
  impl ConstTable {
    pub fn scan_file(source: &str, lang: &str) -> Self
    pub fn merge_from(&mut self, other: &ConstTable)   // FIRST wins; bump self.conflicts on a differing value for an existing key
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str>
    pub fn resolve_expr(&self, expr: &str) -> Option<&str>
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize; pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool
    pub fn files(&self) -> usize; pub fn conflicts(&self) -> usize
  }
  pub fn fold_interpolations(raw: &str, table: &ConstTable) -> Option<String>

BTreeMap (not HashMap) and first-wins over the already-sorted `files` vec is what makes the table deterministic across processes — same reason walk_dir sorts at engine:1096 and parses_by_lang is sorted at engine:405.

scan_file is line-oriented and language-gated only loosely (each form is distinctive enough to run everywhere, the way config.rs:55-67 runs every idiom). Recognised forms, each capturing NAME -> the single-quoted/double-quoted/backtick literal that follows `=`:
  1. `[export ][pub ]const|let|var NAME = "lit"` — JS/TS/Go/Rust-ish
  2. column-0 `NAME = "lit"` where NAME matches ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$ — Python/Ruby module constant
  3. `NAME := "lit"` — Go short declaration
  4. `const NAME: &str = "lit"` / `static NAME: &str = "lit"` — Rust
  5. `... String NAME = "lit";` / `... const string NAME = "lit";` — Java/C# (require at least one preceding type-ish token on the line)
  6. `define('NAME', 'lit')` — PHP
  7. `@name "lit"` at line start — Elixir module attribute
  8. object-literal members: once a line matches `const OBJ = {` (or `OBJ: {`), every following `key: 'lit',` line until the matching close brace at the same indent registers BOTH `OBJ.key` and `key`. This is the environment.ts shape and the single highest-value form.
Reject any value longer than 512 bytes, containing a newline, or empty. Reject any NAME longer than 128 bytes or not matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*.

resolve_expr(expr) normalises then looks up: trim; strip a leading `this.`, `self.`, `@`, `$`; strip a trailing `()`; replace `::` and `->` with `.`; then (a) exact lookup of the full dotted key, (b) lookup of the last dot segment, (c) None. So `this.baseUrl`, `environment.apiUrl`, `Config.API_URL` and bare `TOPIC` all resolve through one path.

fold_interpolations(raw, table) walks `raw` for `${` ... `}` spans. For each span it calls resolve_expr on the inner text; a hit is substituted inline, a miss is rewritten to the literal marker `${…}` so downstream normalise_http_path (graph/src/lib.rs:1290-1303) still collapses it to `{}`. Returns Some(folded) only if at least one span resolved; None otherwise. Mixed cases work: `${environment.apiUrl}/users/${id}` -> `http://users-service:8080/users/${…}`.

Engine side, in build_graphs_for_repo immediately before the file loop (engine:198):
  let mut const_table = ConstTable::default();
  for (path, source) in files { if let Some(lang) = detect_language(path) { const_table.merge_from(&ConstTable::scan_file(source, lang)); } }
Then add `consts: &ConstTable` to apply_cross_cutting_extractors (engine:860) and pass `&const_table` at engine:363. No extractor consumes it in this packet — A2 adds `consts` to the two queues:: calls at engine:890-891, A11.2 consumes it in the fold pass. Nothing about node identity changes here.

Marker, printed once per repo build right after the file loop (beside the `[incremental]` marker at engine:385), only when len()>0:
  eprintln!("[const] repo table: {} bindings from {} files ({} conflicts)", n, f, c);

packets.implementation:
Three pieces.

(a) TypeScript parser — preserve, do not change identity. classify_template keeps emitting `${…}` into the path it returns (so the qname at :1224 is byte-identical to today) but additionally builds raw_path by pushing the substitution's inner source text verbatim between `${` and `}`. classify_path_arg returns raw_path = Some(s) for the template arm and None for the plain-string arm (raw == path, nothing to fold). push_endpoint (:981) carries it onto EndpointCandidate; resolve_intra_file (:1217-1249) passes it into endpoint_hit_cell so the ENDPOINT_HIT JSON gains `"raw_path":"${environment.apiUrl}/users"`. Adding a JSON field is safe: no in-repo consumer deserialises ENDPOINT_HIT into a typed struct — the only reader, endpoint_payloads at typescript/src/lib.rs:1655-1667, goes through serde_json::Value.

(b) code-domain — `pub fn url_split(raw: &str) -> (Option<String>, Option<String>)`. Find `://`; if present take the segment up to the next `/` as the authority (host[:port], strip any `user@` prefix) and the remainder from that `/` as the path (or `/` if none). If absent, authority is None and path is Some(raw) when raw starts with `/`, else None. Drop `?`/`#` and everything after, exactly as url_to_path does today. Then `pub fn url_to_path(raw) -> Option<String> { url_split(raw).1 }` — identical behaviour for every existing caller, which is why this is not a breaking change to go/java/swift/python.

(c) New engine/src/endpoint_fold.rs, roughly 110 LOC:
  pub fn fold_endpoint_paths(fp: &mut FileParse, consts: &ConstTable, repo: RepoId) -> (usize, usize)
For each node whose nav kind is node_kind::ENDPOINT:
  1. Read its ENDPOINT_HIT cell (cell_type::ENDPOINT_HIT, CellPayload::Json). Take `raw_path` if the field is present, else the path half of the node's qname (parsed the same way graph/src/lib.rs:1249-1252 parse_endpoint_qname does: strip `endpoint:`, split_once(':')).
  2. candidate = fold_interpolations(raw, consts).unwrap_or(raw.to_string()).
  3. let (host, path) = url_split(&candidate); if path is None, skip (leave the node untouched).
  4. If path == the current qname path AND host is None, skip — zero-change guarantee for every endpoint that is already relative and unfoldable. This is what keeps ts-http-fetch, react-http_calls, vue-http-calls, xstack-go-http, py-http, swift-http, java-spring-http and angular-http-calls byte-identical.
  5. Otherwise re-mint: new_id = NodeId::from_parts(GRAPH_TYPE, repo, node_kind::ENDPOINT, &format!("endpoint:{method}:{path}")). Rewrite fp.nodes[i].id; rewrite every fp.edges entry whose from/to == old_id; rewrite fp.nav's five maps via a local `fn rewrite_node_id(nav: &mut CodeNav, old: NodeId, new: NodeId)` that moves name_by_id/qname_by_id/kind_by_id entries, re-points parent_of, and patches children_of vectors. Set the nav name to `format!("{method} {path}")` and the qname to the new qname, matching the convention at code-domain/src/lib.rs:817.
  6. Rewrite the cell JSON: set `path` to the new path, add `"host"` when Some, add `"folded_from"` with the pre-fold raw. Build this with serde_json (engine already depends on it) by round-tripping through serde_json::Value so unknown fields survive.
  7. If two endpoints in one file fold to the same id, the duplicate is harmless — merge_parses (graph/src/lib.rs:179-186) stacks cells on an existing NodeId.
Return (folded_count, host_count).

Wiring in engine/src/lib.rs: hoist the fold out of the catch_unwind block so BOTH arms hit it. Concretely, after the cache-hit arm's `let Some(fp) = cached_fp` binding (engine:346) and after the successful parse arm (engine:369), call `let (f,h) = endpoint_fold::fold_endpoint_paths(&mut fp, &const_table, repo); folded += f; hosts += h;` before pushing into parses_by_lang. Do NOT feed the folded fp back into `c.put` — cache the pre-fold parse so the cache stays a pure parser cache (its doc comment at engine/src/cache.rs:1-8 says exactly that) and the fold re-applies on every build. `add mod endpoint_fold;` next to `mod cache;`.

Marker printed once per repo build next to `[incremental]` (engine:385), only when folded+hosts > 0:

config.rs. Change the four source-side scanners to return Vec<(String, Option<String>)>; the seven code-side scanners (scan_python_env at :165 through scan_php_env at :245) keep returning Vec<String> and are mapped to (name, None) at the three call sites (:59-65, :76, :86, :96-98). build_nodes takes Vec<(String, Option<String>)>; the dedupe `seen` set stays keyed on name only so the existing one-node-per-name invariant holds. When side is Side::Define and the value is Some(v) and v is non-empty and <= 512 bytes and contains no newline, push onto the node:
  Cell { kind: cell_type::ENV, payload: CellPayload::Json(format!(r#"{{"name":"{}","value":"{}"}}"#, esc(name), esc(v))) }

packets.title: Service-alias index + host-based narrowing of HTTP_CALLS targets in HttpStackResolver
packets.rationale: This is the join itself. Once A11.2 makes `${environment.apiUrl}/users` pair at all, it pairs with EVERY repo that serves /users — I verified the collision setup directly: three dirs (web, users, orders) where both Go services register `r.Get("/users", ...)` produce two distinct `route:/users` nodes (distinct because RepoId is in NodeId::from_parts) and two HANDLED_BY edges. Nothing in HttpStackResolver (graph/src/lib.rs:1131-1157) or lookup_route_with_prefix_strip (graph/src/lib.rs:1309-1333) knows which service the client meant, so it emits an edge to both. The host `users-service` is the disambiguator, and after A11.3 the aliases that identify a service repo are in the graph as infra:service / infra:deployment / infra:image resources.
entry_points: graph/src/lib.rs:1131-1157 — `impl CrossGraphResolver for HttpStackResolver::resolve`. Build the alias index once before the loop; insert exactly ONE new line after `let targets = lookup_route_with_prefix_strip(&index, &method, &norm);` at :1151 to narrow before the emit loop at :1152.
graph/src/lib.rs:1160-1164 — `struct RouteTarget { route_id, confidence }`; add `repo: RepoId`. It is constructed in exactly one place, build_route_index at :1181-1184.

graph/src/lib.rs:1255-1263 — `fn extract_method_field(json, ) -> Option<&str>`; generalise to `fn extract_json_str_field(json: &str, key: &str) -> Option<&str>` and have extract_method_field delegate. The graph crate has NO serde_json (graph/Cargo.toml) and the comment at :1243 says that is deliberate, so this hand-rolled scanner is the only sanctioned way to read the host off the ENDPOINT_HIT cell.
graph/src/lib.rs:1792 — `pub struct IacResolver`; its index-building loop (:1795-1810) is the exact pattern for collecting INFRA_RESOURCE qnames per repo — copy its shape, do not extend it.
graph/src/lib.rs:1307 — `const API_PREFIXES`; the sibling place for the new `const SERVICE_SUFFIXES: &[&str] = &["-service","-svc","-api","-server","_service","_svc"];`.
packets.implementation:
All of this lives in graph/src/lib.rs next to HttpStackResolver; no new crate, no new dependency.

1. `fn build_service_alias_index(graphs: &[RepoGraph]) -> HashMap<String, HashSet<RepoId>>`. For every node whose kind is node_kind::INFRA_RESOURCE, read its qname; accept `infra:service:<n>`, `infra:deployment:<n>`, `infra:statefulset:<n>` and `infra:image:<n>` (the kinds iac.rs mints, documented at iac.rs:11-21). Skip `infra:image:image`, the degenerate value dockerfile_image_name (iac.rs:148-166) produces for a root-level Dockerfile. Insert `normalise_alias(n) -> {g.repo}`. A name that appears in several repos maps to several RepoIds; that is a genuine ambiguity and the narrowing then no-ops.

2. `fn normalise_alias(s: &str) -> String`: lowercase; replace `_` with `-`; strip one trailing SERVICE_SUFFIXES entry if present; strip a `.`-qualified k8s DNS tail (`users-service.default.svc.cluster.local` -> `users-service` -> `users`). Applied identically to both sides so `users-service` (compose) and `users-svc` (host) meet at `users`.

3. `fn endpoint_host(cells: &[Cell]) -> Option<String>`: find the cell_type::ENDPOINT_HIT cell, take its Json payload, `extract_json_str_field(json, "host")`, then drop an `:<port>` suffix. Returns None for every endpoint whose parser has not recorded a host (all of them before A11.2 / A11.5) — that is the safety valve.

4. `fn narrow_by_host<'a>(alias_index, host: Option<&str>, targets: &'a [RouteTarget], out: &mut Vec<RouteTarget>) -> bool`. If host is None -> copy all targets, return false. Look up normalise_alias(host); if absent from the index -> copy all, return false. Let `owners` be the RepoId set. Let `kept` be the targets whose `repo` is in `owners`. If kept is EMPTY -> copy all, return false (never lose an edge because our map is incomplete). Otherwise copy kept, return true. The invariant is: narrowing only ever fires when it can positively identify at least one better target, so every fixture whose service is unknown is bit-identical to today.

5. In HttpStackResolver::resolve: build the alias index once before the `for g in &merged.graphs` loop (:1134); inside, after computing `targets` at :1151, run narrow_by_host into a reusable Vec and iterate that instead; count how many times it returned true.

6. build_route_index (:1174-1191) and index_route_node (:1206-1240) thread `g.repo` into RouteTarget. index_route_node already takes the target by value, so add the field at the construction site :1181 and pass it through.

7. Marker, printed at the end of HttpStackResolver::resolve when narrowed > 0 (eprintln needs no dependency; graph has no marker today so this establishes the pattern):
  eprintln!("[http-host] narrowed {narrowed} endpoint pairings by service host ({} aliases)", alias_index.len());

Scope note — MONOREPO IS EXPLICITLY OUT. I verified that two services in ONE repo serving the same path collapse to a single `route:/users` node with two HANDLED_BY edges, so repo-keyed narrowing has nothing to choose between. Closing the monorepo case requires ROUTE qnames to carry an owner segment, which is a breaking route-identity change belonging to the route/A3 workstream. Say so in the doc comment above narrow_by_host so the next reader does not try to bolt a path-prefix variant onto this index.
