(b) Precision, which recall cannot see because both ROUTE nodes are named '/users' and grade.py's _node_matches (bench/substrate-gap/grade.py:66-69) is a case-folded substring test: `"expect_category_counts": {"HTTP_CALLS": 1}` from A11.6 must hold — it reads 0 on main, 2 after A11.2 alone, and exactly 1 after A11.4. Plus a Rust unit test in graph/src/lib.rs's test module, built on the existing graph_with_infra helper at graph/src/lib.rs:3216: two RepoGraphs each holding a `route:/users` ROUTE with a ROUTE_METHOD GET cell, one of them also holding `infra:service:users-service`, and one endpoint whose ENDPOINT_HIT cell carries `"host":"users-service:8080"` — assert exactly one HTTP_CALLS cross-edge and that its `to` is the users repo's route id; a second case with host absent asserts two edges (today's behaviour preserved). Full matrix: `python3 bench/substrate-gap/run.py` still 0 blind spots, and py-http / swift-http / xstack-go-http are re-graded explicitly since A11.5 gives them hosts.

breaking.what_changes: HTTP_CALLS cross-edges that exist today can disappear. When an ENDPOINT carries a host, that host normalises to a known service alias, and at least one candidate ROUTE lives in a repo owning that alias, every candidate in a NON-owning repo loses its edge. This is the intended precision fix (it is what stops /users colliding across services) but it is a result change for any multi-repo merge where one service's routes were previously reached from another service's client. Guarded so it can only ever fire in the presence of positive evidence: unknown host, unknown alias, or zero matching targets all fall back to today's full target list. packets.rationale: Five languages already do the right thing with absolute URLs and then throw the host away: code-domain/src/lib.rs:761 url_to_path explicitly drops everything before the first path slash, and go (4 call sites), java (4), python (2) and swift (2) all funnel through it. packets.implementation:
Add `pub host: Option<String>` to ClientEndpoint (code-domain/src/lib.rs:711) and emit it from endpoint_hit_json only when Some, so a parser that has no host produces a byte-identical cell to today. Each parser replaces its `url_to_path(raw)` call with `let (host, path) = url_split(raw);` (the function A11.2 adds at code-domain/src/lib.rs:761) and threads host into the ClientEndpoint it constructs. Nothing about the path changes — url_split's path half is url_to_path's current return by construction — so every ENDPOINT qname in these five languages is unchanged and py-http / swift-http / xstack-go-http / java-spring-http keep their 1.00 cells.

The five parsers are independent files; this packet is splittable into five one-file jobs if the scheduler prefers, with code-domain/src/lib.rs landing first as a shared prerequisite. Two optional key.json keys; a fixture that omits both behaves exactly as today, so all 71 existing fixtures are untouched.

1. `"expect_absent_edges": [{"from": "...", "to": "...", "category": "HTTP_CALLS", "note": "..."}]`. Types:
```rust
/// One side of a message contract: the queue node plus where it lives and what
/// it says it carries. `file`/`line` fall back to the parent MODULE because
/// queue nodes carry no POSITION cell of their own (locate_node returns None).
#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
pub struct MessageContractSide {
    pub node_id: u64,
    pub repo_id: u64,
    pub qname: String,
    pub module: Option<String>,
    pub file: Option<String>,
    pub line: Option<i64>,
    pub message_type: Option<String>,
    pub message_type_raw: Option<String>,
    pub form: Option<String>,
    pub window: Option<String>,
}

/// One row of the contract report.
#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
pub struct MessageContractRow {
    pub topic: String,
    pub topic_is_tag: bool,
    pub producer: Option<MessageContractSide>,
    pub consumer: Option<MessageContractSide>,
    pub status: &'static str,     // "match" | "mismatch" | "unknown"
    pub note: Option<&'static str>,
}

pub fn message_contracts(merged: &MergedGraph) -> Vec<MessageContractRow>
```

Algorithm.
1. Walk every graph's nodes once. For each node whose `nav.kind_by_id` is QUEUE_PRODUCER or QUEUE_CONSUMER, strip `queue_producer:` / `queue_consumer:` off `nav.qname_by_id` (same convention as graph/src/lib.rs:1420) to get the topic, and build the `MessageContractSide` via a `fn side(g: &RepoGraph, merged: &MergedGraph, n: &Node) -> MessageContractSide` helper: `repo_id = g.repo.0`; `module = nav.parent_of.get(&n.id).and_then(|p| nav.qname_by_id.get(p).cloned())`; `(file, line)` = `locate_node(merged, *parent)` fields 4 and 5, falling back to `locate_node(merged, n.id)` first so this keeps working unchanged once A2 puts POSITION on the queue node itself; the message-type fields come from `n.cells.iter().find(|c| c.kind == cell_type::MESSAGE_TYPE)` parsed with `serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>` and `.get("type"|"raw"|"form"|"window").and_then(Value::as_str).map(String::from)` — a malformed payload yields all-None, never a panic.
2. Accumulate into `BTreeMap<String, (Vec<Side>, Vec<Side>)>` (BTreeMap, not HashMap, so topic order is process-stable). Sort each Vec by `(file, node_id)` for the same reason — node ids are xxhash64 of stable strings, so they are deterministic across processes.
3. Emit rows per topic:
   - If `queues::is_framework_tag(&topic)` — DO NOT cross-product. Emit one row per side with the other side `None`, `topic_is_tag: true`, `status: "unknown"`, `note: Some("topic is a framework tag, not a literal — no trustworthy pairing")`. This is the whole guard against the N×M fan-out the review warns about at line 89: on a C#/Java/kafkajs stack every queue node collapses to `kafka`, and a naive cross product would emit N×M bogus rows.
   - Otherwise, emit one row per (producer, consumer) pair: `status = "match"` when both `message_type`s are `Some` and equal; `"mismatch"` when both are `Some` and differ; `"unknown"` otherwise, with `note = Some("producer side has no detectable message type")` / `"consumer side …"` / `"neither side …"` as applicable.
   - A literal topic with producers but no consumers (or vice versa) emits one row per orphan side with the other `None` and `status: "unknown"`, `note: Some("no counterpart for this topic")` — this is the unpaired-topic signal that makes the report useful even before types exist.
4. Final `sort_by` on `(topic, producer.as_ref().map(|p| (p.file.clone(), p.node_id)), consumer.as_ref().map(|c| (c.file.clone(), c.node_id)))` so two runs over the same repo produce byte-identical JSON (house-style determinism, same reason as the `parses_by_lang` sort at engine/src/lib.rs:407).
5. Marker, printed once at the end of the function when `!rows.is_empty()`: `eprintln!("[contracts] topics={t} literal={l} tag={k} rows={r} match={m} mismatch={x} unknown={u}");`

Cases: Go NATS same type both sides → exactly one row, `status == "match"`, `topic == "orders"`, `topic_is_tag == false`; Go NATS differing types → `status == "mismatch"` with both `message_type`s populated; a C# tag-node file → one row with `topic_is_tag == true`, `status == "unknown"`, `consumer.is_none()`, and no combinatorial blow-up; producer-only literal topic → one row, `consumer.is_none()`, `note` naming the missing counterpart; determinism — call `message_contracts` twice on the same MergedGraph and assert the serialised JSON is identical.

bench/message-contracts/ — a two-service Go fixture exercising all three statuses in one build.
- `svc/publisher.go`: `nc.Publish("orders", data)` with `&pb.OrderCreated{}` marshalled above it.
- `worker/consumer.go`: `nc.Subscribe("orders", …)` with `&pb.OrderCreated{}` unmarshalled inside → the MATCH row.
- `svc/shipping.go`: `nc.Publish("shipments", data)` with `&pb.ShipmentCreated{}`.
- `worker/shipping_worker.go`: `nc.Subscribe("shipments", …)` with `&pb.ShipmentDispatched{}` → the MISMATCH row.
Note for the implementer: `extract_topic_near` is first-occurrence PER FILE (queues.rs:196), so the two topics must live in separate files per service — two `nc.Publish` calls in one file collapse to the first topic. That constraint is why the fixture is four files, and the README must say so.

`check.sh`, copied from bench/doc-link/check.sh:
```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
tmp="$(mktemp)"; trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
cargo run -q -p glia-cli -- contracts bench/message-contracts/svc \
    --with bench/message-contracts/worker --json 2>/dev/null > "$tmp"
python3 - "$tmp" <<'PY'
import json, sys, collections
rows = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
st = collections.Counter(r["status"] for r in rows)
seen = sorted(
    (r["topic"], r["status"],
     (r["producer"] or {}).get("message_type"),
     (r["consumer"] or {}).get("message_type"))
    for r in rows)
want = sorted([
    ("orders",    "match",    "OrderCreated",    "OrderCreated"),
    ("shipments", "mismatch", "ShipmentCreated", "ShipmentDispatched"),
])
fail = []
if st["match"] != 1:    fail.append(f"match={st['match']} want 1")
if st["mismatch"] != 1: fail.append(f"mismatch={st['mismatch']} want 1")
if any(r["topic_is_tag"] for r in rows): fail.append("a literal topic was flagged as a framework tag")
if seen != want:       fail.append(f"rows mismatch:\n  got  {seen}\n  want {want}")
if fail:
    print("FAIL:\n  " + "\n  ".join(fail)); sys.exit(1)
print("PASS: 1 match (orders/OrderCreated), 1 mismatch (shipments/ShipmentCreated vs ShipmentDispatched)")
PY
```
A second block in the same script asserts the pyo3 surface agrees, so the two transports cannot drift: `GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 python3 -c "import repo_graph_py as rg, json; rows=json.loads(rg.generate_many(['bench/message-contracts/svc','bench/message-contracts/worker']).contracts()); assert sorted((r['topic'],r['status']) for r in rows)==[('orders','match'),('shipments','mismatch')], rows; print('PASS: pyo3 contracts() agrees with the CLI')"`.

packets.title: SHARES_SCHEMA for namespace-nested types — measured baseline + unblock design (NON-EXECUTING)
packets.rationale: The review defers the SHARES_SCHEMA edge on the grounds that SharedSchemaResolver is structurally blind to C#. Measurement shows the deferral is right but the reason is wrong and the scope is wider, so shipping the 'obvious' fix blind would quietly add cross-repo edges in five languages. This packet ships NO code: it records the falsifiable baseline and writes down exactly what the unblock costs, so the owner decides rather than an implementing agent.
entry_points: graph/src/lib.rs:1586 — `if g.nav.kind_by_id.get(&n.id) != Some(&node_kind::MODULE) { continue; }` — the exact filter that causes the blindness
graph/src/lib.rs:1589-1599 — the single-level `children_of` walk plus the `is_schema_type` gate, where the fix would go
graph/src/lib.rs:1887-1897 — `is_schema_type(qname, kind)`: already gates on kind ∈ {CLASS, INTERFACE, STRUCT} and a name-hint list, so the MODULE walk adds nothing but the blindness
parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:101 — the PACKAGE NodeId for a namespace
parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:120-124 — the branch that hands `ns_id` to visit_children for both namespace forms, even though the grammar nests declarations only under the block form
parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:148 — `let qname = format!("{parent_qname}::{name}");` — the source of the two divergent C# qname shapes

parsers/code/c_cpp/src/lib.rs:118, parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:110, parsers/code/ruby/src/lib.rs:145, parsers/code/elixir/src/lib.rs:138 — the other PACKAGE emitters with the same nesting, which the review omits
packets.implementation:
NO source change. Deliverable is the recorded baseline plus this decision record.

MeASURED (generate_many over two dirs each holding one identical class):
- C# file-scoped `namespace Demo.Events;` → SHARES_SCHEMA = 1, pairing `Events::OrderCreatedSchema` ↔ `Events::OrderCreatedSchema`. Edge dump: `DEFINES MODULE Other -> CLASS Other::PaymentSchema` — the type is a MODULE child, so the resolver sees it.
- C# block `namespace Demo.Events { … }` → SHARES_SCHEMA = 0. Edge dump: `CONTAINS MODULE Events -> PACKAGE Demo::Events` then `DEFINES PACKAGE Demo::Events -> CLASS Demo::Events::OrderCreatedSchema` — the type is a PACKAGE grandchild, invisible to the MODULE-children walk.
- Java → SHARES_SCHEMA = 1 (kinds are only ['CLASS','MODULE']; Java emits no PACKAGE node), contradicting any assumption that package-scoped languages are uniformly blind.

WHAT THE UNBLOCK COSTS. The minimal fix is ~6 LOC: delete the MODULE filter at graph/src/lib.rs:1586 and the children_of indirection at :1589, and index every node directly — `is_schema_type` (:1887) already gates on kind and name-hint, so the MODULE walk contributes only the blind spot. That is NOT free:
1. It is breaking by edge ADDITION in five languages at once — csharp (block namespaces), c_cpp, php, ruby, elixir — every namespace/module-nested CLASS/INTERFACE/STRUCT whose name contains one of the 11 hints at :1888-1891 becomes pairable across repos. SHARES_SCHEMA is a carry edge, so `blast_radius` results change in any polyglot repo.
2. It must be preceded by C# qname normalisation. The same class is `Demo::Events::OrderCreatedSchema` under a block namespace and `Events::OrderCreatedSchema` under a file-scoped one (parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:148 with two different parents), so one C# repo migrating to file-scoped namespaces silently changes every type qname. `is_schema_type` reads the qname, and the pairing key is `name_by_id` (graph/src/lib.rs:1594) — so the pairing survives, but any qname-keyed consumer does not. Normalising C# type qnames to the namespace form is itself breaking (kind: qname_shape) and owns csharp lib.rs:878's test plus any C# fixture key.
3. The precision question is unanswered: `is_schema_type`'s 11-hint list plus an all-to-all pairwise cross product (graph/src/lib.rs:1605-1625) already fans out quadratically within a name group. Widening the index without first bounding that fan-out is the same mistake the review flags for tag-node queue pairing at line 89.
RECOMMENDATION: keep deferred. Sequence it AFTER Batch A rank 4 (which already rewrites C# qnames) and behind a bounded-fan-out change to the pairwise loop, as its own packet with its own 0.00 → 1.00 gate. This packet's fixture is exactly that gate, pre-recorded.

FIXTURE. `csharp-shared-schema/` with `dirs: ["a", "b"]` (2 dirs ⇒ generate_many ⇒ cross-graph resolvers fire) and one BLOCK-namespace `Demo.Events.OrderCreatedSchema` in each, expecting a SHARES_SCHEMA edge between them. It reads 0.00 today and will keep reading 0.00 until someone deliberately lands the unblock. Deliberately block-scoped: a file-scoped copy would read 1.00 and prove nothing.
packets.acceptance: No code ships and no cell flips. `python3 bench/substrate-gap/run.py` lists `csharp-shared-schema: SHARES_SCHEMA` under `BLIND SPOTS (recall 0.00)` and the row is appended to results.jsonl — the first ever SHARES_SCHEMA entry in the matrix (verified: no existing fixture key mentions SHARES_SCHEMA and no test in the repo references SharedSchemaResolver beyond its registration at engine/src/lib.rs:501). Falsifiable in both directions: adding a file-scoped sibling fixture must read 1.00 on the same run, proving the blindness is namespace-form-specific and not language-specific.
packets.fired_on_marker: none — no code ships. The artifact is the `- csharp-shared-schema: SHARES_SCHEMA` line under `BLIND SPOTS (recall 0.00)` in run.py output and the matching entry in bench/substrate-gap/results.jsonl

breaking.what_changes: Nothing changes: fixture data only. Recorded for the future packet — the eventual unblock WOULD be breaking by edge addition (new SHARES_SCHEMA carry edges in csharp block-namespace, c_cpp, php, ruby and elixir repos, changing blast_radius results), and would require C# type-qname normalisation (kind: qname_shape) as a prerequisite.

packets.risks: Same as A12.4: this raises the matrix's blind-spot count off zero on purpose. The key's `note` must say so, or the next session reads it as a regression and 'fixes' it by deleting the fixture.

Turn `is_data_entity` into `fn data_entity_flavor(node: &TsNode, src: &[u8]) -> Option<&'static str>` returning `Some("nosql")` when `@Document` matches and `Some("sql")` when `@Entity` matches (check `@Document` first; a class carrying both is a Mongo document). Update the call site at :151.

`data_entity_id(flavor: &str, simple_name: &str, repo: RepoId) -> NodeId` builds `format!("data_entity:{flavor}:{simple_name}")` — NOTE: pass the SURFACE name through, not the canonical fold. A13.1 canonicalises at index time; folding at emit time would change ~33 other assertions and break the lenient name match in grade.py. `emit_data_entity` gains the flavor param, keeps `cells` and the DEFINES edge unchanged, and at :298 passes `(name, &qname)` to `nav.record` instead of `(name, name)`.

`emit_repository_access` / `scan_repository_generics` only see the heritage clause, so derive the flavor from the base name already being matched against `REPOSITORY_BASES` (java/src/lib.rs:302-317): `MongoRepository` and `ReactiveMongoRepository` ⇒ `"nosql"`, every other base ⇒ `"sql"`. Without this the Mongo pair silently points at a non-existent node — the exact class of bug the existing comment at java/src/lib.rs:270-273 was written to prevent.

No marker of its own: A13.1's `prefixless=` counter going to 0 on a Java repo IS the proof, which is why this packet depends on A13.1.

packets.title: CLI invocation key normalisation — argv tokenisation + binary/subcommand pairing
packets.rationale: `extract_cli_command_nodes` (cli.rs:88-103) mints `cli:<subcommand>` from cobra `Use:` / click / commander / clap, while `extract_cli_invocation_nodes` (cli.rs:173-203) mints `cli_invoke:<first quoted token>` — the BINARY. `CliInvocationResolver` (graph/src/lib.rs:1903-1928) exact-matches the two, so they never pair. Worse, the dominant invocation shape extracts nothing at all: `extract_quoted` requires a quote as the first non-space char after the pattern, so `subprocess.run(["tool","migrate"])` and Go `[]string{"docker","build"}` produce no node (the extractor's own test at cli.rs:244 binds the array form to `_array_form` and tests the string form instead), and the whitespace form keeps the args in the key (`cli_invoke:terraform apply`).
entry_points: parsers/code/extractors/src/cli.rs:155-171 — `INVOCATION_PATTERNS`, the needle table the tokeniser runs behind
parsers/code/extractors/src/cli.rs:173-203 — `extract_cli_invocation_nodes`: `extract_quoted(after.trim_start())` at :186 is the single-token cut that drops every list form
parsers/code/extractors/src/cli.rs:126-153 — `extract_quoted`, reused unchanged for individual tokens
parsers/code/extractors/src/cli.rs:88-103 — `add_cli_command`, the `cli:<name>` declaration shape (UNCHANGED by this packet)
graph/src/lib.rs:1903-1928 — `CliInvocationResolver::resolve`: `qname.strip_prefix("cli_invoke:")` at :1913 becomes a two-key lookup
graph/src/lib.rs:1934-1957 — `build_kind_index`, reused as-is for the `cli:` index
parsers/code/extractors/src/cli.rs:243-249 — `detects_subprocess_invocation`, the test that documents the array-form gap
packets.implementation:
EXTRACTOR (cli.rs). Replace the single `extract_quoted` call at :186 with `fn scan_argv(after: &str) -> Vec<String>` which, from the text immediately following an INVOCATION_PATTERNS needle: skips whitespace and at most one opening `[`, `(`, `{`, or the Go `[]string{` prefix; then reads up to 8 consecutive quoted tokens separated only by whitespace, `,`, `.` (Go `...`) — stopping at the first non-quoted, non-separator char or a closing bracket. On a single quoted token containing spaces (the `subprocess.run('terraform apply')` shape) split that literal on ASCII whitespace into tokens. Then: `argv0 = basename(tokens[0])` (`rsplit('/')`, so `/usr/bin/terraform` → `terraform`; also strip a trailing `.exe`); `args = tokens[1..]`. Reject when argv0 is empty, >64 chars, or contains a `$`/`{` (an unresolved interpolation is not a binary name).

Key the node `cli_invoke:<argv0>` and dedupe per FILE on argv0, accumulating every argv vector seen for that binary into one CODE cell so the second `exec.Command("docker", "push", ...)` is not lost to the dedupe:
```rust
cells: vec![Cell { kind: cell_type::CODE, payload: CellPayload::Json(
    r#"{"bin":"docker","argv":[["build","."],["push","x"]]}"#.into()) }]
```
Build the JSON with the existing `escape_json` idiom (cron.rs:99-101 is the in-repo precedent); do not add serde_json to the hot path. Because the node id is built from the qname before the cell exists, accumulate into a `HashMap<String, Vec<Vec<String>>>` first and emit nodes in a second, sorted-by-argv0 pass so node order is deterministic.

RESOLVER (graph/src/lib.rs). `CliInvocationResolver` keeps its `build_kind_index(.., CLI_COMMAND, "cli:")`. For each CLI_INVOCATION node: (1) look up `argv0` (whole-program match); (2) parse the CODE cell and, for each argv vector, take the first token that does not start with `-` and is `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*` shaped, and look THAT up (subcommand match). Emit CLI_INVOKES for every hit, deduping on `(from, to)`. Cap subcommand lookups at 8 argv vectors per node. Confidence: `weakest(n.confidence, t.confidence)` for the argv0 match (unchanged), one step weaker (Weak) for a subcommand-only match, since `migrate` is a common word. No unwrap — the cell parse is a hand-rolled scan returning `Option`, and a missing/malformed cell just skips step (2).

Update cli.rs:243-249 to assert the concrete qname `cli_invoke:terraform` (not merely non-empty) and add `detects_list_form_invocation` (`subprocess.run(["terraform", "apply"])` → `cli_invoke:terraform` with argv `[["apply"]]`) and `detects_go_string_slice_invocation` (`exec.Command("kubectl", "apply", "-f", p)` → `cli_invoke:kubectl`, argv `[["apply","-f"]]`). Add one resolver test beside graph/tests/stack_resolvers.rs:206-224 for the subcommand path.
packets.acceptance: NEW FIXTURE bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/xcli-invokes (2 dirs ⇒ generate_many): the CLI_INVOKES cell reads 0.00 at HEAD (no CLI_INVOCATION node is emitted at all for the list form — run.py also reports the node miss) and 1.00 after, with BOTH expected edges found. packets.title: k8s CronJob: split multi-document YAML per document
packets.rationale: `extract_k8s_cronjob` (cron.rs:158-200) walks every line of the whole file overwriting `current_schedule`/`current_image`/`current_command` and emits ONE job at :189. A manifest bundle with three CronJobs yields one node; worse, when a non-CronJob document follows (a Deployment with a `command:`), the emitted node pairs the last CronJob's SCHEDULE with the Deployment's COMMAND — a node that is wrong, not merely incomplete. iac.rs:206 already splits the same file on `\n---`, so the asymmetry is internal to one crate.
entry_points: parsers/code/extractors/src/cron.rs:154-156 — `looks_like_k8s_cronjob`: `source.contains("kind: CronJob")`, exact single space, case-sensitive
parsers/code/extractors/src/cron.rs:158-200 — `extract_k8s_cronjob`: the whole-file line loop and the single `out.push` at :193
parsers/code/extractors/src/cron.rs:58-60 — the `if looks_like_k8s_cronjob(source) { jobs.extend(...) }` call site in `extract_cron_nodes`
parsers/code/extractors/src/iac.rs:206 — `for doc in source.split("\n---")`, the in-repo document-splitting precedent to mirror exactly
parsers/code/extractors/src/cron.rs:646-690 — the two existing single-document k8s tests that must keep passing
packets.implementation:
Rename the existing body to `fn extract_k8s_cronjob_doc(doc: &str) -> Option<CronJob>` — unchanged logic, but it returns at most one job for ONE document. Add:
```rust
fn extract_k8s_cronjob(source: &str) -> Vec<CronJob> {
    source
        .split("\n---")
        .map(|d| d.trim_start_matches('\n'))
        .filter(|d| !d.is_empty() && doc_is_cronjob(d))
        .filter_map(extract_k8s_cronjob_doc)
        .collect()
}
```
`doc_is_cronjob(doc)` replaces the file-level `looks_like_k8s_cronjob` gate per document, and fixes the whitespace/quoting brittleness at the same time: for each line, `trim()`, `strip_prefix("kind:")`, then `trim()` + `trim_matches(|c| c == '"' || c == '\'')` and compare `== "CronJob"`. This mirrors `read_k8s_kind` (iac.rs:246-260) — reuse that logic rather than inventing a second one. Keep the file-level `looks_like_k8s_cronjob` as a cheap pre-gate but widen it to a case-insensitive `contains("cronjob")` so `kind: "CronJob"` reaches the per-document check (a false pre-gate hit costs one `split` and is filtered out per document).

The dedupe at cron.rs:66-69 (`seen.insert(qname)`) already handles two identical jobs in one file, so nothing else changes. `extract_cron_nodes` is unchanged apart from the marker.

Marker: emit only when the file actually contained k8s CronJob documents, so it does not fire on every YAML in a repo:
```rust
if k8s_docs > 0 { eprintln!("[cron] k8s docs={k8s_docs} jobs={}", jobs_from_k8s); }
```

No unwrap: `split`/`filter_map` throughout; `extract_k8s_cronjob_doc` keeps its existing `if let Some(schedule)` guard.

Add `k8s_multidoc_emits_one_job_per_document` (three documents: CronJob cleanup, CronJob report, Deployment api-with-a-command → exactly two CRON_JOB qnames, neither targeting `server`) and `k8s_cronjob_kind_tolerates_quotes_and_extra_space` next to the two existing tests at cron.rs:646-690, which must keep passing unmodified.
packets.acceptance: NEW FIXTURE bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/k8s-multidoc-cron (1 dir): its SCHEDULES cell reads 0.00 at HEAD — today the file yields ONE node `cron:0 6 * * 1:server` (last CronJob's schedule + the Deployment's command basename), so NEITHER expected CRON_JOB node is found — and 1.00 after, with both nodes present. Unit gates: `cargo test -p repo-graph-code-extractors cron` — `k8s_cronjob_yaml` (cron.rs:646) and `k8s_falls_back_to_image_basename_when_no_command` (:674) must pass BYTE-UNCHANGED (both are single-document, so the split is a no-op for them), plus the two new tests. Grep gate: `[cron] k8s docs=3 jobs=2`.

breaking.what_changes: For a multi-document YAML the emitted CRON_JOB set changes: today exactly one node with a cross-document mashed qname `cron:<last schedule>:<last command-or-image anywhere in the file>`; after, one correct node per CronJob document. In a bundle whose last document is not a CronJob, the single node that exists today DISAPPEARS and is replaced by different, correct nodes — an edge/node removal, so it counts as breaking even though every removed node was wrong. Single-document manifests (the overwhelming majority, and both existing tests) are byte-identical. Widening the kind gate to tolerate quotes/extra spaces adds nodes only.

packets.title: Config define-side VALUES on an ENV cell (with redaction) — the A11 dependency
packets.rationale: All four define-side scanners parse `KEY=value` and throw the value away: config.rs:289-333 `dockerfile_env_pairs` splits the pair and keeps only KEY, config.rs:335-352 `scan_dotenv` finds `=` and pushes `t[..eq]`, and :354/:390 do the same for k8s/compose. `build_nodes` (config.rs:103-143) then creates the CONFIG_KEY node with `cells: vec![]` at :131. So `API_URL=http://users-svc:8080` is in the graph as a bare name, and service-hostname pairing / base-URL folding (area A11) has nothing to read. A11 MUST consume this, not re-parse the files.
entry_points: parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs:103-143 — `build_nodes(names: Vec<String>, ...)`: the signature and the `cells: vec![]` at :131 are the whole change
parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs:262-282 — `scan_dockerfile_env` → `Vec<String>`
parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs:289-333 — `dockerfile_env_pairs`, which already parses the value and discards it
parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs:335-352 — `scan_dotenv` → `Vec<String>`
parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs:354-389 — `scan_k8s_env` (k8s `env: - name:/value:`)
parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs:390 — `scan_compose_environment`
parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs:55-70 — `extract_config_reads`, the READ side, which must keep passing names only (no value exists at a read site)
code-domain/src/lib.rs:344 — `cell_type::ENV = CellTypeId(12)`: declared, in the ALL table at :374, and emitted NOWHERE today
packets.implementation:
Introduce `struct ConfigDef { name: String, value: Option<String> }` local to config.rs. Change the four DEFINE-side scanners to return `Vec<ConfigDef>`; leave the seven READ-side scanners (config.rs:164-261) returning `Vec<String>` and adapt them at the call site with `.map(|n| ConfigDef { name: n, value: None })`. `dockerfile_env_pairs` already walks the value to find the pair boundary, so capturing it is a few lines; `scan_dotenv` becomes `t[..eq]` / `t[eq+1..]` with the value trimmed and unquoted; `scan_k8s_env` must pair a `name:` line with a sibling `value:` line at the same indent inside the same list item (a `valueFrom:`/`secretRef:` item yields `value: None`); `scan_compose_environment` handles both the `- KEY=value` list form and the `KEY: value` map form.

`build_nodes` takes `Vec<ConfigDef>`, keeps `is_valid_env_name` + the dedupe unchanged (dedupe on name; first non-None value wins), and attaches ONE cell when a value exists:
```rust
cells: vec![Cell { kind: cell_type::ENV, payload: CellPayload::Json(payload) }]
```
with payload `{"value":"http://users-svc:8080","source":"dotenv","redacted":false}` or `{"source":"dotenv","redacted":true}`. `source` is a new `&'static str` param threaded from each `extract_*_defs` entry point (`dockerfile` | `dotenv` | `k8s` | `compose`). Build the JSON with the `escape_json` idiom already used at cron.rs:99-101 — no serde_json in the hot path.

REDACTION IS MANDATORY, not optional: .gmap files are written to `.ai/repo-graph/` on disk and shipped to consumers, so a `.env` secret must not land in the graph. `fn is_secret_name(name: &str) -> bool` — case-insensitive `contains` over SECRET, PASSWORD, PASSWD, TOKEN, APIKEY, API_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, CREDENTIAL, ACCESS_KEY, SESSION_KEY, SALT, SIGNING. Additionally, when a value matches `://<user>:<pass>@` replace the userinfo with `***` and keep the rest (so `postgres://u:p@db:5432/app` stores `postgres://***@db:5432/app` — the HOST survives, which is precisely what A11 needs). Cap stored values at 200 chars.

Marker in `build_nodes`, emitted only for the define side and only when it produced nodes: `[config] defined=N valued=M redacted=K`.

Tests in config.rs: `dotenv_value_lands_on_env_cell`, `dockerfile_env_multi_pair_values`, `k8s_env_value_from_sibling_line`, `secret_named_key_is_redacted`, `db_url_userinfo_is_masked_host_kept`, and a regression test that a READ-side CONFIG_KEY still has `cells.is_empty()`.

NO pyo3/CLI change: `PyGraph.node_cells` (py/src/lib.rs:164-184) returns every cell generically and `cell_type_names()` (py/src/lib.rs:488-491) already includes ENV from the ALL table.
packets.acceptance: Unit-test gated (no new eval cell — grade.py grades nodes and edges, not cells): the six new tests in parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs pass, and every existing config test passes unchanged. Regression gate: all 49 existing substrate-gap cells stay at their current values, since no node id, qname, name or edge changes. Grep gate: building a repo containing a `.env` prints `[config] defined=3 valued=3 redacted=1`. Contract gate for A11: `python3 -c` over `PyGraph.node_cells(<CONFIG_KEY id>)` returns a `(12, '{"value":...}')` tuple.

breaking.what_changes: Additive: CONFIG_KEY nodes emitted from a define-side file gain one ENV cell (CellTypeId 12, already in the ALL table so pyo3 decodes it with no change). No node id, qname, name, edge or existing cell value changes. It does change the bytes of a .gmap for repos with .env/Dockerfile/k8s env, which is normal for any extractor change and is covered by engine/tests/byte_identical.rs comparing two builds of the same tree rather than a golden file.

packets.risks: AREA A11 MUST DEPEND ON THIS PACKET AND NOT RE-IMPLEMENT IT — A11's service-hostname pairing needs exactly the `value` field this emits, and a second value parser in a second crate is the 'wrapper reimplements degraded' anti-pattern. Hand A11 the ENV-cell payload shape above as the contract. Redaction is the one thing that must not be deferred: shipping raw .env values into a persisted .gmap is a data-leak regression, and it is far harder to walk back than to get right the first time. Note that the userinfo-masking rule deliberately KEEPS the host, so a masked DB URL is still pairable.

packets.title: Secrets + feature-flag references as CONFIG_KEY flavors
packets.rationale: The review's matrix has `secrets ●0 ◐0 ·16` and `flags ●0 ◐0 ·16` and the grep confirms it: the only mentions of vault/secretsmanager/launchdarkly/unleash/flagsmith anywhere in the workspace are two doc comments at config.rs:10 and :32 declaring them out of scope. 'Which services read this secret' and 'where is this flag checked' are pure grep tasks today. config.rs:10 already RESERVES the `config:secret:` flavor, so this is the shape the substrate was designed for.
entry_points: parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs:7-10 — the doc block reserving `config:secret:vault/path`, the shape this packet implements
parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs:103-143 — `build_nodes`: the CONFIG_KEY emit + READS_CONFIG/DEFINES_CONFIG edge the new scanners reuse (after A13.7 it is already flavor/value aware)
parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs:125-127 — `format!("config:env:{name}")`: the hardcoded flavor that becomes a parameter
parsers/code/extractors/src/lib.rs:3 — `pub mod config;`; the new `pub mod secrets_flags;` line goes in this file
engine/src/lib.rs:889 — `run_with_edges!(config::extract_config_reads(source, module_id, repo));` — the new extractor is wired immediately after it
engine/src/lib.rs:213-217 — the yaml branch's `extract_yaml_env_defs` call, where k8s `Secret` data keys are picked up
code-domain/src/lib.rs:90-94 — `CONFIG_KEY = NodeKindId(38)`: reused verbatim, no new kind
packets.implementation:
NO NEW IDs OF ANY KIND. NodeKind stays CONFIG_KEY(38); edges stay READS_CONFIG(25) and DEFINES_CONFIG(26); the cell is `cell_type::ENV`(12), already in the ALL table (code-domain/src/lib.rs:374) — so the 'any new CellType MUST get its ALL entry' rule is satisfied vacuously and pyo3 decodes everything with zero change. The extension point is the QNAME FLAVOR SEGMENT, exactly as config.rs:7-10 reserved:
  - `config:secret:<provider>/<ref>` — e.g. `config:secret:vault/secret/data/db`, `config:secret:aws_sm/prod/db-creds`, `config:secret:gcp_sm/projects/p/secrets/db`, `config:secret:azure_kv/db-password`, `config:secret:k8s/api-keys`
  - `config:flag:<key>` — e.g. `config:flag:new-checkout`
The provider is joined with `/` rather than a fourth `:` segment so nothing that reasons about `config:<flavor>:<rest>` has to change.

First, generalise config.rs minimally: make `build_nodes` take a `flavor: &'static str` (today's callers pass `"env"`) and make it `pub(crate)` so secrets_flags.rs reuses the identical emit path (node + edge + dedupe + ENV cell). Do NOT copy it.

New `parsers/code/extractors/src/secrets_flags.rs` with two public entry points mirroring config.rs's shape:
```rust
pub fn extract_secret_refs(source: &str, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId) -> ConfigNodes;
pub fn extract_feature_flags(source: &str, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId) -> ConfigNodes;
```
Both are language-blind string scanners (the established pattern for this crate — data_sources.rs:12 documents the trade-off) built on a `(needle, provider, arg_index)` table plus the existing `capture_first_string_arg` helper (config.rs:164-180 idiom) generalised to `capture_nth_string_arg(source, needle, n)`.

SECRET needles (~14 rows): Vault — `client.read("`, `.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(`, `vault.Logical().Read(`, `KVSecretV2.Get(`; AWS — `get_secret_value(SecretId=`, `GetSecretValueRequest`/`SecretId =`, `secretsmanager.GetSecretValue(`, `@aws-sdk/client-secrets-manager` + `SecretId:`; GCP — `access_secret_version(name=`, `AccessSecretVersion(`; Azure — `SecretClient(` + `.get_secret(`/`.GetSecret(`; k8s — `secretKeyRef:` (yaml path only, DEFINES side). Reject a captured ref that is empty, >200 chars, or contains `$`/`{` (unresolved interpolation).

FLAG needles (~12 rows): LaunchDarkly — `.variation("`, `.boolVariation("`, `.BoolVariation("`, `ldclient.variation(`; OpenFeature — `.getBooleanValue("`, `.getStringValue("`, `GetBooleanValue(`; Unleash — `.isEnabled("`, `unleash.isEnabled(`; Flagsmith — `.has_feature("`, `.hasFeature("`; Split — `.getTreatment("`. Gate each flag capture on a flag-key shape (`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,63}`, must contain a `-`, `_` or `.` OR be ≥4 chars) so `.variation("a")` noise is dropped. Store the provider on the ENV cell: `{"provider":"launchdarkly"}`.

Wire both into `apply_cross_cutting_extractors` right after engine/src/lib.rs:889 with `run_with_edges!`, so they fire for every code file in every one of the 16 languages — that is what turns two `·16` rows into coverage. The k8s `secretKeyRef:` define-side capture goes into the yaml branch alongside `extract_yaml_env_defs` (engine/src/lib.rs:213-217).

No unwrap; every capture is `Option`-returning. Marker emitted only when something was captured.
packets.acceptance: TWO NEW FIXTURES. bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/secrets-vault-aws·READS_CONFIG and bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/flags-launchdarkly·READS_CONFIG each read 0.00 at HEAD (no CONFIG_KEY node of either flavor exists — run.py also reports the node misses) and 1.00 after. Unit gates: `cargo test -p repo-graph-code-extractors secrets_flags` — at least `vault_read_path`, `aws_secret_id_kwarg`, `ld_bool_variation_key`, `unleash_is_enabled_key`, `rejects_interpolated_ref`, `rejects_single_char_flag_key`. Guard: the existing config tests and all 49 pre-existing cells are unchanged. Grep gate: `[secrets] refs=1 providers=1 flags=0` on the secrets fixture and `[secrets] refs=0 providers=0 flags=1` on the flags fixture.

breaking.what_changes: Purely additive: new CONFIG_KEY nodes under two new qname FLAVORS and new READS_CONFIG / DEFINES_CONFIG edges. No new NodeKind, EdgeCategory or CellType id is introduced, so no ALL table grows and no decode table changes. Existing `config:env:*` nodes, their ids and their edges are untouched. NOTE that READS_CONFIG and DEFINES_CONFIG ARE in blast_carry_edges() (graph/src/lib.rs:2192-2193), so these new edges DO widen blast_radius answers on repos using a secrets manager or a flag SDK — intended (a flag check is a real dependency) but it is a visible result change on real repos.

packets.title: Migration file routing + SQL DDL and ORM-DSL table capture
packets.rationale: The `migr` row is 0/16 for three separate reasons, all verified: (1) `.sql` is in neither `detect_language` (engine/src/lib.rs:756-786) nor `is_bypass_path` (engine/src/lib.rs:1182-1193), and walk_dir reads a file only if one matches (engine/src/lib.rs:1132-1137), so Flyway/golang-migrate/knex SQL is never read off disk at all; (2) Django/Alembic/Rails migrations ARE read but their DDL is a DSL (`op.create_table("users")`) that `has_sql_context` (data_entities.rs:126-142) rejects; (3) even for real SQL, `scan_sql_tables` (data_entities.rs:144-198) scans only FROM/JOIN/INTO/UPDATE, so `CREATE TABLE users` names nothing. 'Which service owns the table this migration alters' is unanswerable.
entry_points: engine/src/lib.rs:1182-1193 — `is_bypass_path`: the gate that decides whether a file's bytes are read; gains `migrations::is_migration_path(path)`
engine/src/lib.rs:291-313 — the `is_dotenv_path` bypass branch in `build_graphs_for_repo`: the exact shape the new `.sql` branch copies (module_id + extractor + `stash_synthetic_parse` + `continue`)
engine/src/lib.rs:2016-2057 — `stash_synthetic_parse`, which mints the MODULE node the ACCESSES_DATA edges anchor on
parsers/code/extractors/src/data_entities.rs:144-198 — `scan_sql_tables`: the FROM/JOIN/INTO/UPDATE keyword loop that gains `TABLE`
parsers/code/extractors/src/data_entities.rs:126-142 — `has_sql_context`: already lists `create table` / `alter table` as signatures, so the gate passes; only the capture is missing
parsers/code/extractors/src/data_entities.rs:46-113 — `extract_data_entity_nodes`, where the ORM-DSL scanner is added to the existing scanner list
parsers/code/extractors/src/lib.rs — `pub mod migrations;` declaration
packets.implementation:
NO new NodeKind / EdgeCategory / CellType — the migration file's MODULE node (already minted by `stash_synthetic_parse`) is the anchor, and the edges are the existing ACCESSES_DATA(18). That keeps the packet out of the grade.py registry-ordering trap entirely.

BLOCK 1 — `TABLE` keyword (data_entities.rs, ~15 LOC). Add `"TABLE"` to the keyword array at :146. It covers `CREATE TABLE x`, `ALTER TABLE x`, `DROP TABLE x`, `TRUNCATE TABLE x` in one row because the table name always follows. Two guards inside the existing capture: after `TABLE`, skip a leading `IF NOT EXISTS` / `IF EXISTS` token run before reading the identifier; and skip `ONLY` (Postgres `ALTER TABLE ONLY x`). This affects every language (a `.py` file with a `CREATE TABLE` string literal now names the table) — additive only, and `has_sql_context` already gates it.

BLOCK 2 — new `parsers/code/extractors/src/migrations.rs` (~90 LOC):
```rust
pub fn is_migration_path(path: &str) -> bool;   // used by engine's is_bypass_path
pub fn migration_framework(path: &str) -> Option<&'static str>;
pub fn extract_sql_migration(source: &str, path: &str, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId) -> DataEntityNodes;
pub fn scan_migration_dsl(source: &str) -> Vec<String>;   // called from data_entities.rs
```
`is_migration_path`: extension is `sql` AND a path segment is one of `migrations`, `migrate`, `migration`, `changelog`, `sql` under a `db/` parent; OR the basename matches Flyway `V<digits>__*.sql` / `R__*.sql`; OR the basename ends `.up.sql` / `.down.sql` (golang-migrate). Normalise `\\` to `/` first (the repo does this at iac.rs:148). Deliberately NARROW: an arbitrary `.sql` anywhere is NOT read, so a repo full of query fixtures does not flood the graph.
`migration_framework` maps the matched shape to `flyway` | `golang-migrate` | `knex` | `liquibase` | `raw` for the marker.
`extract_sql_migration` just calls `data_entities::extract_data_entity_nodes(source, module_id, repo)` — the DDL scan from Block 1 does the work — and is a thin wrapper so the engine branch reads cleanly.
`scan_migration_dsl` covers the read-but-not-understood cases with ~10 needles, each capturing the first string/symbol arg: Alembic `op.create_table("`, `op.add_column("`, `op.drop_table("`, `op.rename_table("`; Django `migrations.CreateModel(name="`, `migrations.AddField(model_name="`; Rails `create_table :`, `add_column :`, `change_table :`, `drop_table :` (Ruby SYMBOL form — read `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` after the `:`, no quotes); knex `knex.schema.createTable("`, `.table("`; EF Core `migrationBuilder.CreateTable(name: "`, `migrationBuilder.AddColumn<`+`table: "`. Wire it into `extract_data_entity_nodes` beside the other `for name in scan_*` loops at data_entities.rs:92-110, emitting flavor `Sql`. It runs on every code file, which is correct — a Rails `create_table :orders` is a table declaration wherever it appears.

BLOCK 3 — engine routing (~35 LOC). Add `|| repo_graph_code_extractors::migrations::is_migration_path(path)` to `is_bypass_path` (engine/src/lib.rs:1190-1192) so walk_dir reads the bytes, then add a branch in `build_graphs_for_repo` modelled exactly on the dotenv branch at :291-313 (module_id from `path_to_qname`, call `extract_sql_migration`, `stash_synthetic_parse("migration", ...)` when non-empty, `continue`). Place it AFTER the dotenv branch and BEFORE `detect_language` so a `.sql` never reaches the language dispatch.

No unwrap anywhere; every capture returns Option.

Tests: in migrations.rs — `flyway_path_matches`, `golang_migrate_up_down_matches`, `query_fixture_sql_does_not_match`, `alembic_create_table_captured`, `rails_symbol_create_table_captured`. In data_entities.rs — `create_table_if_not_exists_captured`, `alter_table_only_captured`.

Unit gates: the 7 tests above. Guard: all 49 pre-existing cells unchanged — in particular the four `*-accesses-data` cells, which the new `TABLE` keyword must not disturb. Grep gate: `[migrations] file=db/migrations/V1__create_users.sql framework=flyway tables=1`.

The `TABLE` keyword can only ADD table names inside sources that already pass has_sql_context. No existing node, qname, name, cell or edge changes. Node counts rise on any repo with migrations, which is a visible but intended result change.

packets.title: ORM: Hibernate/JPA @Table(name=) and @Document(collection=)
packets.rationale: parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:280-299 names the DATA_ENTITY after the CLASS. Every JPA codebase where the table differs from the class — the normal case for a legacy schema, `@Table(name = "app_users")` on `class User` — produces an entity named `User` that can never join the `app_users` the SQL/migration side sees. Same for `@Document(collection = "...")`.
entry_points: parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:259-262 — `DATA_ENTITY_ANNOTATIONS`, where `@Table` joins as a NAME SOURCE (not a trigger)
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:264-269 — `is_data_entity` / (post-A13.2) `data_entity_flavor`, which already reads `modifiers_text`
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:280-299 — `emit_data_entity(name, ...)`: `name` becomes the resolved table name, while the node's display name stays the class simple name
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:151-153 — the call site that must pass both the class name and the resolved table name
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:320-334 — `emit_repository_access`: it only sees the entity TYPE name, so it needs the class→table map
packets.implementation:
Add `fn annotation_string_arg(modifiers: &str, annot: &str, key: &str) -> Option<String>` — find `@Table`/`@Document`, then inside its parens find `name =` / `collection =` and read the following string literal; fall back to the first bare string literal (`@Table("app_users")`). Returns None when absent. Reuse the existing `has_annotation` / `modifiers_text` helpers rather than adding a parser pass.

At the call site (java:151-153), resolve `table = annotation_string_arg(mods, "@Table", "name").or(annotation_string_arg(mods, "@Document", "collection")).unwrap_or_else(|| name.to_string())` — expressed without `unwrap`, via `match`/`map_or_else`. Pass `(display_name = class simple name, key_name = table)` into `emit_data_entity`: the qname/NodeId uses `key_name` (so A13.1 canonicalises `app_users` and it joins the migration and the SQL query sites), while `nav.record`'s NAME argument stays the CLASS simple name so `glia find User` still works and grade.py's lenient name match is preserved.

Because `emit_repository_access` (java:320) only sees the bare TYPE name from the heritage generics, add a pre-pass (mirroring python's `scan_model_tables` at python/src/lib.rs:913-936, the in-repo precedent) that walks the file's top-level type declarations once, recording `class simple name -> resolved table name` into `acc`. `scan_repository_generics` then looks the entity type up in that map before falling back to the bare name. This is same-file resolution off a literal, not cross-file resolution — a repository in another file still falls back to the type name, which is exactly today's behaviour.

Tests: `jpa_table_annotation_overrides_class_name` (entity qname keys on `app_users`, node name is still `User`, and the repository ACCESSES_DATA edge targets the SAME id) and `jpa_entity_without_table_keeps_class_name` (the java-spring-accessdata shape, unchanged).

packets.title: ORM: EF Core DbSet<T> / ToTable() (first C# DATA_ENTITY)
packets.rationale: C# emits no DATA_ENTITY node of any kind — the `db ◐` in the review's csharp row comes from data_sources.rs provider buckets only. An EF Core `AppDbContext` is the single place a .NET service declares every table it owns, and it is invisible: `glia blast-radius` on a table cannot reach the .NET service, and the polyglot join from A13.1 has nothing on the C# side to join.
entry_points: parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:142 — `"class_declaration" | "record_declaration" | "record_struct_declaration" => node_kind::CLASS`: the type-visit seam where the DbContext is recognised and its node id is in hand
parsers/code/extractors/src/data_entities.rs:46-113 — `extract_data_entity_nodes`, the shape the new emit mirrors (node + ACCESSES_DATA edge, deterministic id)
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:280-299 — `emit_data_entity`, the in-repo precedent for a parser emitting a name-derived DATA_ENTITY + edge
code-domain/src/lib.rs — `data_entity::canonical_entity_name` (A13.1) is NOT called at emit time; the surface name goes in the qname
packets.implementation:
At the class-visit seam (csharp/src/lib.rs:142 onward), when a class's base list contains `DbContext` (or ends in `DbContext`), walk its body for two shapes:
(a) property declarations whose type is `DbSet<T>` / `DbSet<T>?` — take `T`'s simple name (strip any namespace qualifier) as the entity;
(b) inside `OnModelCreating`, the fluent `modelBuilder.Entity<T>()` chain followed by `.ToTable("name")` — when present, `name` OVERRIDES the `DbSet<T>` name for that `T`.
Collect into a `HashMap<String /*T*/, String /*table*/>` in a first pass over the class body (so `.ToTable` wins regardless of source order), then emit once per entry: a DATA_ENTITY node with qname `data_entity:sql:<table>` (built through the shared helper so the id matches every other emitter), display name = `<table>`, plus an ACCESSES_DATA edge from the DbContext CLASS node to it. Dedupe on the NodeId within the file.

Use the tree-sitter C# node kinds the parser already handles; do not add a second parse. For the `.ToTable` chain, walk the `invocation_expression` subtree looking for a `generic_name` whose base is `Entity` and a sibling `.ToTable` invocation in the same statement — bounded to the single statement so unrelated `.ToTable` calls elsewhere are not picked up.

No unwrap; every `child_by_field_name` is `let ... else { continue }`.

Tests: `efcore_dbset_emits_entity`, `efcore_to_table_overrides_dbset_name`, `plain_class_emits_no_entity` (mirroring java/src/lib.rs:1394-1406 so the noise gate is pinned).

Unit gate: the three new tests in parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs. Guard: the csharp-aspnet cell is unchanged. Grep gate: `[orm-efcore] contexts=1 tables=1`.

packets.title: ORM: GORM TableName() / db.Model() / db.Table()
packets.rationale: Go's only DATA_ENTITY path is raw-SQL string scanning (parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:840-886). A GORM service issues zero SQL strings — `db.Model(&User{}).Find(&us)` — so the Go row's `db ◐` is raw-SQL-only and every GORM service is a data blind spot, including the `TableName()` override that is the whole point of the pattern.
entry_points: parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:619 — the call-visit site in the fn-body walk where `try_detect_go_data_access` already fires with the enclosing fn id in hand
parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:840-861 — `try_detect_go_data_access`: the sibling detector the new one sits beside
parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:864-886 — `emit_data_access(table, from, repo, acc)`: reused verbatim, including its `(from, entity_id)` dedupe at :870
parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:176 — the `Acc` dedupe field doc, where the type→table map is added
packets.implementation:
Pre-pass over the file's top-level declarations (mirroring python's `scan_model_tables`, python/src/lib.rs:913-936): record `struct type name -> table name` for every `func (X) TableName() string { return "..." }` / `func (x X) TableName() string` whose body is a single string-literal return. Store in a new `Acc` field `gorm_tables: HashMap<String, String>`. Default when absent: GORM's own convention is snake_case + pluralise (`User` → `users`), so fall back to `canonical_entity_name(type)` + `"s"`; simpler and safer, fall back to the snake_case singular and let A13.1's index fold do the joining — do NOT hand-roll a pluraliser here.

New `try_detect_gorm_access(call, src, from, repo, acc)` called from the same place as `try_detect_go_data_access` (go:619). It matches three shapes on a `call_expression`: `.Model(&T{})` / `.Model(T{})` — take T's simple name and look it up in `gorm_tables`; `.Table("name")` — take the literal directly; `.Find(&ts)` / `.First(&t)` where the argument is a composite literal of a known type (optional, only when the type is already in `gorm_tables`). Then call the existing `emit_data_access(&table, from, repo, acc)` so the node id, dedupe and edge are byte-identical to the SQL path.

No unwrap; every field access is `let ... else { return }`.

Tests: `gorm_model_uses_tablename_override`, `gorm_table_literal_captured`, `gorm_without_tablename_falls_back_to_type`, and a noise test that `x.Model(cfg)` with a non-composite arg emits nothing.

packets.title: ORM: Eloquent $table / Model subclass (first PHP DATA_ENTITY)
packets.rationale: PHP emits no DATA_ENTITY node at all (the php row's `db ◐` is data_sources provider buckets). Laravel's entire data layer is `class User extends Model` with an implicit or `protected $table` explicit table name, so a Laravel service is a complete data blind spot: neither the polyglot join (A13.1) nor the migration join (A13.9) has a PHP side to join to.
entry_points: parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:133-161 — `visit_class`: the class node id is minted at :147 and recorded at :161, the seam where the model is recognised
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:280-299 — `emit_data_entity`, the in-repo precedent for a parser-emitted DATA_ENTITY + edge

In `visit_class` (php:133), after the CLASS node is recorded, check the heritage clause for a base named `Model` or `Illuminate\\Database\\Eloquent\\Model` (compare the last `\\`-separated segment). packets.title: ORM: TypeORM @Entity('table') decorator
packets.rationale: TypeScript's only DATA_ENTITY paths are the language-blind mongoose/collection scanners in data_entities.rs — a TypeORM backend, the dominant Nest/Express SQL stack, emits nothing. The decorator argument is the table name and is a pure literal, so this is the cheapest per-cell ORM packet in the set.

parsers/code/extractors/src/data_entities.rs:366-388 — `scan_mongoose_models`, the existing TS-facing entity scanner this sits beside conceptually
packets.implementation:
In `visit_class` (ts:168), inspect the class's decorators for `@Entity`. Table name = the decorator's first string-literal argument when present (`@Entity('app_users')` or `@Entity({ name: 'app_users' })` — read `name:` inside the object literal), else the class simple name. Emit a DATA_ENTITY node with qname `data_entity:sql:<table>`, display name `<table>`, plus a DEFINES edge from the class node.

Gate on the decorator NAME only (`Entity`), and additionally require that the file imports from `typeorm` (a cheap `source.contains("typeorm")` check threaded in, or the parser's existing import list) — `@Entity` is also a Nest/Mikro-ORM decorator and the gate keeps the flavor honest. Without the gate this scanner fires on any `@Entity` in any TS file, which is the precision failure the review flags repeatedly for tag-only nodes.

Record class→table on `Acc` and, at a `getRepository(User)` / `@InjectRepository(User)` site inside a method, emit ACCESSES_DATA from the enclosing method to the entity id.

No unwrap; decorator/argument reads are Option-returning. Since ts/src/lib.rs also backs the react/angular/vue parsers, confirm the change is inside `visit_class` and not in a path those three re-enter differently.

Tests: `typeorm_entity_decorator_arg_is_table`, `typeorm_entity_without_arg_uses_class_name`, `entity_decorator_without_typeorm_import_is_ignored`.

packets.rationale: `schema.prisma` matches neither `detect_language` (engine/src/lib.rs:756-786) nor `is_bypass_path` (:1182-1193), so walk_dir never reads it (:1132-1137) — the single file that declares the entire data model of a Prisma stack is not in the graph at all. Prisma is the default ORM of the Next.js/T3 stack the review calls the largest full-stack blind spot.

engine/src/lib.rs:291-313 — the dotenv bypass branch in `build_graphs_for_repo`, the exact template for the new branch

New `parsers/code/extractors/src/prisma.rs` (~60 LOC), zero deps, a line scanner over the Prisma DSL (it is block-structured and regular enough that a tokenizer is unnecessary):

```rust
pub fn extract_prisma_models(source: &str, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId) -> DataEntityNodes;
```

Table = the `@@map` value when present, else `<Name>`. Emit a DATA_ENTITY (`data_entity:sql:<table>`, display name `<table>`) plus an ACCESSES_DATA edge from the schema file's MODULE node, matching the `extract_data_entity_nodes` shape at data_entities.rs:69-82 — return the same `DataEntityNodes` struct so the engine branch can reuse `run_with_edges!`-style plumbing. Also scan `datasource db { provider = "postgresql" }` and note the provider in the marker (it decides the flavor: `mongodb` ⇒ `nosql`, everything else ⇒ `sql`).

packets.title: ORM: Django models.Model implicit table name
packets.rationale: data_entities.rs:313-333 captures Django tables ONLY via an explicit `db_table = '...'` in `class Meta`. The overwhelming majority of Django models never set it and rely on the implicit `<app_label>_<lowercased model>` convention, so a standard Django service contributes zero entities — while python/src/lib.rs:913-936 already does the equivalent pre-pass for SQLAlchemy's `__tablename__`, which is why py-accesses-data reads 1.00 and Django reads nothing.
entry_points: parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs:913-936 — `scan_model_tables`: the SQLAlchemy pre-pass that records `class_name -> entity id`; the Django branch extends it
parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs:938-965 — `find_tablename`, which reads `__tablename__` and returns None for a Django model
parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs:966+ — the edge-emit path that anchors ACCESSES_DATA on the enclosing accessor
parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs:180 — the `Acc.model_tables` field doc
parsers/code/extractors/src/data_entities.rs:313-333 — `scan_orm_table_decls`, the explicit `db_table` path (left unchanged)
packets.implementation:
Extend `scan_model_tables` (python:913): when `find_tablename` returns None, check the class's base list for a Django model base — an `attribute` whose tail is `Model` with a `models`/`django` head (`models.Model`, `django.db.models.Model`) — and when it matches derive the table. Precedence: (1) `class Meta: db_table = "..."` inside the class body (walk one nested `class_definition` named `Meta` for an assignment to `db_table`); (2) `class Meta: app_label = "shop"` ⇒ `shop_<lowercased model name>`; (3) fall back to the module path's Django app segment — the LAST path segment before `models.py` in the module qname (`shop::models` ⇒ `shop`) ⇒ `shop_<lowercased model>`; (4) if none apply, `<lowercased model>` alone.

Record the result into the existing `acc.model_tables` map so the EXISTING edge-emit path (python:966+) anchors ACCESSES_DATA on the enclosing accessor with no further change — that is what keeps this packet at 80 LOC. Extend the query-site recogniser so Django's `Model.objects.<method>(...)` shape resolves the receiver the same way `session.query(Model)` does today.

Note for the implementing agent: Django's real rule lowercases the model name WITHOUT snake-casing (`class OrderItem` ⇒ `shop_orderitem`, not `shop_order_item`). Match Django, not A13.1's fold — A13.1 canonicalises at index time, so the two still join.

No unwrap; every nested lookup is `let ... else { continue }`.

Tests: `django_model_implicit_table_from_module_app`, `django_meta_db_table_wins`, `django_meta_app_label_used`, `sqlalchemy_tablename_still_wins` (regression on python:938).
packets.acceptance: NEW FIXTURE bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/py-django-orm·ACCESSES_DATA reads 0.00 at HEAD (no `db_table`, so no DATA_ENTITY node exists) and 1.00 after. The pre-existing py-accesses-data cell stays 1.00 — that is the proof the SQLAlchemy path was not disturbed. Unit gate: the four new tests plus the existing `session_query_emits_accesses_data_from_enclosing_function` (python/src/lib.rs:2581). Grep gate: `[orm-django] models=1 implicit=1`.

breaking.what_changes: Additive: Django models gain DATA_ENTITY nodes and accessor-anchored ACCESSES_DATA edges where they had none. SQLAlchemy models (explicit `__tablename__`) take the same path as today and are byte-identical, because the Django branch is only reached when `find_tablename` returns None.

fixtures.name: py-django-orm
fixtures.purpose: The implicit-table convention that covers most real Django models; app-label derivation from the module path is the part no string scanner can do.

packets.risks: `scan_model_tables` is per-file, so models.py and views.py in different files mean the view's `Order` receiver resolves only via the fallback; put both in one file OR accept the fallback key — settle it before recording the 0.00 baseline. The implicit-name derivation is a convention, not a declaration: a project that overrides db_table elsewhere (an abstract base, a third-party app) gets a wrong-but-consistent key, which A13.1's fold will still join to itself but not to the real table. Keep confidence Medium.

packets.title: Kotlin blind-spot caveat rows + "kt" language detection in coverage_report, plus the four failing Kotlin fixtures that record the 0.00 baseline
packets.rationale: Measured today on a pure-Kotlin repo: `g.coverage()` returns exactly two rows, both `language: "*"` (CALLS, HTTP_CALLS), `edges_found: 0`. Nothing tells a consumer that Kotlin has no parser. An agent asking `blast_radius` for a Kotlin symbol gets an empty answer that is indistinguishable from "nothing depends on it" — the substrate is confidently wrong. This is the interim that makes graph+grep fallback deliberate, and it also lands the four fixtures whose 0.00 cells are the falsifiable baseline for every later Kotlin packet (per the house rule that the baseline is recorded BEFORE the fix).

Insert `"kt" => "kotlin",`. VERIFIED: without this, `languages_present` (engine/src/lib.rs:1629) can never contain "kotlin" and a kotlin-scoped caveat row is unreachable.

engine/src/lib.rs:1556 — `static COVERAGE_CAVEATS: &[CoverageCaveat] = &[`, array closes at engine/src/lib.rs:1593 with `];` (last entry is the `language: "dart"` HTTP_CALLS row at :1588). Append the Kotlin rows before the `];`.

engine/src/lib.rs:1612 — `pub fn coverage_report(merged: &MergedGraph) -> Vec<CoverageNote>`; `let langs = languages_present(merged);` is the first line. Emit the fired_on marker here, gated on `langs.contains("kotlin")`.
engine/src/lib.rs:2321 — `mod walk_tests` (the only `#[cfg(test)]` block in engine/src/lib.rs; it already builds tmp repos and calls `generate_one`). Add the unit test here.

engine/src/lib.rs:1132 — `let matches_lang = detect_language(&rel_str).is_some();` in `walk_dir`. Read-only for this packet: it is the proof that `.kt` must STAY routed, because an unrouted extension is never read and so contributes no POSITION cell for `languages_present`.
packets.implementation:
Three surgical edits to engine/src/lib.rs plus four fixture dirs.

(1) `ext_to_language` (engine/src/lib.rs:1653): add `"kt" => "kotlin",` to the match. Do NOT add `"kts"` — `.kts` never reaches `walk_dir`'s read gate (engine/src/lib.rs:1132) so the arm would be dead; name it in the caveat prose instead.

(2) `COVERAGE_CAVEATS` (engine/src/lib.rs:1556-1593): append five `CoverageCaveat` entries before the closing `];`, all `language: "kotlin"`. Do NOT change the `CoverageCaveat` struct (engine/src/lib.rs:1540) — four `&'static str` fields is all this needs, and changing the struct changes the serialized shape of `PyGraph.coverage()` (py/src/lib.rs:259) and the CLI table (cli/src/main.rs:722-728).
  - `edge_category: "*"`, note: "no Kotlin parser: .kt files are parsed with the Java grammar, so only declarations whose header is also valid Java survive (`interface X {`, `open class X {`). Kotlin `fun`, primary constructors, `: Base()` heritage and every call are invisible. `.kts` (Gradle KTS) is not read at all. Treat the Kotlin surface as ungraphed.", verify: "grep the Kotlin symbol directly; an empty blast_radius / impact for a .kt symbol means NOT-EXTRACTED, not dead code".
  - `edge_category: "CALLS"`, note: "zero CALLS are extracted from Kotlin — no function or method node exists to hang one on", verify: "grep the callee name across *.kt".
  - `edge_category: "IMPORTS"`, note: "Kotlin `import a.b.C` resolves only when the target class happened to survive the Java grammar; treat Kotlin import edges as best-effort", verify: "grep '^import' in the .kt file".
  - `edge_category: "INHERITS_FROM"`, note: "Kotlin `: Base()` / `: Iface` delegation specifiers are never extracted — no heritage edge exists for any Kotlin type", verify: "grep the supertype name".
  - `edge_category: "HANDLED_BY"`, note: "Ktor `get(\"/path\") { }` ROUTE nodes ARE emitted by a text scan, but with no handler and no HANDLED_BY edge; Spring `@RestController` / `@GetMapping` on a Kotlin class is usually invisible because the primary constructor breaks the class node", verify: "grep for routing { / @GetMapping in *.kt".

(3) `coverage_report` (engine/src/lib.rs:1612): after `let langs = languages_present(merged);`, add `if langs.contains("kotlin") { eprintln!("[coverage] kotlin: no parser — .kt routed through the java grammar"); }`. One line per call, matching the unconditional `[incremental]` marker style at engine/src/lib.rs:64,394. No unwrap, no panic.

(4) Unit test in `mod walk_tests` (engine/src/lib.rs:2321): `fn kotlin_reports_as_blind_spot()` — write `Sample.kt` with `class Foo {\n    fun bar(): Int = 1\n}` into `unique_tmp("kt")`, call `generate_one(repo)`, then `coverage_report(&result.merged)`; assert at least one note has `language == "kotlin"` and that one of them has `edge_category == "*"`. Use the existing `unique_tmp` helper already in that module.

(5) Fixtures — four dirs, all contents MEASURED today against engine 0.4.18 so the baselines in `acceptance` are real, not predicted. All Kotlin sources must be multi-line (single-line `object X { fun go() {} }` sets has_error in tree-sitter-kotlin-ng). Do NOT name a class the same as its file stem: `grade.py`'s `_node_matches` is a substring test over name OR qname, so a class named `UserService` in `UserService.kt` false-positives against the MODULE qname `UserService` and against any nested qname `UserService::X`. That is why the fixtures use neutral file names (`api.kt`, `svc.kt`, `service.kt`, `web.kt`, `app.kt`, `store.kt`).

(6) BLINDSPOTS.md: add a Kotlin block under "The 9 patterns" recording the measured numbers (4 nodes / 2 edges on kotlin-entities; ROUTE 2/2 on kotlin-ktor; IMPORTS 1/1 on kotlin-spring) and the `.kts` gap.

packets.rationale: Today a Kotlin repo is ungraphed: measured 4 nodes / 2 edges on a 50-line 2-file sample, zero functions, zero methods, zero calls. Without type and function nodes there is nothing for any later mechanism to hang an edge on — no CALLS target, no INJECTS source, no HANDLED_BY handler — so this is the load-bearing packet. NEW CRATE `parsers/code/kotlin/`.

Cargo.toml — copy parsers/code/java/Cargo.toml verbatim, rename to `repo-graph-parser-kotlin`, swap `tree-sitter-java = "0.23"` for `tree-sitter-kotlin-ng = "1.1"`. Keep `tree-sitter = "0.26"`, `repo-graph-core`, `repo-graph-code-domain`, `repo-graph-doc` (path `../docs`), serde, serde_json, thiserror. `publish = false`, `edition = "2024"`, `version = "0.4.9"` (match the other parsers — they are NOT on workspace.package). VERIFIED: I built a scratch crate with exactly `tree-sitter = "0.26"` + `tree-sitter-kotlin-ng = "1.1"`; it resolved tree-sitter 0.26.13 and tree-sitter-language 0.1.7 (already in Cargo.lock) and parsed every probe clean.

src/lib.rs — `pub fn parse_file(source: &str, file_rel_path: &str, module_qname: &str, repo: RepoId) -> Result<FileParse, ParseError>`, byte-identical signature to the java parser (engine/src/lib.rs:820 calls it that way). Language init: `let lang: tree_sitter::Language = tree_sitter_kotlin_ng::LANGUAGE.into();` then `parser.set_language(&lang).map_err(|e| ParseError::LanguageInit(e.to_string()))?`. NEVER bail on `root.has_error()` — measured, real Kotlin sets it (a nested trailing lambda `{ call.respond("x") }` produced an ERROR node while the rest of the file parsed fine); tree-sitter error recovery still yields the surrounding tree.

AST facts, all MEASURED against tree-sitter-kotlin-ng 1.1.0 — do not re-derive:
  * root is `source_file`; named children include `package_header`, `import`, `class_declaration`, `object_declaration`, `function_declaration`, `property_declaration`, `typealias`.
  * `child_by_field_name("name")` WORKS on class_declaration / object_declaration / function_declaration.
  * `child_by_field_name("body")` returns None — THERE IS NO `body` FIELD. Scan named children for `class_body`, `enum_class_body`, `function_body`.
  * There is NO `interface_declaration`. `interface Foo {}` is a `class_declaration` whose children are `[*interface, identifier, class_body]` (`*` = anonymous). Discriminate by walking `node.children(&mut cursor)` and checking `!k.is_named() && k.kind() == "interface"`.
  * `enum class Status { A, B }` is a `class_declaration` with an `enum_class_body` child (entries are `enum_entry`).
  * `object X { }` is `object_declaration`; `companion object { }` is `companion_object` with a nested `class_body`.
  * `data`/`sealed`/`open`/`annotation`/`abstract` all land in a `modifiers` child (`class_modifier` / `inheritance_modifier`), so the base `class_declaration` handling covers them.
  * `import com.a.B` is an `import` node (NOT `import_declaration`) with a `qualified_identifier` child whose named children are the dotted `identifier` segments.
  * `primary_constructor` -> `class_parameters` -> `class_parameter` (each: optional `modifiers`, `identifier`, `user_type`).
  * `delegation_specifiers` -> `delegation_specifier`; a `constructor_invocation` child means SUPERCLASS, a bare `user_type` child means INTERFACE. (Consumed by A14.3.)

What to emit (mirroring parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs structure — an `Acc { nodes, edges, imports, calls, refs, nav, properties }`):
  1. MODULE node for the file, id `NodeId::from_parts(GRAPH_TYPE, repo, node_kind::MODULE, module_qname)`, cells from a `file_cells` clone. `acc.nav.record(...)`.
  2. Type declarations, recursively (nested types included), qname `{parent_qname}::{Name}` — `::` separator, locked. Kind mapping uses ONLY existing locked ids, no new NodeKind: anonymous `interface` keyword -> `node_kind::INTERFACE`; `enum_class_body` child -> `node_kind::ENUM`; `object_declaration` -> `node_kind::CLASS` (a singleton IS a class; this keeps `enclosing_class_or_struct` at graph/src/lib.rs:790 working, which only matches CLASS or STRUCT); everything else -> `node_kind::CLASS`. Each gets `entity_cells` and a DEFINES edge from its parent.
  3. `companion_object` — do NOT emit a node. Recurse into its `class_body` so its members attach to the ENCLOSING class (they are the outer type's statics).
  4. `function_declaration` -> `node_kind::METHOD` when the nearest declaring ancestor is a `class_body` / `enum_class_body`, else `node_kind::FUNCTION` (Kotlin has real top-level functions; this distinction is what makes A14.3's call resolution work). Extension functions (`fun String.slugify()`) have an extra leading `user_type` child before the name `identifier` — take `child_by_field_name("name")`, which is correct in both cases (measured). qname `{parent_qname}::{name}`.
  5. `property_declaration` -> `node_kind::ATTRIBUTE`, gated like parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:403 `visit_field_decl` so it stays quiet: emit only when the modifiers contain `const`, OR `repo_graph_doc::leading_doc` returns Some, OR the initializer is not a plain literal. `val`/`var` with a getter also go into `FileParse.properties` (the HashSet<NodeId> at code-domain/src/lib.rs:642) so downstream path BFS treats `obj.x` as a valid attribute read.
  6. Imports. For each `import` node take the `qualified_identifier` text, split on '.', and emit exactly the java shape (parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs `collect_import`): trailing segment starting uppercase (or an `as` alias) -> `ImportTarget::Symbol { module: prefix.replace('.', "::"), name, alias, level: 0 }`; otherwise `ImportTarget::Module { path: dotted.replace('.', "::"), alias }`. Handle `import a.b.*` (star -> Module) and `import a.b.C as D` (alias). NOTE the resolver matches by qname SUFFIX — kotlin-spring's `import com.example.service.UserService` resolves to `service::UserService` because the file is `service.kt`; that is why it already reads 1.00 and why it must keep doing so.
  7. `pub fn trace(parses: &[(&str, Vec<FileParse>)])` (or a slice of FileParse — pick one and keep it) emits the single greppable marker line. Later packets append their own eprintln INSIDE this function so the engine is never touched again.

src/routes.rs — near-verbatim port of parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:708 `scan_ktor_routes` + :870 `emit_ktor_route`. Port the KTOR scanner ONLY, not `scan_javalin_routes` (:815): Javalin's discriminator is a comma after the path, but idiomatic Kotlin Javalin is `app.get("/x") { }` with a trailing lambda and no comma, so the port would be dead code. Keep emit's Confidence::Medium and the ROUTE_METHOD cell so route NodeIds are byte-identical to today's. Add a `// TODO(A14.5): replaced by the AST scanner` comment.

Unit tests inside src/lib.rs `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (mirroring parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:1224): `classes_objects_and_interfaces` (kind discrimination incl. `interface`-as-class_declaration and `enum_class_body`), `top_level_fun_is_function_member_fun_is_method`, `companion_members_attach_to_outer_class`, `imports_symbol_and_star_and_alias`, `ktor_routes_ported` (the same source as the java test at :1488, asserting GET /users, POST /users, DELETE /users/{id}), `has_error_source_still_yields_declarations`. All sources multi-line.

Also: add a Kotlin section to dev-notes/glia-memory/reference_treesitter_quirks.md with the three measured traps (no interface_declaration; no `body` field; single-line `object X { fun go() {} }` sets has_error while multi-line does not).

Finally, rewrite the five Kotlin rows in COVERAGE_CAVEATS (engine/src/lib.rs:1556-1593) from "no Kotlin parser" to the true post-landing residual: entities and imports extracted; calls, heritage, Spring/Ktor annotations still partial.
