packets.title: Kotlin calls + heritage: CallSite/UnresolvedRef emission and the build_kotlin extra_hook for bare self-calls
packets.rationale: Measured on kotlin-entities: CALLS 0/2, INHERITS_FROM 0/1, IMPLEMENTS 0/1. After A14.2 the nodes exist but nothing connects them, so `blast_radius`, `trace` and PPR activation still see a Kotlin repo as a pile of disconnected declarations. Kotlin additionally needs the `extra_hook` seam (which the review notes has never been used) because it is the only JVM language in the tree with BOTH top-level free functions and unqualified self-method calls — `logIt(saved)` inside a class and `topLevelHelper(2)` at file scope are syntactically identical, and graph/src/lib.rs:802 `push_edge` does not dedupe so emitting both qualifiers would double every edge.
entry_points: graph/src/lib.rs:542 — `fn resolve_calls<H>(g: &mut RepoGraph, calls: &[CallSite], extra_hook: H)`; the doc at :538-541 says the hook is "unused today (pass `|_, _| None`)". Fill it in for Kotlin.

graph/src/lib.rs:554-572 — the `CallQualifier::Bare(name)` arm: bindings -> module_symbols -> enclosing_package symbols. It does NOT consult `class_methods`, which is exactly the gap for a Kotlin bare self-call.
graph/src/lib.rs:592-599 — the `CallQualifier::SelfMethod(name)` arm, which DOES consult `enclosing_class_or_struct` + `class_methods`. This is the fallback the hook replicates.

graph/src/lib.rs:790 — `fn enclosing_class_or_struct`; matches CLASS or STRUCT only. Kotlin `object` is emitted as CLASS by A14.2 so it works; INTERFACE-owned default-implementation methods will NOT resolve — a known, documented residual.
graph/src/lib.rs (build_kotlin, added by A14.2 right after :127 build_dotted) — swap its `|_, _| None` for the Kotlin hook. Engine is NOT touched by this packet.

parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:930 `fn collect_calls_in` and :961 `fn classify_method_invocation` — the template. Java maps a receiver-less call to SelfMethod because Java has no free functions; Kotlin must NOT copy that.

parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:234-257 `fn emit_heritage_ref` — the exact recipe for heritage: strip generics at '<', take the trailing simple name after '.'/':', push `UnresolvedRef { from, from_module, qualifier: CallQualifier::Bare(simple), category }`. Reuse verbatim.
code-domain/src/lib.rs:477-496 — the `CallQualifier` enum (Bare / SelfMethod / SuperMethod / Attribute / ComplexReceiver) and :464 `UnresolvedRef`.
packets.implementation:
PARSER SIDE (parsers/code/kotlin/src/lib.rs).

Add `collect_calls_in(node, src, from, repo, file_rel, acc)` called from the function/method visitor on the `function_body` child (remember: there is no `body` field — find the named child of kind `function_body`). Walk with an explicit stack, exactly like parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:930, but DO descend into `lambda_literal` / `annotated_lambda` (Kotlin's dominant call shape lives inside trailing lambdas — measured: `routing { get("/x") { store.all() } }` nests calls three lambdas deep, and refusing to descend would lose nearly every Ktor/Compose/coroutine call). Do NOT descend into nested `class_declaration`, `object_declaration` or `function_declaration` (those get their own `from`).

Classify each `call_expression` (measured shapes):
  * first named child is `identifier` -> receiver-less. Emit `CallQualifier::Bare(name)`. NOT SelfMethod — Kotlin free functions are real, and the extra_hook below covers the self-method case.
  * first named child is `navigation_expression` whose own first named child is an `identifier` -> `CallQualifier::Attribute { base, name }` where `name` is the navigation_expression's LAST named child. This covers `userService.findById(id)` and also `r?.load("y")` — measured, the safe-call `?.` produces the same `navigation_expression [identifier, identifier]` shape, so no special handling.
  * `this_expression` as the navigation base -> `CallQualifier::SelfMethod(name)`.
  * `super_expression` -> `CallQualifier::SuperMethod(name)` (resolver returns None today at graph/src/lib.rs:606; emit it anyway for future wiring).
  * anything else (chained `Repo.Companion.create()`, `"hello".slugify()`) -> `CallQualifier::ComplexReceiver { receiver, name }`, kept for diagnostics.

Heritage: on each type declaration, find the `delegation_specifiers` named child and iterate its `delegation_specifier` children. MEASURED discriminator — a `delegation_specifier` containing a `constructor_invocation` child is a SUPERCLASS (`class UserService : BaseService()`), and one containing a bare `user_type` child is an INTERFACE (`class UserController(...) : Auditable`). Route the former to `edge_category::INHERITS_FROM` and the latter to `edge_category::IMPLEMENTS`, both through an `emit_heritage_ref` clone of parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:243-257 so the qualifier is `CallQualifier::Bare(simple_name)` and the graph resolver binds it (never fabricate a name-derived NodeId — that is the Dart/TS/Solidity bug the review flags under §3 Structural).

GRAPH SIDE (graph/src/lib.rs, inside `build_kotlin`).
Replace the `|_, _| None` hook with a closure that fires only where the generic pass already failed:

    |g: &RepoGraph, site: &CallSite| match &site.qualifier {
        CallQualifier::Bare(name) => enclosing_class_or_struct(&g.nav, site.from)
            .and_then(|cls| g.symbols.class_methods.get(&cls).and_then(|m| m.get(name).copied())),
        _ => None,
    }

Order matters and is already correct: `resolve_calls` tries the generic Bare chain first (import binding -> module top-level -> enclosing package) and only calls `extra_hook` on miss (graph/src/lib.rs:610), so a genuine top-level `fun` wins over a same-named method, which is Kotlin's real resolution order. Exactly one edge is produced either way, so graph/src/lib.rs:802 `push_edge`'s lack of dedupe is not a problem. Add a doc comment on `build_kotlin` naming this as the first real use of the seam, and update the stale `resolve_calls` doc at graph/src/lib.rs:538-541 which currently says the hook is unused.

Extend `trace()` in the kotlin crate with the second marker line.

Tests: in the kotlin crate — `attribute_call_emits_attribute_qualifier`, `bare_call_in_class_emits_bare` (asserting the qualifier, not the edge), `safe_call_classifies_as_attribute`, `superclass_vs_interface_delegation` (asserting one INHERITS_FROM ref and one IMPLEMENTS ref with the right Bare names, mirroring parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:1298-1324), `calls_inside_trailing_lambda_are_collected`. In graph/src/lib.rs's test module — `kotlin_bare_call_resolves_to_sibling_method_via_hook` and `kotlin_bare_call_prefers_top_level_fun`.

NEW MODULE parsers/code/kotlin/src/spring.rs, called from the type and function visitors in lib.rs.

(1) Routes. `check_route_annotations(node, src, file_rel, handler_id, repo, acc)` — a direct port of parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:625-684. Call it (a) on every type declaration with the CLASS node as handler_id and (b) on every `function_declaration` with the METHOD node as handler_id, mirroring the java call sites at :188 and :226. Because it matches on `text_of(node, src)`, the Kotlin `modifiers` -> `annotation` -> `constructor_invocation` shape (measured: `@GetMapping("/users/{id}")` is `annotation > constructor_invocation > [user_type GetMapping, value_arguments]`) needs no AST work. `emit_route` and `extract_annotation_string` port verbatim so ROUTE NodeIds and the `{METHOD} {path}` name shape are byte-identical to the Java ones — that keeps the HttpStackResolver index consistent across a polyglot JVM repo and keeps Kotlin ROUTEs pairing with existing clients.

(2) Beans. `is_spring_bean(node, src)` — port parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:514 but read the Kotlin `modifiers` child instead of java's `modifiers_text`. Also accept `@RestController` / `@Controller` on `object_declaration`.

(3) INJECTS — the Kotlin-specific part. When a type declaration is a bean, find its `primary_constructor` named child (measured shape: `primary_constructor > class_parameters > class_parameter`, where a class_parameter's children are optional `modifiers` (visibility_modifier private / member_modifier), `identifier`, `user_type`). For each `class_parameter` whose `user_type` is not in the extended `is_non_injectable_type` denylist, push `UnresolvedRef { from: class_id, from_module: module_id, qualifier: CallQualifier::Bare(simple_type_name), category: edge_category::INJECTS }`. Strip generics at '<' and take the trailing segment after '.', same as `emit_heritage_ref`. Also handle `class Repo @Inject constructor(private val api: UserApi)` — measured, the annotated form still yields a `primary_constructor` child, so the same walk covers it; additionally treat a class whose primary constructor carries any of INJECT_ANNOTATIONS as a bean even without a stereotype. Also port field injection: a `property_declaration` carrying `@Autowired` / `@Inject` emits the same ref from the class to the property's `user_type`.
  Emit INJECTS as an UnresolvedRef, never a direct edge — `resolve_refs` binds `Bare(TypeName)` to the real class NodeId, and fabricating a name-derived id is precisely the bug the review flags for TS/Solidity/Dart heritage.

(4) Micronaut/JAX-RS come free with the ported pattern table; no extra work.

packets.implementation:
MEASURED AST shape for the Ktor DSL (tree-sitter-kotlin-ng 1.1.0) — `get("/api/items") { call.respond(...) }` is:

    call_expression
      call_expression
        identifier              <- "get" / "post" / "put" / "patch" / "delete" / "head" / "options" / "route"
        value_arguments
          value_argument
            string_literal
              string_content    <- "/api/items"
      annotated_lambda
        lambda_literal          <- the handler body

and `routing { … }` is a `call_expression(identifier "routing", annotated_lambda)` with no value_arguments.

Replace the text scanner with a walker run from the enclosing function's `function_body`. Recognise a route when ALL of: the outer node is a `call_expression`; its first named child is a `call_expression` whose first named child is an `identifier` matching a verb; that inner call has a `value_arguments` whose first `value_argument` is a `string_literal`; and the outer call has an `annotated_lambda` child. Take the path from the `string_content` child (no manual quote scanning — that is what the text version had to do).

Guards this buys, none of which the text scanner had: a bare `map.get("/key")` is a `navigation_expression`-based call and is structurally excluded, so the `path.starts_with('/')` heuristic is no longer load-bearing — KEEP it anyway as belt-and-braces, because dropping it would change the emitted route set for a file with `get("count") { }`.

HANDLED_BY target. Ktor handlers are anonymous lambdas, so there is no named handler node. Bind the ROUTE to the nearest ENCLOSING DECLARED function — the FUNCTION or METHOD node whose body the route literal sits in (`Application.itemRoutes` in the fixture). Emit `Edge { from: route_id, to: enclosing_fn_id, category: edge_category::HANDLED_BY, confidence: Confidence::Medium }` (Medium, not Strong — the binding is structural, not a declared handler reference). This makes a Ktor route a real `trace` hop instead of a terminus. If there is no enclosing declared function (a top-level `val module = { routing { … } }`), fall back to the MODULE node so the route is never orphaned.

Attach a POSITION cell to the ROUTE node via `repo_graph_doc::position_json(&outer_call_expression, file_rel)` so `locate_node` returns a real file:line for Kotlin routes. This is a strict improvement over the ported scanner's cell-less node and is additive (a cell appears where there was none).

Do NOT concatenate nested `route("/admin") { … }` prefixes. The Java test at parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:1488 asserts the flat form and prefix concatenation would change existing route NAMES (which are the NodeId key) — a separate cross-language packet.

Delete the ported text scanner from routes.rs once the AST version passes the same test. Keep the dedupe `HashSet<String>` keyed on `{METHOD} {path}` so a file declaring the same route twice still emits one node.

Extend `trace()` with the fourth marker line, reporting both the AST count and how many routes the (now removed) text path would have found, so a mismatch is visible during the transition.

Tests: `ktor_ast_routes_match_text_scanner` (the exact source from parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:1489-1503, asserting GET /users, POST /users, DELETE /users/{id}), `ktor_route_handled_by_enclosing_function`, `map_get_string_key_is_not_a_route`, `ktor_route_carries_position_cell`, `route_outside_any_function_falls_back_to_module`.

packets.title: Kotlin/Android needles: Retrofit interface ENDPOINTs and Android component classification
packets.rationale: Measured on kotlin-retrofit: HTTP_CALLS 0.00 with the Go server side already at 1.00 (ROUTE /api/users + HANDLED_BY both present) and INTERFACE UserApi already found — so the gap is isolated precisely to Kotlin ENDPOINT extraction, not the HttpStackResolver. This is the Kotlin instance of the review's Pattern A ("client HTTP-call extraction is TypeScript-ONLY", the highest-value pattern in BLINDSPOTS.md): Retrofit is how essentially every Android app talks to its backend, so without it a Kotlin/Android client is permanently disconnected from its server in any cross-service trace. Retrofit's shape is also unusually tractable — the verb and path are literal annotations on an interface method, no receiver-type inference needed.
entry_points: code-domain/src/lib.rs:711-722 — `pub struct ClientEndpoint { method, path, file, line, col, confidence }`, the shared client-endpoint carrier.

code-domain/src/lib.rs:790-808 — `pub fn push_client_endpoint(repo, ep, from, nodes, edges, nav, seen) -> NodeId`; mints `endpoint:{method}:{path}` under `node_kind::ENDPOINT` and wires the CALLS edge from `from`. This is the ONLY correct way to emit a client endpoint — the HttpStackResolver indexes on exactly this qname.

parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:1009 `fn try_detect_java_endpoint` — the Java precedent (RestTemplate / WebClient), showing how a parser hands a ClientEndpoint to push_client_endpoint from inside a call collector. Retrofit is declarative rather than call-site based, so the Kotlin version hangs off the interface method declaration instead.
parsers/code/kotlin/src/spring.rs (from A14.4) — `extract_annotation_string` is already ported there; reuse it to pull `"/api/users"` out of `@GET("/api/users")`.
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs:996 `const HTTP_VERBS` — the verb list.
bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/xstack-go-http and xstack-ts-go-http — the proven-working cross-stack pattern this fixture mirrors (2 dirs => generate_many => cross-graph resolvers fire).
packets.implementation:
NEW MODULE parsers/code/kotlin/src/android.rs.

(1) Retrofit ENDPOINTs. When visiting a `function_declaration` whose enclosing type is an INTERFACE, read its `modifiers` -> `annotation` children. If an annotation's `user_type` name is one of GET / POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE / HEAD / OPTIONS (Retrofit's `retrofit2.http.*`), take its string argument as the path and build a `ClientEndpoint { method: verb.to_uppercase(), path, file: file_rel.into(), line, col, confidence: Confidence::Strong }` from the annotation node's start position, then call `repo_graph_code_domain::endpoint::push_client_endpoint(repo, &ep, method_node_id, &mut acc.nodes, &mut acc.edges, &mut acc.nav, &mut acc.seen_endpoints)`. The `from` is the METHOD node for the interface function (`listUsers`), which is what makes the eventual cross-repo pairing read `listUsers -> GET /api/users -> ListUsers`.
  Disambiguation from Spring: Spring's server-side `@GET` is JAX-RS and is always paired with `@Path` (handled in A14.4's ported table), whereas Retrofit's `@GET("/x")` carries the path itself and sits on an INTERFACE method with no body. Gate on: enclosing type is INTERFACE, the function has no `function_body`, and the annotation carries a string argument. Also honour `@Headers`/`@Query`/`@Path` parameter annotations only insofar as they must not be mistaken for the route annotation.
  Also handle the base-URL-relative form `@GET("users")` (no leading slash, very common in Retrofit since `baseUrl` supplies the prefix) by normalising to `/users` before building the ClientEndpoint — otherwise the HttpStackResolver can never pair it, which is the same class of bug the review records for ASP.NET routes lacking a leading slash.

(2) Android component classification, kept deliberately small. A class whose `delegation_specifiers` name an Android base (`AppCompatActivity`, `Activity`, `Fragment`, `ViewModel`, `Service`, `BroadcastReceiver`, `ContentProvider`, `Application`) or that carries `@AndroidEntryPoint` / `@HiltViewModel` / `@HiltAndroidApp` is an entrypoint. Emit it as `node_kind::COMPONENT` IN ADDITION TO its CLASS node (a parallel classification, exactly the pattern parsers/code/extractors/src/services.rs uses for SERVICE), with a CONTAINS edge to each of its METHOD children. COMPONENT is already in `is_entrypoint` (engine/src/lib.rs, the P3 liveness helper), so this immediately stops Android screens being flagged dead by blast_radius liveness. Use the existing locked `node_kind::COMPONENT` id — no new NodeKind, no new CellType, so nothing needs an `ALL`-table entry.

(3) Hilt/Dagger DI: `@Inject constructor(...)` is already covered by A14.4's INJECTS walk (a class whose primary constructor carries an INJECT_ANNOTATION is treated as a bean). Add `@HiltViewModel` and `@AndroidEntryPoint` to A14.4's stereotype list rather than duplicating the walk here — one-line change in spring.rs, counted in this packet's LOC.

Extend `trace()` with the fifth marker line.

Tests in android.rs: `retrofit_get_on_interface_emits_endpoint`, `retrofit_relative_path_gets_leading_slash`, `spring_jaxrs_get_with_path_is_not_a_retrofit_endpoint` (negative control — an interface method with `@GET` and `@Path("/x")` must not double-emit), `activity_subclass_is_component`, `hilt_viewmodel_is_component_and_bean`, `interface_method_with_body_is_not_an_endpoint`.

The Go side must stay untouched: ROUTE `/api/users` and HANDLED_BY `/api/users -> ListUsers` both still present in `grade.py --dump`. `cargo test --workspace` gains 6 tests. Marker: `cargo run -p repo-graph-cli -- analyze bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/kotlin-retrofit/client 2>&1 | grep '\[kotlin/retrofit\]'` prints `endpoints=2 components=0`. Cross-stack proof in one call: `cargo run -p repo-graph-cli -- trace bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/kotlin-retrofit/client UserApi --with bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/kotlin-retrofit/server` returns a hop labelled mechanism=http with cross_service=true.

That changes `trace` and `blast_radius` answers for those repos — by design, it is the whole point — but it is an answer change, not a pure addition, because a trace that previously terminated at the Kotlin client now continues into the server. New COMPONENT nodes also change `is_entrypoint` results, flipping Android classes (and everything reachable from them) from `live: false` to `live: true` in blast_radius liveness. No existing node or edge is removed; no qname shape, signature or cell value of an existing node changes. packets.title: key.json schema v2 — `cells`, `expect_literals`, `forbid` (additive, in grade.py)

packets.implementation:
Three optional top-level key.json fields, all absent from all 71 existing fixtures, all ignored by run.py.

(1) `cells`: a list of `"<language>/<mechanism>"` strings declaring which matrix cells this fixture speaks to, e.g. `["typescript/http_client", "go/http_server"]`. Absent => the fixture is legacy-only and contributes to no matrix cell (never silently mis-attributed). Any entry in `expect_nodes` / `expect_edges` / `expect_literals` may carry its own `"cell": "<lang>/<mech>"` (string or list) to scope that one assertion; an entry with no `cell` applies to every cell in the top-level `cells` list. This is what lets `fixtures/xstack-ts-go-http` score typescript/http_client and go/http_server independently. Do NOT validate the language/mechanism strings here — grade.py must stay importable without matrix_vocab.py; matrix.py (A15.3) validates them.

(2) `expect_literals`: list of `{"kind": "QUEUE_PRODUCER", "literal": "orders", "where": ["name","qname"], "cell": "...", "note": "..."}`. `where` defaults to `["name","qname"]`; permitted tokens are `"name"`, `"qname"`, `"cell:<CELL_TYPE_NAME>"` and `"cell:*"`. Grading: find every node whose `kind` id equals `_KIND_BY_NAME[kind]`; for each, test the requested locations — `name`/`qname` reuse `_norm` for case-folding and `::`/`.`→`/` normalisation exactly as `_node_matches` does; `cell:X` calls `g.node_cells(n['id'])`, keeps pairs whose cell-type id is `_CELL_BY_NAME['X']`, and does a case-folded raw substring test on the payload (NOT `_norm` — payloads are JSON such as `{"method":"GET","path":"/users",...}` and `_norm` would mangle the slashes and dots). Found iff any node of that kind matches in any requested location. Unknown kind name or unknown cell-type name => `raise ValueError(f"{fixture}: unknown cell type {name!r} — add it to code-domain cell_type::ALL")`, mirroring the existing kind/category validation at grade.py:91/:100.

(3) `forbid`: list of anti-assertions, each either `{"kind": "GRAPHQL_OPERATION", "name": "client.subscribe"}` (a node that must not exist; `name` optional, omit it to forbid the kind entirely), or `{"from": "...", "to": "...", "category": "..."}` (an edge pairing that must not exist), or `{"kind": "ROUTE", "name": "{id}", "max_cells_of_type": {"ROUTE_METHOD": 1}}` (duplicate-emission guard — counts matching cells on the matched node). Reuse `_node_matches` for identity. Each entry graded to `{**entry, "violated": bool, "detail": "..."}`.

`grade_fixture` gains exactly three new keys and changes none: `"literal_recall": [...]`, `"forbidden": [...]`, `"cells": [...]`. Add a `"schema": 2` key only when any v2 field is present, so legacy records stay byte-identical in shape.

Marker, printed to stderr from `_print_verbose` (i.e. only on direct `python3 grade.py <fixture>` invocation, never on import, so run.py output is untouched):
`[matrix] schema v2 <fixture>: cells=<n> literals=<found>/<expected> forbid=<violations>/<checked>`

test_grade_schema.py: zero-dependency, runnable as `python3 test_grade_schema.py`, prints `PASS`/`FAIL` per assertion and `sys.exit(1)` on any failure (bench has no pytest/conftest; bench/doc-link/check.sh is the house precedent). It grades real repo fixtures rather than synthetic graphs, so it also pins engine behaviour: (a) `fixtures/py-http` + a literal `{"kind":"ENDPOINT","literal":"/users","where":["cell:ENDPOINT_HIT"]}` is FOUND (verified: the node's ENDPOINT_HIT payload is `{"method":"POST","path":"/users","file":"client.py","line":…}`); (b) the same literal with `where:["name"]` is also found; (c) `{"kind":"ROUTE","literal":"GET","where":["cell:ROUTE_METHOD"]}` on py-http is found; (d) an unknown cell-type name raises ValueError whose message contains `cell_type::ALL`; (e) `forbid` a nonexistent GRAPHQL_OPERATION on fixtures/py-calls => 0 violations; (f) `forbid` `{"kind":"ROUTE","name":"{id}","max_cells_of_type":{"ROUTE_METHOD":1}}` on fixtures/csharp-aspnet => 1 violation (verified: that node carries ROUTE_METHOD twice); (g) `grade_fixture('fixtures/py-calls')` returns a dict whose `per_category`, `node_recall`, `edge_recall`, `node_by_kind`, `framework`, `language`, `node_count`, `edge_count` keys are all present and whose `per_category` equals the pre-change value; (h) a key.json with `cells` but no v2 assertions grades without error.

No unwrap/panic equivalents: every dict access uses `.get` with an explicit raise carrying the fixture name.

packets.title: The harness — matrix.py: discovery, tri-level derivation, aggregation, stdout matrix
packets.rationale: This is the eval gate for the entire programme. The review's §3 table is a hand-made snapshot that goes stale the moment any fix lands (it is already stale: README.md:52-60's three 'confirmed blind spots' all read 1.00 today). Deriving the cell from three graded assertions turns `full/partial/none` from a claim into a measurement, and — decisively — distinguishes `none` (measured: a fixture exists and nothing of the right kind was emitted) from `unknown` (no fixture, no claim). Every fixture-corpus packet downstream is worthless without this.
entry_points: bench/substrate-gap/run.py:29-30 `discover()` — READ-ONLY, and the reason matrix fixtures live in a separate tree: it globs `fixtures/*/key.json` unconditionally, and run.py:78-80 prints `BLIND SPOTS (recall 0.00): 0` as a committed invariant that ~95 deliberately-failing baseline fixtures would destroy.

packets.implementation:
Discovery: `sorted(glob('fixtures/*/key.json')) + sorted(glob('matrix/*/*/key.json'))`. A fixture participates iff its key.json has a non-empty `cells` list; everything else is counted as `legacy_only` and reported in the footer. `matrix/<language>/<mechanism>/` is the canonical layout and the directory names are cross-checked against each fixture's declared `cells` — a mismatch is a hard error naming both, so a copy-pasted fixture cannot silently score the wrong cell.

Per (fixture, cell) the four graded assertions, all computed from one `grade_fixture()` call:
  extract = for every `expect_nodes` entry scoped to this cell, a node of that KIND exists anywhere in the graph. Kind-only, no identity — this is the level `_node_matches` cannot express. (Implementation note: `grade_fixture`'s `node_recall` rows carry the kind name, so matrix.py recomputes kind-presence from `node_by_kind`-style data; to avoid re-deriving, A15.1's `node_recall` rows should also carry `"kind_present": bool`. Add that field in A15.1 if it is not already there — it is one line and keeps matrix.py from re-walking nodes.)
  literal = every `expect_literals` entry scoped to this cell is found. FALLBACK when the cell has no `expect_literals`: every `expect_nodes` entry scoped to this cell is `found` under today's `_node_matches` — i.e. exactly today's node_recall. This is what makes the 71 legacy fixtures gradeable at level 2 with no source edits (A15.6 only adds `cells`).
  route = `expect_edges` scoped to this cell is NON-EMPTY and every entry is `found`. Empty => route is not-applicable; the cell caps at `partial` and records `reason: "no routing expected"`.
  forbid = zero violations among `forbid` entries scoped to this cell.

Level:
  `none`    iff not extract  (nothing of the right kind emitted at all)
  `full`    iff extract and literal and route and forbid
  `partial` otherwise
  `error`   if grade_fixture raised (record the exception type+message; do NOT swallow it the way run.py:41 does — an unbuildable matrix fixture is a real failure)
The `forbid` clause is what caps a phantom-emitting cell at `partial`, giving the review's precision fixes their first eval gate; the review's matrix is recall-only and could not express it.

`via`: the label from `via_labels` at the index of the first `kinds` group with any node present. Recorded on the cell so `python/mqtt = full via=eventbus` reads honestly rather than pretending the queue path works.

Aggregation when several fixtures claim one cell: MIN level (none < partial < full; `error` dominates everything). Rationale in the docstring: the matrix is a blind-spot map, so a cell is only `full` when every fixture for it is full. The contributing fixture paths are recorded on the cell so a drag is always traceable to one fixture. Cells with no fixture: `unknown`, excluded from the full/partial/none denominators and reported separately.

CLI: `python3 matrix.py` (render + marker), `--json` (machine dump to stdout), `--cell <lang>/<mech>` (single-cell detail, the fired_on marker for every corpus packet), `--language <l>`, `--mechanism <m>`, `--fail-on-error`.

Stdout render: 16 rows × 30 cols using `●` full, `◐` partial, `·` none, `?` unknown, `!` error — the exact glyph set of review §3 plus the two new states — followed by per-mechanism and per-language rollups in the review's `● F ◐ P · N ? U` form (all four counts always printed, so the denominator is never hidden) and a `COVERAGE OF THE COVERAGE: N/480 cells have a fixture (P%)` line. That last line is the honest headline the hand-made table could never carry.

Markers (stderr):
  `[matrix] {L} languages x {M} mechanisms, {F} full, {P} partial, {N} none, {U} unknown`
  `[matrix] cell {lang}/{mech} = {level} (extract={a}/{A} literal={b}/{B} route={c}/{C} forbid={d}/{D}) via={via} fixtures={comma-separated paths}`

packets.implementation:
`matrix_emit.py` exposes `write_results(matrix, path)` and `write_markdown(matrix, path)`; `matrix.py` grows `--emit` and `--check`.

DETERMINISM IS THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT. `results-latest.json` contains NO wall-clock timestamp — re-running with no behaviour change must produce a byte-identical file, so `git diff` is the signal and a noisy diff means something really moved. Written with `json.dumps(obj, indent=2, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"`. Shape:

packets.title: Fixture template, scaffolder and AUTHORING.md — make per-cell authoring near-mechanical
packets.rationale: 16 × 30 = 480 cells is far beyond hand-authoring, and the six corpus packets that follow depend entirely on per-fixture cost being low and uniform. Every fixture needs four decisions that the vocabulary already knows: how many dirs (cross-repo mechanisms need two so resolvers fire — engine/src/lib.rs:96 runs resolvers for a single dir too, but only emits within one repo, which is why all 15 legacy cross-stack fixtures use `["client","server"]`), which node kinds to expect, which edge category is the routing proof, and what the identifying literal is. A scaffolder that reads matrix_vocab.py and stamps a correct key.json skeleton turns each cell from a design task into a fill-in-the-source task, and stops six parallel agents inventing six different conventions.
entry_points: bench/substrate-gap/matrix_vocab.py — `cross_repo`, `kinds`, `categories`, `literal` drive every field of the generated key.json.
bench/substrate-gap/README.md:25-50 — the canonical key.json prose; AUTHORING.md complements it rather than duplicating it.
bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/xcut-queue-queue_flows/key.json — the reference two-dir cross-stack shape (client/consumer.go + server/publisher.go + a QUEUE_FLOWS expectation).
bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/py-tests/key.json — the reference single-dir structural shape (two files, one TESTS edge).

bench/substrate-gap/grade.py:143 `_dump` — `python3 grade.py <dir> --dump` is the authoring loop: write source, dump reality, write the key against it. AUTHORING.md must make this the explicit first step, exactly as README.md:22 already recommends.
packets.implementation:
`python3 scaffold.py <language> <mechanism> [--force]` creates `matrix/<language>/<mechanism>/`:
  - `key.json` prefilled from the vocabulary: `framework` = `"<language>-<mechanism>"`, `language` = the language, `dirs` = `["client","server"]` when `cross_repo` else `["."]`, `cells` = `["<language>/<mechanism>"]`, one `expect_nodes` entry per kind in the FIRST `kinds` group, one `expect_literals` entry per kind with `"literal": "TODO"` and the vocabulary's literal description in `note`, one `expect_edges` entry using the first `categories` value with `TODO` endpoints, and an empty `forbid` list with a comment note.
  - source stubs at the right paths with a banner comment: `// FIXTURE: <lang>/<mech>. Smallest real-library usage that a real repo would contain. Replace TODOs, then: python3 grade.py matrix/<lang>/<mech> --dump`.
  - refuses to overwrite an existing dir without `--force`.

`AUTHORING.md` — the per-cell recipe, six steps, each concrete:
  1. `python3 scaffold.py <lang> <mech>`.
  2. Write the SMALLEST source that a real repo would contain, using the real library's canonical import/needle. Two hard rules learned from measurement: (a) include the real import line, because it is load-bearing — `from kafka import KafkaConsumer` is what makes `extract_topic_near` (queues.rs:196) find the import instead of the call and collapse the node to `queue_consumer:kafka`, and a fixture that omits it would measure a rosier world than production; (b) use the library's canonical casing — `using Confluent.Kafka;` is what makes the case-sensitive gate at queues.rs:120 fail, and lowercasing it to make the fixture 'pass' would falsify the cell.
  3. `python3 grade.py matrix/<lang>/<mech> --dump` and read reality.
  4. Write the key AGAINST THE INTENDED graph, not the observed one. A baseline fixture is supposed to fail; the review's hazard note ('record every new fixture's 0.00 baseline before fixing') is the whole point.
  5. Fill `expect_literals` from the vocabulary's literal description. Note the measured gotcha: ROUTE identity shape differs per language (flask `GET /users`, Go/chi `route:/users`, ASP.NET `ANY api/users`), so assert the PATH against name|qname and the METHOD separately against `cell:ROUTE_METHOD`.
  6. Add `forbid` entries for any phantom the fixture provokes. Worked example to include verbatim, because it is real: a paho-mqtt fixture containing `client.subscribe("sensors/temp")` mints a phantom `GRAPHQL_OPERATION 'client.subscribe'` from the ungated needle at graphql.rs:16, so the mqtt fixture carries `{"kind":"GRAPHQL_OPERATION","name":"client.subscribe"}` in `forbid` and the cell is correctly capped at partial.
  Plus: a size budget (<= 2 files per dir, <= 20 lines per file), the naming convention, and the rule that one fixture serves one cell unless it is genuinely cross-language (then it declares both cells with per-assertion `cell` tags, as fixtures/xstack-ts-go-http will after A15.6).

`matrix/README.md` — one screen: what this tree is, why it is separate from `fixtures/` (run.py:29-30 globs `fixtures/*` and its `BLIND SPOTS: 0` is a committed invariant that deliberately-failing fixtures must not break), and a pointer to AUTHORING.md.
packets.acceptance: `python3 scaffold.py python kafka --force` creates `matrix/python/kafka/{key.json,client/,server/}` with `dirs == ["client","server"]` (cross_repo), `cells == ["python/kafka"]`, and expect_nodes for QUEUE_PRODUCER + QUEUE_CONSUMER. `python3 scaffold.py python calls --force` creates a single-dir skeleton with `dirs == ["."]`. `python3 grade.py matrix/python/kafka` runs without raising on the freshly-scaffolded (TODO-filled) key. `python3 matrix.py --cell python/kafka` reports the cell as no longer `unknown`. Re-running scaffold without `--force` exits non-zero without touching the dir.

breaking.what_changes: New files only.

packets.risks: The scaffolder writes files, so it must refuse to overwrite by default — an accidental `scaffold.py` over a finished fixture would silently destroy an authored baseline. AUTHORING.md's two hard rules (real import line, real casing) are the difference between a corpus that measures production and one that measures a flattering toy; if they are not stated explicitly, six parallel agents will each quietly sand off the friction that makes the cell honest.

New `doc-sources/src/markdown.rs`. Pure, zero new dependencies (line scanner, no pulldown-cmark), and it is the entire unit-tested core; the transport stays untouched. ```rust #[derive(Default, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct StorageStats { pub headings: usize, pub code_blocks: usize, pub links: usize, pub inline_code: usize } pub fn markdown_to_storage(md: &str) -> String; // delegates pub fn markdown_to_storage_with_stats(md: &str) -> (String, StorageStats); ``` Block scanner over `md.lines()` with three bits of state (`fence: Option`, `para: Vec<&str>`, `list: Option`): - ```` ``` ```` toggles the fence. On close emit `` + (`L` only when the info string is non-empty) + ``. Body is verbatim EXCEPT every `]]>` is rewritten to `]]]]>` (the standard CDATA split) — otherwise a fenced block containing `]]>` produces an unparseable page. - `#{1,6} ` (outside a fence) → flush the paragraph, emit `{inline(rest)}`; bump `headings`. - `- `/`* `/`+ ` → `
  • …
`; `\d+. ` → `
  1. …
`. Consecutive items of the same kind group into ONE list element; a blank line or a different block closes it. - Blank line → flush `para` as `

{inline(joined_with_space)}

packets.rationale: TWO independent one-line-class defects in the same file.
